tom_tat: The manuscript of this book had just been written. Several Venerable Venerables asked to borrow it and took turns reading it, then they refused
noi_dung:
Foreword

As soon as the manuscript of this book was written, several Venerable Venerables asked to borrow it, taking turns to read it, then asked:

- We see that you are promoting Zen school, seemingly intending to discredit Pure Land. For example, in the book Six Doors to Thieu That Cave, there is a sentence: 'Reciting the Buddha chanting sutras is all delusion'. And here it says: 'The Pure Land discipline is opportune, including the three senses, and also masters meditation, teachings, rules, and secrets'. It seems like there is an intention for Pure Land to be the winner, how did that happen?

Answer: Is that not so? Each subject has its own syllabus. The preachers depend on their legislative position, and all means of preaching all follow those principles. As the meditation side takes: 'Point directly to one's heart, see one's nature and become Buddha' make cardboard. Pure Land subjects take: 'One life of rebirth, irreversible' make cardboard. Hoa Nghiem party took: 'Leaving the world and entering the Dharma world' make cardboard. Tiantai Buddhism takes: 'Open, reveal, and enlighten Buddha's knowledge' make cardboard. The Tam Luan side takes: 'Leave the two sides, enter the middle path' make cardboard. Phap Tuong Mon takes: 'Reflecting all dharmas on True Consciousness' make cardboard. Tantrism takes: 'The three secrets are compatible, that is, the body becomes a Buddha' make cardboard. And the Law takes: 'The photographer's body and mind entered Thi La Tanh' make cardboard.

Therefore, what is said about meditation above is not to refute Pure Land, or to refute the Buddha chanting sutras, but rather to destroy the practitioner's view of Buddha and the Dharma. If reciting Buddha and chanting sutras are inferior and wrong, why from Venerable Thich to Bodhisattva and Patriarchs all praise and advise chanting sutras to recite Buddha? You should know that meditation master Vinh Minh, who is said to be the reincarnation of Amitabha Buddha, recites a set of Dharma flowers every day. Furthermore, Master Pho Am also attained enlightenment by chanting the Avatamsaka sutras. The teachings in Pure Land are the same, not to refute the Zen school, but only to express the essential characteristics of the sect, so that scholars can consider and learn more deeply, but can choose the interesting path to enter as they please.

Again, although each discipline has different teachings, they are all a common means of leading to Buddha Nature. It's like a big city with eight entrances, but all roads focus on that city. The sects are roughly divided into two, the Empty sect and the Right sect. The empty door enters from the means of reason. The door of existence enters from the means of appearance. But when we get to the end, we integrate everything, the truth is the reason, the reason is the thing, the nature is the form, the form is the nature, in other words: 'Form is emptiness, emptiness is form, emptiness and form are no different. So once upon a time there was a great master who practiced meditation and attained enlightenment, but secretly practiced in the Pure Land. At his deathbed, he left a verse of blessing for the assembly, then recited the Buddha's coming rebirth. A meditator suddenly spoke up and asked: 'Ultimate Bliss is a conditioned realm, why do you pray for it?' The great master shouted: 'Do you say that there is nothing outside of existence?' After hearing this, the Zen monk suddenly became enlightened. So meditation and meditation have the same goal. Although the Right Gate and the Empty Gate seem to be mutually destructive, they actually complement each other.

Coming as said: 'Pure Land is opportune, includes the three senses, and is also proficient in meditation, Doctrine, Vinaya, and Tantra', is the teaching of the ancients such as: 'Lien Tri, Triet Ngo, Random Ich, Kien Mat. These great masters were dragon statues at one time. After participating in meditation and enlightenment, they clarified the principles of Pure Land dharma. As Master Triet Ngo, in Ngu Luc, said: 'A sentence of Amitabha, the heart essence of my Buddha. vertical meditation throughout the five times, horizontal including eight teachings'. And great master Kien Mat, after observing the opportunity, in the Three Great Essentials, also said: 'In this life, meditation should not be combined with the Pure Land. In case the person who has not yet attained enlightenment becomes regressed, shouldn't he be scared and cold?' One sentence, Amitabha, if one is not of superior capacity, great thoroughness, great enlightenment, cannot be fully initiated. But with this sentence, even the most foolish person will not lack anything!' Therefore, medicine is not precious and convenient, healing is good medicine; The dharma is not low or high, it is a wonderful dharma in harmony. Pure Land and Zen school are actually neither superior nor inferior. But when it comes to fundamentals, the Zen school only has superior abilities that can benefit; As for the Pure Land discipline, it includes all three senses, and if you practice it, you will easily get results. Talking about the weather, in this time of the end of the dharma, there are many middle-class people, many people with lower abilities, and very few people with high abilities. If you want to definitely achieve liberation, you must pay attention to Pure Land dharma. This is due to the great compassion of the Buddha and the Patriarchs, because they clearly saw the opportunity and wanted sentient beings to soon escape the suffering of samsara, so in the sutras they have repeatedly reminded. This is a very important and very true fact!

However, as the scriptures say: Living beings' interests and desires have thousands of differences, so all Buddhas must open countless dharma doors to be able to capture them all. Therefore, although Pure Land is opportune, it is only partially adapted and cannot suit everyone's interests, so it is necessary to have Zen school and other subjects, so that all sentient beings can benefit, and Buddha Dharma can be fully and widely spread. So even though I chose Pure Land as a subject depending on my background and interests, I still hope that Zen school and other subjects will spread widely in this country. And other subjects, if they bring sentient beings even a small point of benefit, the writer will wholeheartedly rejoice. In short, the Right Gate and the Emptiness Gate in general, Zen school and Pure Land in particular, walk together towards the true nature, though two but one, they both depend on each other to manifest their achievements, and are also very necessary to be present in Vietnam, even in the whole world.

After listening, several venerable monks all expressed their agreement. By the way, the writer narrates the poem of Tay Trai elder Nhon to conclude, and proves that the ancients also shared that view:

That is, the mind is the salvation of reason, no exaggeration

Purity is no different from meditation, it's still the same house

The colors appear solemnly in the wonderful land

Unobstructed and unobstructed in the eternal world

The Western sky is bright and beautiful, the color of pearls

May Buddha bless you with vast oceans of virtue

Looking back on the path of practice, who woke up early?

The pain of evil always comes in and out!

Like meditation, careful mind

-ooOoo-

tom_tat: This volume is divided into different Chapters, Sections, Sections, Sections, each Chapter has many Sections, each Section has many Sections, and each Section has many Sections.
noi_dung:
Second and Essential Chapters

This book is divided into Chapters, Sections, Sections, and Sections, each Chapter has many Sections, each Section has many Sections, and each Section has many Sections.

Regarding the Chapters, there are only ten, with Roman ordinal numbers (I-II-III) from the First Essential to the Tenth Essential.

Regarding the Section, write the sequential number A-B-C.

Regarding the Section, write the number 1-2-3, but continue to meditate from the beginning to the end of the book, forming from number 1 to number 72. Although it is arranged into Chapters, Sections, Sections, and Paragraphs, Sections are the unit and core component of the entire volume. And this book is a combination or component of 72 combined sections.

Regarding the Paragraph, the word Paragraph is not mentioned, because it only has the nature of attracting attention or distinction in each section, so the fake pen marks it with a star (*), sometimes also writes the sequential number 1-2-3. But this is only a singular number, there is no way to make it plural like Tiet's order. And that's the difference.

The Ten Essentials of Buddha Recitation, according to the title, are the ten essential things of the Buddha Recitation discipline or of those who practice the Buddha Recitation method. These ten articles will be divided into ten chapters as mentioned above.

Those ten chapters are as follows:

1. Reciting Buddha's name is to escape birth and death.

2. To recite Buddha's name, one must develop the heart of Bodhi.

3. Reciting the Buddha's name must eliminate doubts.

4. Chanting the Buddha's name must decide to vow rebirth.

5. Reciting the Buddha's name must be practiced sincerely.

6. Reciting Buddha must eliminate afflictions.

7. Reciting the Buddha's name must diligently seek realization.

8. Reciting Buddha must last a long time without interruption.

9. Reciting the Buddha's name must be patient with all obstacles.

10. Reciting Buddha's name must be prepared for the moment of death.

-ooOoo-

tom_tat: The ancients said: "Revealing poetry in literature and youth." This is what it means: Writing a book should wait until you are old, because the older you are, the more knowledge and experience you have, so the value of the book can be fulfilled. Fake pens are not old enough...
noi_dung:
The Last Word

The ancients said: "Revealing poetry in literature and youth." This is what it means: Writing a book should wait until you are old, because the older you are, the more knowledge and experience you have, so the value of the book can be fulfilled. Authors are not yet in their old age, so their experience and understanding are bound to have many shortcomings, but because of the urgent need to benefit others, and not knowing when impermanence will come, so I try my best to use my ignorance as an offering to fake knowledge. Although this is said to be an original work, most of it draws from the Buddha's sutras and the opinions of ancient monks and wise men. So I think it can also bring some benefit to readers.

In the past, Master So Thach had two verses:

The birth of a thousand years of life is seven weeks of hy.

Returning from the past to the end of enlightenment!

These words were uttered while He was in his seventies, lamenting: Although a human life is said to be a hundred years, it is very rare to live to be seventy years old, and at the age of seventy like Him, when looking at the past, he sees that he has all made mistakes. If a high-ranking monk still criticizes himself like that, then how much are the mistakes of ordinary people? Therefore, when writers think that their sins are still full, and they have not yet finished saving themselves, they venture to talk about advising others, sometimes they feel ashamed and hesitant and do not want to write. But thinking back to the word encouragement, I actually don't dare to accept it, but using the personality of a person in a sea of suffering, I try to call on my friends to overcome the sea of suffering, hoping that thanks to that influence, I can reduce some of my sins, so I don't hesitate.

Recalling the Ming Dynasty in China, Mr. La Dien wrote the exam "Sobriety" as follows:

Pray hastily and painfully,

Rain, rain, sunshine, spring and autumn.

Every day, early in the morning, I worry about my livelihood,

Forgetting and forgetting to see the white head.

Thirst, philandering and philandering do not end,

Sorrows, afflictions, sorrows and sorrows.

There is a clearly clear path,

Tens of thousands of thousands refuse to practice!

The above text, although rudimentary, does not seem to have any profound principles, but it describes all actions and karma obstacles in human life very clearly. Anyone who can avoid the framework of the above test and try to practice is called a person on the path of liberation.

Mr. La Dien's reason for complaining above is because he sees that the sea of profanity is easy to sink and the path of practice is difficult to follow. In the Forty-Twelve Chapters of the Sutra, the Buddha taught:

There are twenty difficult things in human birth:

- Poverty giving is difficult

- Being rich and studying religion is difficult

- Giving up your life and deciding to die is difficult

- Reading the Buddha's Sutras is difficult

- Abstaining from desire is difficult

- Being born into the Buddha's life is difficult

- It is difficult to see what is good and not seek it

- It's difficult to be humiliated and not angry

- It's difficult not to rely on it

- It is difficult to encounter indifferent things

- Studying widely and researching a lot is difficult

- Getting rid of arrogance is difficult

- Not looking down on those who have not learned is difficult

- Equality of mind is difficult

- Not saying that gossiping is difficult

- Meeting good and knowledgeable people is difficult

- See the nature of learning the Dharma is difficult

- Depending on fate, helping people is difficult

- Seeing a scene without movement is difficult

- Knowing how to use the means is difficult.

Of the twenty things above, I would like to briefly mention a few details here. Like poverty, giving is difficult, because poverty even wants to give, but it is difficult to have the heart but lack the strength. If you try to give, it will affect your life, so it becomes difficult. Or like being rich, it is difficult to learn the Dharma, because although wealth has the power to give, it is attracted by sensual pleasures, making it difficult to let go of body and mind to practice. Being born into the Buddha's life is difficult, as the Treatise on Wisdom says: - The city of Savatthi consists of nine billion people, but only three billion people have met and seen the Buddha, three billion people have heard and believed in the name but have not seen it, and three billion people have absolutely neither heard nor seen it. The Buddha lived in this land and taught for twenty-five years, but there are still three billion people who have not seen or heard of him. Those who were born in the Buddha's lifetime but lived far away, or were born before or after the Buddha was born, have the opportunity to meet the Buddha or hear the Buddha's teachings. It is not easy. But even though you don't meet the Buddha, but follow the Buddha's method of practice, it is the same as meeting the Buddha. If you do not follow Buddha's teachings, even if you are close to Buddha, you are still far away. As in the past, Devadatta was Buddha's cousin. Bhikkhu Thien Tinh worked as Buddha's attendant for twenty years. Because he did not follow the correct path, he ended up falling into hell. And the old woman in the east of Xa Ve city was born in the same year, month, day and time as the Buddha, but because she was unlucky, she did not want to see the Buddha. Therefore, to see the Buddha listening to the Dharma and following the teachings, must be a person with many good roots, merits and blessings. Now that Tathagata has entered nirvana, good wise men have replaced Buddha to spread the Dharma. If they closely listen to the advice of practice, they will also be liberated. But it is difficult for people with good roots and weak roots to meet good and knowledgeable people. Even if you have the opportunity to see and hear the Dharma, if you do not understand the meaning, or accept the external form and refuse to believe, it is all in vain. According to the Brahma Vong and Hoa Nghiem Sutras, if you want to seek good knowledge, don't be attached to external forms; For example, do not accept that the person is young, poor, low status, or of low birth, ugly appearance, or inadequate faculties, but only pray that the person understands the Buddha's teachings and can benefit you. Also, with a wise person, you should not look for mistakes, because that person sometimes acts like that because of the secret practice, because of the means of salvation, or even though his moral force is high but his habit energy has not yet ended. If you are attached to formality and look for mistakes, you will certainly not benefit on the path. When Buddha was still alive, Ca Luu Da Di had the habit of chewing his mouth back and forth like a buffalo; Bhikkhunī Lotus Flower Nature likes to look in the mirror and apply makeup; A Bhikkhu likes to climb trees and jump; Another Bhikkhu spoke to someone, saying in a loud voice that he was great. But the truth is that these four have all attained Arhat. Because in a previous life, one was a buffalo, one was a courtesan, one was a monkey, one was a Brahman aristocrat, lived in that situation for many lifetimes, and even though he has attained enlightenment now, the redundant habits still remain. Just like the Sixth Patriarch, because he saw that people studying Buddha at that time preferred to speak according to the sutra text and did not immediately recognize Buddha nature, he appeared as an ignorant and illiterate person. Because Ngoc Lam meditation master wanted to avoid predestined conditions to practice, he pretended to be a crazy person, dressed in messy clothes, and spoke impolitely. Venerable Hu Van, because he saw people in the Dharma Ending Age, most of them were leaving the home life, but the mind was not leaving the home life, so even though he had attained enlightenment, he often grew a beard and hair, secretly indicating "the Way". not where the head is round and the shirt is square. But at their time, there were also many people who criticized the Sixth Patriarch for being ignorant, Ngoc Lam for being crazy, and the Venerable Hu Van for violating the rules of meditation. That's why it's so difficult to look for a wise man. Those who study Buddhism should also understand these things, to reduce stubbornness and avoid the mistake of scorning monks and nuns. As for the other difficult things, you can deduce them to understand.

However, difficulty and ease are opposites, in difficulty there is ease, in ease there is difficulty. If you understand and are determined, difficult tasks are not impossible. Like in the life of Buddha Bhikkhu Thi, there was a poor couple named Ke La Di and his wife who changed to wear the same loincloth. When the husband went to work, the wife had to stay naked and stay at home. The wife took turns going to work and the husband did the same. But when they heard that the Sangha was promoting and saying that Giving would have blessings to avoid poverty, the couple discussed giving that only loincloth through Giving's window, and had to resign themselves to being naked, closing the door, and lying dead in the house. Because of that determination to do good, the king heard about it and brought his clothes and money to help. From then on, in each life they were born, both husband and wife had their own clothes, and eventually they both attained enlightenment. Therefore, although poverty and giving are difficult, if you understand the cause of poverty due to not giving, and then resolve to endure the lack of hardship and use your own to practice blessings, all giving can be done. Like King Thuan Tri of the Qing Dynasty, he ascended the throne at the age of six, but at the age of twenty-four, he renounced the throne and followed the head monk Buddha, leaving the home life. Being an extremely wealthy emperor, living in the Dragon Palace, guarding the phoenix, eating delicious seafood, having thousands of beautiful concubines, and having the power to hold all the subjects in a country, what could be better than wealth? But if you clearly realize that the blessings of worldly happiness, impermanence, are like an illusory dream, and the scene of true and eternal peace, then it is truly joyous. Then, although it is said that learning the Dharma to be rich and wealthy is difficult, if you are determined, you can definitely practice it. In addition, it is still difficult to practice spiritually because of extreme poverty, but if you have the will, it is not impossible. Like when Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha was still alive, there was an old woman who was very poor. She rented a house for someone from the age of thirteen until she was eighty years old, still working hard. She worked without rest during the day. Every night she had to prepare rice until the second watch. The rooster crowed in the morning and gathered around the flour mill. In such a difficult and free time situation, wanting to practice is a difficult task. But thanks to Venerable Ca Chien Dien's encouragement, every evening after she finished eating rice, she showered, changed her clothes, and meditated until past midnight before going to rest. Thanks to that determination and effort, after death she was reborn as a heavenly son in Da Ma heaven.

Dear ladies and gentlemen! The human body is difficult to obtain, Buddha's teachings are difficult to hear. Now that you have received a human body, and have had the opportunity to read this book, that means you have encountered the mysterious method of becoming Buddha. Even though you encounter difficult circumstances, please clearly recognize the fate of this life of suffering and dreams, and be determined to practice, so that the precious lotus in the western sky can bloom with more virtuous lines.

Section A. Pure Land Monasticism, A Dharma That Fits the Opportunity

tieu_de: Lesson 1 - Northern Buddhism with Pure Land of Cause and Effect
tom_tat: * According to tradition in Vietnamese Zen practice, at the beginning of the day's session, monks and nuns of all pagodas recite the Amitabha Sutra, followed by reciting the names of the Western Three Saints (Amitabha, Avalokitesvara, The Chi). And Buddhists leaving the home life or at…
noi_dung:
Lesson 1 - Northern Buddhism with Pure Land of Cause and Effect

• According to custom in Vietnamese Zen practice, at the beginning of the day's session, monks and nuns of all pagodas recite the Amitabha Sutra, followed by reciting the names of the Western Three Saints (Amitabha, Avalokitesvara, The Chi). And every Buddhists leaving the home life or lay, when meeting fellow believers, folds their hands to greet with "Amitabha Buddha."

• The Buddha Recitation method, indeed, has responded to the opportunity, with Buddha's original nostalgia, silently penetrating deep into the subconscious of Vietnamese Buddhists. Not only in this country, but also in China and Korea, wherever Buddhism is prevalent, most Buddhists do not forget to recite Buddha's words. Buddhist followers in Japan also have the following legend: "The Tantric and Thien Thai sects were for the nobles, the Zen school for the samurai, and the Pure Land sect for the common people. But ordinary people are the majority."

Seeing this, we know that in Northern Buddhist lands, the people who claim to recite the name Amitabha Buddha account for the maximum number.

But why does such an event happen?

---o0o---
