noi_dung:
Lesson 2 - Legends about Pure Land

• In the Infinite Life Sutra, Buddha Thich Ton has a mysterious saying: "In the future, when the teachings of the sutra will be completely destroyed, I will use compassion and mercy to preserve this sutra (the Infinite Life Sutra) for about a hundred years. If any sentient being encounters this sutra, they will attain salvation according to their wishes." (In the future, the sutra path will be completely destroyed, the self will be compassionate and attentive, and the sutra will be preserved for many years. If there are sentient beings who meditate on the sutras, depending on their wishes, they will be able to attain salvation. - Infinite Life Sutra.)

• In the Great Collection Sutra, the World-Honored One said: "In the age of the end of the dharma, there are countless people cultivating, very few people have attained enlightenment, only relying on the Buddha's Recitation method to escape samsara." (The end of the dharma and the memories of many people practice, and most of them attain enlightenment. Only by relying on the Buddha's Recitation method, they will attain birth and death. - Great Collection of Sutras).

• Zen master Thien Nhu, after attaining enlightenment, also advised: "After the end of the dharma, all the sutras were destroyed, only the four words Amitabha Buddha remained to save sentient beings. If anyone does not believe, he will surely fall into hell." (After the end of the dharma, all sutras will be destroyed, save only Amitabha Buddha's four words to save sentient beings. Those who do not believe will fall into hell. - Thien Nhu signed language). Because in the Dharma-ending age, when all the sutras are hidden, sentient beings have weak faculties, and besides reciting the Buddha's words, they do not know any other dharma to practice. If you do not believe in Buddha's recitation and practice, you will definitely suffer samsara. And in samsara, good deeds are difficult to do and evil deeds are easy to do, so sooner or later you will fall into hell.

*An Quang Master, a modern monk in China, also said: "At the end of the dharma in this world, sentient beings have heavy karma and mixed minds. If in addition to Buddha's Recitation practice other methods are practiced, in the part of sowing wisdom, merits and blessings of good roots are yes, but in the part of willowing samsara in the present world, it is not. Although there are a few highly virtuous people who perform extraordinary miracles, they are all Bodhisattvas who, according to their original vows, act as models to guide sentient beings to the Dharma Ending Age, as said in the Shurangama Sutra. But those people are only at the level of sentient beings and show enlightenment, not enlightenment. In the Pure Land dharma alone, although few practitioners can attain Buddha Samadhi like in the past, they can rely on their own vows and Amitabha Buddha's original vows to bring about karma rebirth to the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. When you return to that realm, you will no longer have samsara, you will not be regressed, gradually practice until you attain the fruit of No Birth."

• Mysterious words like the above show us that the Buddha's Recitation method is very suitable for the weather conditions and the level of ability of living beings today. That is why the Tathagata used the force of his compassionate vow to abide in the Infinite Life Sutra to encourage the Buddha's Recitation. In addition, the Bodhisattva and Patriarchs also raised their hearts to propagate compassion and, depending on the opportunity, taught the Pure Land method to save sentient beings.

Due to those aspirations, Pure Land is popular among the majority of the public.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Lesson 3 - The Transition From meditation to Purity
tom_tat: * Since ancient times, Truc Chi meditation practice has been very popular in China, Korea and Japan. Our country, Vietnam, is rich in intuition and influenced by Chinese Buddhism, so in the past Zen school was almost in a unique position...
noi_dung:
Lesson 3 - The Transition From meditation to Purity

• Since ancient times, Truc Chi meditation practice has been very popular in China, Korea and Japan. Our country, Vietnam, is rich in intuition and influenced by Chinese Buddhism, so in the past Zen school was almost at the top. Especially in the Ly and Tran dynasties, there were half the world's monks and nuns and most of them practiced meditation. At that time, Buddhism in Vietnam was very strong, many Buddhist monks gathered in large numbers. That's why there is a saying: "In the three-thousand-house monk's room, there are seven-ten monks." This sentence speaks of the prosperity of Buddhism at that time through the meaning "The Sangha room had up to three thousand rooms, every morning it took seventy people to clean it."

But fate also changes with the times. — China from the Song Dynasty onwards, nobles like you: Nhat Nguyen, Thien Nhu, Ngau Ich, Triet Ngo, Lien Tri..., after participating in the Zen school, contemplating the opportunity, out of compassion for the benefit of living beings, tried their best to propagate the Pure Land dharma. The gradual shift from meditation to Purity arose from that moment. At that time, there were many other virtuous meditation practitioners who, although outwardly propagating the Zen sect, secretly practiced Pure Land inwardly to ensure they would not fall into ruin. This can be called the period of parallel meditation. So in a temple, there used to be only a Meditation Hall, but now there is also a Buddha Recitation Hall to provide for the Sangha to practice. Starting from the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties, the power of the Zen school gradually declined, because few people practiced. On the contrary, Buddha's Recitation once again prevailed, and many monks and nuns who practiced Pure Land were reborn. Although Zen school is still in circulation now, in reality it was during the period when Pure Land took over the guidance. Because of that influence, in Vietnam, Buddha Recitation is almost universal. Later, due to the influence of the revival of Buddhism in the country and the propagation of Sangha Ni studying abroad from Japan and other Theravada Buddhist countries, Zen school Vietnam will probably recover. But the truth is that most practitioners only practice teachings such as Zhiquan meditation, or the Four Eighth Dharma meditations, and it is difficult for them to study the original practice of Truc Chi meditation of the sect like in the past.

• Someone said: My nature is definitely not as good as the ancients, it's just that I despise myself so I don't try. - Although self-effort is always encouraging, this statement is actually not true. If the nature is equally diverse, why did Buddha say there are three periods: Right Dharma, Statue of Dharma and End of Dharma? And why do other sutras also talk about the five times of solidity, from Steady Dharma to Steadfast Struggle? Furthermore, the Tripitaka today is much more numerous and complete than in the past, so why are there so few people who practice? Is it because nowadays the fundamentals of the majority of the masses are weak?

Master An Quang said: "Like wearing cotton clothes in summer and cotton clothes in winter; Cultivation is the same, it cannot go against the weather and conditions. Even if Patriarch Bodhisattva Bodhisattva reappears right now, if we want to take the opportunity to save sentient beings and quickly achieve liberation, there is no method better than Buddha's Recitation." Therefore, if the Dharma teaching is not suitable, all sentient beings will be submerged in the sea of suffering. (Preaching the Dharma without success, sentient beings are in a sea of suffering). The sutra advises fellow human beings, even though they practice other disciplines, to take Pure Land as their refuge. If you see that a white apricot is as good as a yellow chrysanthemum, you will also be happy with your pen!

---o0o---

Section B. Pure Land Subject with the Problem of Life and Death

tieu_de: Section 4 - How to recite Buddha's name in accordance with Buddha's original intention?
tom_tat: As mentioned above, in the lands of Northern Buddhism, people chanting the name Amitabha Buddha account for the maximum number. Particularly in Vietnam, among the monks and believers, there are not only many people who practice the Buddha's Recitation method, but also some teachings...
noi_dung:
Section 4 - How to recite Buddha's name in accordance with Buddha's original intention?

As mentioned above, in the lands of Northern Buddhism, people chanting the name Amitabha Buddha account for the maximum number. Particularly in Vietnam, among the monks and believers, there are not only many people who practice the Buddha Recitation method, but also some sects that are not Buddhist, but they also recite the name of the Buddha in the West. However, considering the number of people reciting Buddha's name, although there are many, there are also many people who do not understand the purpose of reciting Buddha's recitation. Therefore, their recitation of Buddha is not in accordance with the Buddha's original intention. Try checking again, we will see:

• There are people who go to the temple and see people reciting Buddha and also imitate the recitation, completely without intention. Although this action also sowed good roots for future merits and blessings, it was not in accordance with Buddha's original intention.

• There are those who recite Buddha's name to pray for disaster to be eliminated, for their families to be healthy and peaceful, and for their daily lives to become more and more prosperous. Praying like that is good, but it is not in accordance with Buddha's original intention.

• There are people who encounter many unsatisfactory situations in their lives and become sad and disheartened. They recite the Buddha's name and pray that they will no longer encounter such situations in their present and future lives, and will be beautiful and glorious, and everything will go as smoothly as they wish. Praying like that is of course still good, but it is not in accordance with Buddha's original intention.

• There are people who feel that life on earth is not interesting, even if they are rich and powerful, they still have many worries and sufferings. They hope to use the merit of reciting Buddha's name so that in their next life they will be reborn in heaven and live a long, leisurely, happy life. Praying like that is also a good thing, but it is not in accordance with Buddha's original intention.

• There are also people who think that they have many sins and that liberation is not easy in this one life. They recite Buddha's name to pray for the next life to change from female to male, leave the home life to practice, and become enlightened monks. Praying like that can be called extraordinary, but it still lacks wisdom and faith, and is not in accordance with Buddha's original intention.

• So how does reciting Buddha match Buddha's original intention?

- The World-Honored One clearly saw that all conditioned dharmas are impermanence, all sentient beings still have all the virtues and wisdom of the Tathagata, but due to the ignorance of the original mind, they create karma, forever subject to life and death in samsara. Even if you are born in heaven, when you enjoy all the blessings, you will still fall. Therefore, the Buddha's original intention is for sentient beings to quickly escape the suffering of samsara through the method of reciting the Buddha's name.

All Buddhas in many eons have cultivated blessings and wisdom. If anyone recites the Tathagata's holy name, they will receive boundless merits. Again, Buddha Amitabha took an oath: If any living being chants His name and prays for Ultimate Bliss, when they die, they will receive rebirth in the West and become irreversibly enthroned. Bringing the immeasurable merit of reciting the Buddha's name and hoping for petty blessings in the human and heavenly realms without praying for rebirth liberation is like a child exchanging priceless mani pearls for candy to eat? That's such a waste and not worth it at all! Furthermore, Buddha's vow power is very great. Anyone with even severe karma who even thinks of Buddha even in this life will be led to rebirth. Seeking to become a highly enlightened monk in the next life is a lack of wisdom and faith. How can we ensure that in this life we will be born in the West and become a Bodhisattva in the irreversible state? Therefore, the Buddha's original intention is for sentient beings to recite the Buddha's name to escape the samsara cycle of birth and death, and that liberation can actually take place in one lifetime.

But why do we need to escape the samsara cycle of life and death?

- That's because in the path of samsara we have indeed endured great suffering. If a person studies Buddha without paying attention to that suffering as it really is, then even if he studies Buddha, he will not get good results, because he does not have the mind of fear and desire to escape. Kinh says: "If the mind is afraid that it will be difficult to arise, it will certainly be difficult to arise." When the World-Honored One once preached the Four Noble Truths to the five people in Mr. Kieu Tran Nhu's group, he first talked about the Truth of Suffering, but this idea was still not lost on him. So let's try to follow the Buddha's teachings of the Noble Truth of Suffering, and observe the suffering of human life. Thus we will have a clearer concept: "Why do we need to quickly escape the samsara cycle of birth and death?"

---o0o---

tom_tat: In the Buddha's explanation of the Truth of Suffering, there are eight things. The suffering of human life is still infinite, but these eight things hold the foundation
noi_dung:
Lesson 5 - Eight Great Sufferings

In the Buddha's explanation of the Truth of Suffering, there are eight things. The suffering of human life is still infinite, but these eight things hold the core.

• The first is Birth Suffering, which refers to the suffering in birth. Humans already have consciousness when they are in the womb. Because there is consciousness, there is emotional movement. When I eat cold food, I feel like I'm in ice; When I eat hot food, I feel like I'm being burned. The fetus lived in a cramped, dark, dirty place. As soon as it was born, it cried loudly. From then on, when cold, hot, hungry, thirsty, bitten by mosquitoes and ants, all I can do is cry. Buddha's wisdom eye clearly saw those details, so he confirmed that it was suffering. If Sanh did not suffer, then when he was born, he would not cry loudly. Therefore, the ancient monk lamented:

As soon as I left the womb, I entered the womb again.

The saints saw how sad they were!

The illusory body is clearly seen as filthy.

Quickly escape and return to your original nature.

• The second thing is Old Man's Suffering, which means suffering in old age. When people get old, their senses are weakened, their eyes are blurred, their ears are deaf, their back is tired, their legs are shaky, their appetite is poor, they don't sleep well, their memory is no longer clear, their skin is dry and wrinkled, and their teeth gradually ache and fall out. Whether you are a handsome young man or a beautiful young woman, when you reach this age:

The magnificence is nowhere to be seen anymore.

A dry body and sad thoughts!

Many people are confused when they are old, their clothes and their clothes are dirty, and their children and grandchildren, even if they are close, are bored. Human life is like the life of flowers, the law of impermanence changes as it brings fragrance, it also brings fading. It turns out that old age is really not fun, human life is really not worth loving! That's why the Buddha said: Old age is suffering!

• The third thing is Sickness and Suffering, which means suffering during illness. Having a body means having illnesses, from mild external illnesses to severe illnesses caused by internal injuries. Some people suffer from serious diseases such as: tuberculosis, leprosy, cancer, palsy. In that situation, you yourself are in pain, you have to spend money or have no money for medicine, you are suffering, and you are causing more suffering to your relatives. That is on top of suffering but adding more suffering! The suffering of illness is obvious, we can easily perceive it.

• The fourth thing is Death Suffering, which means suffering at the moment of death. Everyone wants to have a smooth birth and a peaceful death, but that is very difficult to achieve, and when they die, most of their physical bodies are tormented by illness and pain.

When the body is like that, the mind is terrified, greedy for fields and wealth, sad to leave the body, all worries are overwhelmed, it is truly suffering. Mentioning the word Death, few people want to hear it, let alone like it.

• The fifth thing is Love and Separation Suffering, which is the suffering of separation from a loved one. We see this even more clearly in war situations. So many families suffer from the situation of the North and the South. So many young people have to commit to battle, some stay and miss them, some leave in sadness. That's just the suffering of birth and separation. How many people, still young, have their loved ones snatched away by death, leaving them widowed and helpless? Then there were the parents, brothers, and children who were killed by bullets and bombs. How many other children and relatives are dead, lacking intimacy, living helplessly in orphan villages! This is the suffering of death. So in these times, the sea of longing and the river of love are deep and long, but the mountains of hatred and sky of sorrow are also high and wide! The scene of birth and death separated from loved ones is truly suffering!

• The sixth thing is Oon Tang Assembly of Suffering, which means the suffering of meeting unjust family members. Being slandered, slandered, and plotted to harm by hostile opponents nearby, making us angry, difficult to endure, fearful and restless, is a suffering. There are also many families, parents, siblings or spouses who disagree, often arguing, angry, hateful and sad with each other. That's no different from a meeting in an unjust family, it's not happiness at all!

• The seventh thing is the Unsatisfactory Desire, which is the suffering of unsatisfactory desire. In life, people have many wishes and desires. Roughly like being poor, wanting to be rich, ugly wanting to be beautiful, having children, wanting to have children, having children, wanting to give them, so smart people want to be filial. Thousands of wishes like that, praying but not being satisfied, that is suffering.

• The eighth thing is the Five Skandhas of Thanh Khau, which is the suffering of the five skandhas of enlightenment. Warm years are: form, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness. The physical skandhas belong to the body, the other four skandhas belong to the mind. Simply put: This is suffering of body and mind. This eighth article covers the previous seven sufferings: The body is born, grows old, gets sick, dies, is hungry, thirsty, hot, cold, and tired; The mind is sad, angry, worried, hurt, and hundreds of troubles. Once upon a time, Prince Siddhartha walked around the four gates of the city and saw scenes of old age, illness, and death. He was a deeply wise man and felt compassion for the suffering of human life, so he left the palace to find a way to liberation. On the contrary, wise people are tolerant, think superficially, do not know how to reflect on suffering, so they always take suffering for pleasure. Some people say that Birth is suffering; they said: When I was born I didn't know anything, so I didn't feel suffering! If we say that old age is suffering; they said: I'm not old yet! If we say illness is suffering; they said: Up until now I've always been healthy, rarely get sick, if I get sick it's only trivial, I don't feel any pain! If we say Death is suffering; they said: Death hasn't come yet, maybe it's like a peaceful sleep? If we say that love and separation are suffering; they said: My family is still happily reunited, there is no separation! If we say that encountering resentment is suffering; they said: I haven't done anything to make anyone hate or plot harm? If we say that Bridge cannot be achieved, it is suffering; they said: My life is full as expected, I don't want anything else. - Then that person does not suffer? - They have suffering, that is, the suffering of the five skandhas, or the fullness of body and mind. - If the body and mind are strong and healthy, why suffer? - Let's try to see in this society, cases like: shooting, robbing, raping, fighting. These criminal records are partly due to people being idle, their bodies and minds being too full, they are subject to psychological and physiological stimulation, unable to sit still, unable to do anything, causing cruel things. Like today, from Europe and America to Vietnam, many people live according to the hysteria trend, indulging in strong alcohol, dancing, smoking marijuana or injecting drugs, being lewd, smuggling, liking striptease or exciting music, having fun in all kinds of ways, even liking danger and violence. Their bodies and minds are restless, like a burning fire, causing many mistakes and crimes, leading to suffering. That is the suffering of "The year of blazing warmth."

The above eight things are called the Eight Sufferings. These eight sufferings are only an outline, their content also includes many other sufferings. Let's try to observe ourselves and others, have we suffered more or less in the Eight Sufferings? If a person who studies Buddha knows how to reflect on the eight great sufferings of human beings, it can be said that he has come close to the path.

---o0o---

Section C. Knowing Suffering Must Be Aware of Liberation

tom_tat: * Living beings from one life to another live and die in samsara, down and up in the six realms. These are: the heavenly realm, the human realm, the asura realm, the animal realm, the hungry ghost realm, and the hell realm. Although other species also have more or less suffering,...
noi_dung:
Section 6 - Contemplation on Suffering samsara

• Living beings from one life to the next live and die in samsara, down and up in the six realms. These are: the heavenly realm, the human realm, the asura realm, the animal realm, the hungry ghost realm, and the hell realm. Although other species also have more or less suffering, it is the focus of suffering in the human world. Although heaven is happier than the human world, it still has signs of decline and unsatisfactory things. The Asura world suffers from the suffering of quarrels and competition. The animal world is born like buffaloes, cows, donkeys, and horses, burdened with heavy suffering. Goats, pigs, ducks, and chickens all suffer from the suffering of having their skin cut into pieces. Other species suffer from ignorance; dirty and devour each other. - In the realm of hungry ghosts, sentient beings have foul-smelling and ugly bodies, bellies as big as drums, throats as small as needles, and fire coming out of their mouths, enduring hunger and thirst for thousands of eons. As for hell, there are oil fields, pillars of fire, icy tunnels, mountains of swords, and unspeakable suffering. The four final realms later on are called the Four Evil Beasts in the sutras. From the Asura realm, going down, the suffering in each realm gradually increases. In the six realms, living beings rotate from one place to another, like a wheel turning without a clue. In general, being born in the human world is difficult and rare, falling into the Four Evil Beasts is very easy and many. The ancients lamented:

The six paths rotate without gaps.

Impermanence rushes to the point of letting go!

While still alive, one day the Buddha used his fingernail to scratch some soil, then asked Ananda: "The soil at my fingernails compared to the soil on the mainland, which is more?" Mr. Ananda replied: "World-Honored One! The land of the great land is immeasurably more than the land of your fingernails!" Buddha said: "Same, Ananda! Sentient beings are born into the heavens and humans, like the soil on the fingernails, and fall into evil beasts, like the soil of the great earth!" The above examples are the sounds of tomorrow's bells to awaken the contemplative practitioner.

Many people do not believe in heaven and hell, but those realms do indeed exist. The Buddha's scriptures have clearly shown them, just because the human eye cannot see them. Recently, the daily newspaper has published many paranormal stories, such as the fact that Mr. Hue was taken to the underworld. The Chicken Porridge girl at Vong Nho market in Dinh Tuong also reported on the punishment in the underworld in the book Hell Records. These are probably the Good Gods, seeing that earthly people are sinking in the sea of greed, anger and ignorance, they use their power to send people to hell, so that when they return to the human world, they can tell the people about the path of sin and blessings, so that they can stop evil and do good.

• In short, the three realms are impermanence, and conditioned dharmas have no joy. (The Three Realms stage impermanence. The bliss of non-existence - Lotus Sutra). People who recite Buddha's name must pray to be reborn in the West to escape the samsara cycle of life and death; Gradually practice to attain the normal state, happiness, self, and purity of Nirvana, and do not seek blessings of false pleasures in the world. Reciting the Buddha's name like that is consistent with the goal of liberation, with the World-Honored One's compassionate mind to save suffering and bring joy. And to be like that, the practitioner must constantly contemplate and reflect on the Eight Sufferings of human life until the endless suffering in the six realms. If we don't contemplate like that, it will be difficult for the mind to seek liberation to arise, and the wish to return to the West will not be fulfilled. How can we one day step onto the shore of enlightenment and use the boat of prajna to guide us across the shores of delusion? Once upon a time the Buddha lamented: "In the age of the end of dharma, my disciples only pursue the outside, few of them think about the issue of life and death!" Not wanting to be free from birth and death is because of lack of awareness, because of not really contemplating the suffering of samsara. These people not only failed Buddha, but also betrayed themselves. What a pity and pain!

---o0o---

tieu_de: Lesson 7 - If you want to quickly escape suffering, you should practice Pure Land
tom_tat: Many people who study Buddha, because of their preference for sublime mysteries, consider the Buddha's Recitation to be for the elderly and those with low abilities. But they don't know that Pure Land is a profound door to the depths of Buddha nature, a safe boat to quickly escape...
noi_dung:
Lesson 7 - If you want to quickly escape suffering, you should practice Pure Land

Many people who study Buddha, because of their preference for sublime mysteries, consider the Buddha's Recitation to be for the elderly and those with low abilities. But they don't know that Pure Land is the profound door to the depths of Buddha nature, the most precious boat to quickly escape samsara. Therefore, there are people of superior ability who, because they have not yet realized the Pure Land, are forever stagnant in the path of delusion. And there are people whose nature is only ordinary, but because they practice Pure Land, they soon embark on the path of liberation. Let me tell you a few stories here for scholars to compare.

During the Tang Dynasty in China, at Huong Son Pagoda in Lac Duong there was monk Thich Giam Khong. The monk originally lived as Te, who lived in Wu District.

As a child, he was poor. Although he studied diligently, he had little memory. Growing up, I liked to write poetry, but it was only mediocre. He often traveled to the Ngo and So areas to meet with lords and lords, but did not receive much help. When you have enough money, you will be sick, only when you have enough money will you be cured.

At the beginning of Nguyen Hoa's reign, he wandered around Tien Duong, encountered a poor harvest year, and thought of going to Thien Truc Pagoda to pray for food. But as soon as he reached the west of Co Son Tu, he was too hungry to move forward, so he sat on the bank of a snowy stream, shedding tears and reciting a few words of sorrow and indignation. At first, a Sanskrit monk came along the stream and sat down, looked at him, smiled and asked: "Has the magician tasted enough of the flavors of travel?" He replied: "The taste of traveling can be called full, but where is the person known as Quan Phong, who was once a magician?" Sanskrit monk said: "Don't you remember the time when you preached the Lotus Sutra at Dong Duc Temple?" - Answer: "Since I was born, I have been forty-five years old. I have always been in awe in the Ngo and So regions. I have never been to the capital. How can there be such a thing preaching sutras in the Lac Trung region?" Sanskrit monk said: "You must have been burned by the fire of hunger, so you forgot all about the past!" Having finished speaking, he immediately reached into the bag, took out a large wet apple the size of a fist, gave it to him and said: "This apple is produced in our country, and wise people eat it and know clearly the past and future; Lower level people can also remember past lives." He took the apple, ate it, drank the stream water, felt tired and wanted to sleep, so he leaned his head against the rock and lay down. The moment I woke up, I remembered my past life as a shaman preaching the sutras, with my fellow practitioners, as clearly as yesterday, with tears in my eyes I asked: "Where is Venerable Chan now?" Pham Sang replied: "My diligence was not up to the mark, so I was reborn as a monk in Tay Thuc land. Now I have ended my false fate." Ask again: "How are the gods and the Enlightenment wizards doing now?" - Answer: "God's mercy is not yet finished. As for Master Ngo, standing in front of the stone statue of Huong Son pagoda, making vows jokingly: 'If in this life I don't practice and attain enlightenment, I vow to be a noble god in my next body.' so he is now born as a general. Of the five ancient friends, only I was liberated, the other three were like that, and you are the only one who is still hungry and suffering here! He wept and said: "For more than forty years in my previous life, I only ate one meal a day and wore only one robe. My evil deeds were completely eliminated. Why did I still lack blessings to the point that today I am a hungry and miserable person?" Pham Sang replied: "In the past, when you sat on the dharma throne, you used to say many superstitious things, causing your listeners to become suspicious, and your moral conduct was still lacking, so you had to be punished like today." Saying this, he took out a transparent mirror from the bowl and said: "I can't do anything about the past, but you want to know the fate of high and low, short life, and the future, up to the rise and fall of the Dharma, so you'll see clearly by looking at it." He took the mirror and looked at it for a while, then handed it back and said: "Retribution, honor and glory, thanks to Your grace, are now known." The Sanskrit monk took the mirror and put it in the bowl, held his hand and walked with him, after about ten steps he disappeared.

That night he went to Linh An pagoda and asked to leave the home life, his name was Giam Khong. After receiving the monkhood ordination, he immediately went to practice, his asceticism and noble conduct were praised by everyone. Later, meditation master Giam Khong met Mr. Lieu Sinh at Thien Truc pagoda, described his ancestors and said: "I have lived for seventy-seven years, Sangha has lived for thirty-two, now I have only nine years left to live my full life. After I pass away, will the Buddhadharma still be the same as it is today?" I heard something strange and asked. The monk did not answer, but only asked for a pen to write a few lines on the north wall of the Tang Kinh building as follows: "The grain of sand increases, the sand of the Ganges river declines. Rabbits were caught in nets and dogs hunted them. Buffaloes and tigers fight with horns and teeth. The light of the sandalwood flower still shines for thousands of years." This is the monk's prophecy. The previous sentence talks about the Dharma that will decline. The second sentence indicates a very cruel destruction of religion. The third sentence clearly states that the time to destroy the dharma is in the year of At Suu, followed by Binh Dan. The last sentence says: However, Buddha's teachings still exist, the light of the path is not destroyed. The above prophecy corresponds to Tang Vo Ton's destruction of the Buddha Dharma. This king ordered the destruction of forty-seven thousand pagodas and forced more than twenty-seven thousand monks and nuns to return to the secular life. (Excerpt from Cao Tang's story, Cam Thong series, volume 3).

• During the Yuan Dynasty in China, in the year of Canh Ngo, the year of Chi Thuan in the Triet Tay region, there were consecutive crop failures. In Hangzhou city, people were starving to death lying on the streets. Every morning, the chief guard hired someone to carry the corpse and drop it into the mountain cave, behind Thai Hoa tower. Among the corpses was the body of an old woman who did not stink for more than ten days, and every day she rose to lie on top of other corpses. They were surprised, pulled the rope and brought it up. Inside, they found a cloth bag containing three Amitabha Buddha recitations. This matter was passed to Mandarin Huu Tu, who ordered the coffin to be shrouded in shroud and burned. When the wood is burned, in the fire and smoke, a Buddha statue, Bodhisattva, appears with bright light. Because of that cause, many people started thinking about Buddha. (Excerpt from Son Am Tap Luc).

Looking at the above story, we see that Mr. Giam Khong was a lecturer in his previous life; The root of the worldly world has been removed, cultivating is also very difficult, but because the fruit has not yet been attained and there are still some blemishes, one must transform into a hungry, thirsty and miserable scholar. In the past life, with five fellow practitioners, only the Sanskrit monk alone achieved liberation.

In addition to Mr. Giam Khong, there is also the story of the great monk Vien Quan, because he was not yet clean of karma, so he could not escape the fetus of Vuong Thi. The story of Bhikkhu Phap Van used to be a great Dharma Master, but because he was greedy for profit and sharing the Buddha Dharma, he fell into the body of a buffalo. The story of Mr. Hai „n, also a famous monk, because of making offerings, had to be reincarnated as the daughter of a benefactor. The story of Mat Son has an extraordinary background, but because of the karma he discovered from countless lifetimes, Samsara becomes a fool and hates people who practice recitation. The story of Duan Nghia Nhai who participated in meditation and became enlightened, reincarnated as a monk in his next life, was worshiped by people making offerings, and enjoyed blessings but forgot the path of liberation. In the story of Master Tuyet Hoc Thanh Cong's disciple, meditation clearly shows the source of the mind, because he has not yet attained enlightenment, his next body becomes an intelligent monk, filled with luxury and arrogance, and from then on there is no evil karma that he does not do. The story of a nun chanting the Lotus Sutras for thirty years, because her mind had not yet stopped reciting beauty and sound, she fell into the body of a singer in her next life, the beauty of her voice often emitting the scent of lotus flowers from her mouth. The story of a monk from Nhan Dang mountain who, because he had not yet attained enlightenment, became Tan Coi in his next life. Because of his previous merits in cultivating and reciting, he was intelligent enough to pass the exam to become a top-ranked mandarin, but because of his love for power and nobility, he created evil things and fell into the three realms for many lifetimes.

Looking at old stories, there are so many more cases like that! Through the above examples, we see that if we practice on our own, when karma has not been purified of emptiness, when we are reborn, we must be confused, ten people have failed eighty-nine. As for the old woman reciting Buddha, although she was ignorant of morality and did not understand anything about religion or religion, thanks to her sincere recitation of Amitabha, many strange things happened after death, proving that the old woman's rebirth of Ultimate Bliss was beyond doubt. Therefore, participating in meditation, chanting sutras and practicing other disciplines are valuable things to do and should be encouraged. But in the midst of this Dharma-ending age, it is necessary to further practice Buddha Recitation, and then bring all those dedicating merits to the West, to be sure of avoiding samsara and depravity. If you do not take Pure Land as a guide, then the merit of cultivating other subjects will only cause good roots, blessings, and favorable conditions to attain salvation later. Thus, I am afraid that when reincarnated, the karma-creating coma will have to stagnate for a long time in the suffering of samsara. Few people are as intelligent as the national teacher Ngo Dat, who for ten lifetimes was a high monk practicing meditation, and in his last lifetime, at the age of fourteen, he preached the entire Nirvana Sutra. But because of a passionate thought in front of the incense throne, he was reprimanded and scolded. After returning to chant Buddha's name, he received rebirth liberation. Those who rely on their own intelligence, talk about mystical theories, only focus on self-reliance and despise reciting the Buddha's name, should also look at the above example and think carefully.

-ooOoo-

Chapter II: Second Essential - Reciting the Buddha's name must develop Bodhi heart

Khai De:

The three realms are not at peace

Where is the land of true joy and suffering?

impermanence,

Scene of impermanence!

Advise to wake up together

Return to the clear enlightenment pool.

Awaken compassion and wisdom

Wishing to save the ten directions.

Three monks practice countless lives throughout their lifetimes.

Persevere and do not give up

Pray for the throne of the Dharma King!

---o0o---

Section A. Essay on Bodhi Mind

tom_tat: Reciting Buddha's merits to pray for petty blessings and benefits in the world is not in accordance with Buddha's original vision, so practitioners must recite Buddha's name for the sake of escape from the samsara cycle of life and death. But if it's for your own liberation...
noi_dung:
Section 8 - Meaning of Bodhi Mind

Reciting Buddha's merits to pray for petty blessings and benefits in the world is not in accordance with Buddha's original vision, so practitioners must recite Buddha's name for the sake of escape from the samsara cycle of life and death. But if we practice meditation for our own liberation, it only matches Buddha's vision to a small extent. So what is Buddha's ultimate goal? - The Buddha's true ambition is for all sentient beings to escape the cycle of birth and death and to be enlightened like Him. Therefore, people who recite Buddha's name need to develop Bodhi mind.

• Bodhi means Enlightenment. There are three levels in it: Sravaka Bodhi, Pratyekabuddha Bodhi, and Buddha Bodhi. This refers to the enlightenment fruit of the Sravaka class, the enlightenment fruit of the Pratyekabuddha class and the enlightenment fruit of the Buddha class. The person who recites Buddha's name generates Bodhi mind, which is the mind to seek Buddha's enlightenment; That state of being is the ultimate, beyond all Sravaka Pratyekabuddha, so it is called the Supreme Bodhi. This mind consists of two main seeds, compassion and wisdom, or gives rise to the power of saving oneself and all sentient beings.

To confirm again, the Bodhi mind mentioned here is the Supreme Bodhi mind, which refers to Buddha Bodhi, not Sravaka or Pratyekabuddha Bodhi mind.

• Sutra says: "Bodhi mind is the cause, compassion is the basis, means is the end." For example, a person going far must first identify the destination, be aware of the purpose of the journey, and finally use a vehicle, boat, or plane to proceed. Likewise, practitioners must first take Supreme Bodhi as their ultimate goal; Take great compassion for the benefit of yourself and others as the main goal of your practice; And next, depending on your fundamental preferences, choose the methods of meditation, purity, or esoteric practice as a means of practice. Means in a broader sense is also the wisdom and power to adapt to the occasion, applying all favorable actions while practicing the Bodhisattva path. Therefore, Bodhi mind is the goal that needs to be identified by the practitioner, before starting the practice of monkhood. Therefore, the previous chapter mentioned the necessity of Buddha's Recitation and its purpose of escaping from birth and death, the next chapter needs to note Bodhi mind as the final focus to reach. In the past, when the World-Honored One preached about the Four Noble Truths, he should have first said that the Noble Truth of Origin is the cause, but He placed the Noble Truth of Suffering first, wanting to present the results of suffering so that living beings can easily see them so that they can be apprehensive and attentive, and then look for the root cause. Likewise, here the writer follows the opinion of the ancestors, first raising the Buddha's Recitation for liberation as an urgent issue, and then discussing the Bodhi mind.

Avatamsaka Sutra says: "If you forget the Bodhi mind and practice good dharmas, that is karma." This statement turns out to be very true. For example, if a person sets out without knowing where he will go, and for what purpose, then won't the journey become meandering, tiring, and useless? The same is true for practitioners, if they use hard work and forget the goal of praying to become a Buddha for their own benefit, then many good deeds will only bring the result of enjoying divine blessings, but in the end they will still be immersed in the path of samsara, suffering boundless suffering. So if that's not karma, what else is it? Then, generating the Supreme Bodhi mind to benefit yourself and all sentient beings, must be recognized as a very essential point of generating the mind.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Lesson 9 - Bodhi Mind with Pure Land Subject
tom_tat: * Buddha Dharma according to customization, usually has two levels: Hinayana and Mahayana. The Hinayana speaks of low and small dharmas, focusing on the goal of urgently praying for one's own life and death, and only reaching Arhat or...
noi_dung:
Lesson 9 - Bodhi Mind with Pure Land Subject

• Buddha Dharma according to customization, usually has two levels: Hinayana and Mahayana. The Hinayana speaks of low and small dharmas, focusing on the goal of urgently praying for one's own birth and death, and only reaching the level of Arhat or Pratyekabuddha. Mahayana teaches vast dharmas, aiming to spread the vow to liberate all sentient beings, and reach the Full Enlightenment of the Tathagata. The Buddha's Recitation Dharma belongs to the Mahayana, so it not only goes in the direction of saving oneself but also saves others.

Buddhism was introduced to China and was propagated by the Patriarchs, resulting in the establishment of ten sects. Among them, there are two sects belonging to Hinayana: Thanh That Tong and Cau Xa Tong. But the nature of the Chinese people is not compatible with the Hinayana dharma, so these two sects soon faded away. The other eight sects belong to Mahayana, including Thien Thai sect, Hien Thu sect, Tam Luan sect, Phap Hien sect, Luat sect, Zen school, Tantric sect and Pure Land sect. Pure Land Buddhism's propaganda method is the Buddha Recitation method. If this method only preached self-liberation, I'm afraid it would have been destroyed like the other two Hinayana sects a long time ago. Our country, Vietnam, is a peninsula in the coastal region. Our people tend to have a wide range of thinking activities, so most of them are suitable for Mahayana. So from ancient times until now, in this country, Zen school and Pure Land have prevailed.

• Discussing dharma, which dharma leads to the ultimate Buddhahood, preaching extensively on external precepts and benefiting others, that is the Mahayana dharma. On the contrary, it is the Hinayana dharma. But the main point to distinguish between Hinayana and Mahayana is the mind, not the dharma. If you use the Hinayana dharma to propagate as a means to lead to Buddhahood, then that is Mahayana. Isn't that so, when the Tathagata teaches about Hinayana Buddhism, is he also a Hinayana person? For that reason, people who recite Buddha's name need to focus on developing the mind, that is, developing the Supreme Bodhi mind. The Buddha Recitation method already belongs to the Mahayana dharma. If a practitioner practices according to this method and develops great Bodhi mind, then the mind and dharma will both be complete and will reach Complete Enlightenment and also benefit oneself and others. If you develop the mind of human nature and recite the Buddha, then the method of reciting Buddha becomes the dharma of human nature. People who recite Buddha's name and develop such a mind will only enjoy luxury in the human and celestial realms. When the blessings are exhausted, they will suffer samsara and fall. If you develop the Hinayana mind and recite Buddha's name, then the Buddha's Recitation will become the Hinayana dharma. People who chant the Buddha's name and develop this mind will only attain the low, incomplete enlightenment of Sravaka Pratyekabuddha. They will also commit a small and narrow-minded lack of compassion, only worrying about their own liberation and not caring about the many other suffering sentient beings. Therefore, reciting Buddha requires developing the Supreme Bodhi mind. Proverbs often say: "One mistake, a thousand miles." Isn't it a very interesting thing for people who recite Buddha's name to practice correctly towards the starting point of their mind?

---o0o---

Section B. The Virtues of Bodhi Mind

tieu_de: Lesson 10 - How to Develop Bodhi's Heart
tom_tat: Boundless sentient beings vow to save. Endless afflictions vow to end. Countless Dharma methods vow to learn. Buddha's supreme vow
noi_dung:
Lesson 10 - How to Develop Bodhi's Heart

Developing Bodhi mind as mentioned above can be summarized in four vows:

Boundless sentient beings vow to save.

Endless afflictions vow to end.

Countless Dharma methods vow to learn.

Buddha vows to achieve the supreme path.

But it's not just talk: "I have developed Bodhi mind", is to have developed the mind, or every day to recite the four oaths, is called to have developed Bodhi mind. To develop Bodhi mind, practitioners need to observe to develop the mind realistically, and act according to that wish in their spiritual life. There are Buddhists who leave the home life, lay, every day after chanting Buddha sutras, they kneel and read the dedicating merit: "May I eliminate the three hindrances and afflictions...", but then in action it's the opposite: Today we are greedy, tomorrow we are angry, one day we are lazy and lazy, the other day we speak ill and criticize others, so that the next day we have arguments and quarrels and hate each other. Thus, how can the three hindrances be eliminated, and how can afflictions be eliminated? Most of us only practice in the form of meditation, paying little attention to initiation, so the fire of the three poisons still burns brightly, unable to enjoy the pure flavor of liberation taught by the Buddha. So here it is necessary to ask the question "How to develop Bodhi mind?" If we want Bodhi to arise in a real way, we should meditate and observe to develop our mind according to the following six key points:

• The first point is enlightenment of the mind. Sentient beings often accept this body as me, the mind with understanding, sadness, anger, love and joy is me. But in reality, this physical body is false, one day when it dies it will dissolve into dust, so the body of the four elements is not me. The same goes for the mind, it is just a synthesis of the knowledge of the six senses: form, sound, smell, taste, touch, dharma, like a person who was previously ignorant, but now studies Vietnamese and English, and when he is successful, he has knowledge of Vietnamese and English. Like someone who doesn't know Paris, after a trip to France, he collects images of that city in his mind. When returning to my hometown, someone mentioned Paris, and the scene of that city immediately appeared in my mind. That knowledge was previously non-existent, but when it was received into the past, it was temporarily present, but then neglected without thinking about it. Gradually it would fade away until it completely disappeared, returning to nothing. Our knowledge sometimes exists, sometimes not, this image disappears, another image appears, depending on the world, it always changes, it is false and not real, so it is not us. The ancients said: "The body is like foam, the mind is like the wind. Illusory appearances have no basis, no real nature." If you enlighten your body and mind as illusion, without attachment, you will gradually enter the realm of "emptiness". there is no more ego. If our ego is empty, then the ego of others is also empty, so there is no human form. The self of oneself and others is empty, and the self of countless sentient beings is also empty, so there is no form of sentient beings. The self is empty, so there is no lasting ego, no one can truly attain it, not even the everlasting realization of Nirvana, so there is no false life. This needs to be clearly recognized, it is not that there is no real true self of the eternal True Nature, but because the saint does not accept attachment, that entity becomes emptiness.

If the cause is not, then the Dharma is also not, because the situation is always changing, arising and dying, and has no self-substance. Here again we need to clearly realize that it is not only when dharmas are destroyed that they become empty, but because they are illusory, they are inherently empty, and so is the Human Being. Therefore, the ancients said: "There's no need to wait for the flowers to fall. I just realized that form is empty." (Ha Tu Dai Lac Hoa Lac. Naturally, the queen said no).

When the practitioner has enlightened that Nhon and Dharma are both empty, he should keep his heart pure and clear without attachment and recite Buddha's name. Using enlightenment like that to practice the path is called developing Bodhi mind.

• Điểm thứ hai: is Equality of Mind. In the Sutra, the Buddha advises: "All living beings have Buddha nature, are the parents of past lives and all Buddhas of future lives." All Buddhas see that living beings are Buddhas, so they should use a mind of equality and great compassion to help them. Sentient beings see that all Buddhas are sentient beings, so they start to feel afflicted with discrimination, hatred, and contempt. Same view, but different because of delusion and enlightenment. As Buddha disciples, we should obey the Buddha's teachings, to have equality and respect for living beings, because all future Buddhas are of the same Buddha nature. When you practice mindfulness with equality, respect and reverence, you will end the karma obstacle of discrimination and contempt, and give rise to good virtues. Using such equanimity to practice the Dharma is called developing Bodhi mind.

• Điểm thứ ba: is compassionate Mind. We and all sentient beings have all the virtues and wisdom of the Tathagata, but because we are ignorant of true nature and karma, we must suffer samsara and endure boundless suffering. Now that it is clear, we must stop hating, loving, and discriminating, and start feeling compassion and repentance to find a way to save ourselves and others, so that together we can be happy and free from suffering. We should clearly recognize that compassion is different from love. Love is love that is attached to form, so the result is bound by the rope of love. compassion is the mercy that saves, that separates appearances, regardless of attachments; This mind manifests itself in all aspects, so the result is increased happiness, liberation blessings and wisdom.

If we want to broaden our compassion mind, we should, from our own suffering, sympathize with the more difficult to endure suffering of others, naturally giving birth to compassion and wanting to save, and from there arises Bodhi's compassion concept. Basically, in the current war situation, children have to rely on their parents to raise them, but their parents are killed and become orphans. It's like an old person who has to rely on his children to take care of him, but his children all die prematurely, so he has to feel sad and lonely. Seeing these scenes, moved with compassion and wanting to save, Bodhi's compassion thought that had not yet arisen suddenly arose spontaneously.

Smart, healthy young men with hopeful futures were suddenly crippled by bombs and bullets. Many young women are in the prime of their youth, and loved ones they rely on are suddenly snatched away by death, causing them to lose their way to depravity, or become widows and orphans, leaving their future survival uncertain. Seeing these scenes, moved with compassion and wanting to save, Bodhi's compassion thoughts that had not yet arisen suddenly arose spontaneously.

There are many people who are sick, but because of the high price of things, there is no money for medicine, so their illness and suffering prolong for years, sometimes many people have to commit suicide. There are poor people who have lost their karma, today their wife is sick, tomorrow their children are sick, they are wandering around in rags, they are in debt, they are hungry and cold day by day, they live a miserable life and even die. There are also those who have many sad feelings and have no good friends to advise and explain; Those who are confused and create karma do not know that tomorrow they will suffer, and do not meet Buddha's teachings to find a way to escape. Seeing these scenes, moved with compassion and wanting to save, Bodhi's compassion thoughts that had not yet arisen suddenly arose spontaneously.

Broadly speaking, as in the Avatamsaka Sutra, Samantabhadra taught: "Bodhisattva contemplates helpless beings and arouses great compassion. Observing the nature of sentient beings without any favorable conditions causes great compassion. Contemplating poor sentient beings without good roots causes great compassion. Observe sentient beings sleeping soundly in the long night of ignorance and generate great compassion. Observe sentient beings who do evil things and generate great compassion. Observe sentient beings who are bound, and like to throw themselves into the bondage, to generate great compassion. Observe sentient beings immersed in the ocean of birth and death and generate great compassion. Observing living beings with long-term suffering causes great compassion. Observing sentient beings, not liking good dharmas, gives rise to great compassion. Observing sentient beings who are far away from Buddha's teachings leads to great compassion..."

Having developed a great heart of compassion, one must develop a great mind of Bodhi vowing salvation. Then great compassion and great Bodhi are mutually compatible. Therefore, developing a compassionate mind means developing a Bodhi mind. Using great compassion like that to practice religion is called developing Bodhi mind.

• The fourth point is Joyful Heart. If there is compassion, it must be expressed through joy. There are two things here: rejoicing and letting go. Rejoicing is when you see that above, from all Buddhas, Saints, down to all kinds of sentient beings, you can rejoice in any merit, no matter how small. And when we see someone receiving blessings, prosperity, success, and peace, we also have happy thoughts and rejoice. Joyful equanimity means that even if sentient beings do evil, ungrateful, destructive, malicious, or harmful things to others or themselves, they can patiently and happily ignore them. If we think deeply about this happiness and patience, it turns out that there is no real patience, because human appearance, self appearance, and harmful brain appearance are all empty. So the Diamond Sutra teaches: "The Tathagata said that the Paramita of patience is not the Paramita of patience, that is called the Paramita of patience."

A joyful heart can eliminate petty jealousy. The joy of letting go can be overcome by hatred and revenge. Because the heart of joy is not expressed outside of enlightenment, that is Bodhi's heart. Using such joy to practice the Dharma is called developing Bodhi mind.

• The fifth point is Repentance and Prayer of the Mind. In samsara life, all living things are constantly changing and are related to each other. Yet, because of confusion and error, from the beginningless life until now, due to the ego-centred desire to benefit ourselves, we have harmed sentient beings, creating boundless and boundless evil karma. Even all Buddhas and saints, out of great compassion, were born to preach the Dharma to save sentient beings, including me, but towards the Three Jewels I was ungrateful and destructive. In today's enlightenment, we must be ashamed and repent, bringing our three karmas to repentance. Maitreya Bodhisattva ascended the throne and never returned, because he wanted to quickly attain Buddhahood, and still prayed six times a day. So we must bring our karma body to pay homage to the Three Jewels, our karma speech to express our sins and pray to be eliminated, our karma mind to sincerely repent and vow not to commit the same sin again. Having repentance, one must completely stop the evil mind and no longer allow it to continue, until one reaches the point where the mind and the scene are both empty, which is true repentance. You have to make vows again, vowing to ascend the throne of the Three Jewels, vowing to save all sentient beings, to atone for past sins and repay four heavy favors. The four graces are: Gratitude to the Three Jewels, gratitude to parents and elders, gratitude to good and knowledgeable friends, and gratitude to sentient beings.

With such a mind of repentance and vows, only then will the sins and obstacles be eliminated, merit will increase day by day, and only then will we reach the place of blessings and full wisdom. Using such repentance and vows to practice the Dharma is called developing Bodhi mind.

• The sixth point is the Unrelenting Mind. Even though you have repentance making vows to practice, karma or demonic obstacles are not easy to eliminate, and establishing merit and cultivating virtue that represents the six degrees of all virtues is not easy to achieve. But Bodhi's path to enlightenment is far away and full of hardships and hardships. It must go through many lifetimes, not just one or two lifetimes? In his previous life, Sariputta attained the throne of the Six Pillars and developed the great Bodhi mind of cultivating giving. But when he endured the pain of gouging out an eye for a pagan, but they didn't use it, threw him to the ground, spit on him, and trampled on it with his feet. He still lost his Mahayana mind. Then we see that keeping one's vow is not easy! Therefore, practitioners who want to have an irreversible path of enlightenment must make solid vows. Swear that: "Even if this body is subjected to countless hardships and humiliations, or is beaten and killed until it burns and crumbles to ashes, it will not commit evil deeds or retreat from practice because of that." Using such an irreversible heart to practice the Dharma is called developing the Bodhi mind.

The six essential points outlined above are a must-have for those who develop Bodhi mind. If you do not follow this and establish sincere practice, then even if you say that you are developing your mind, it is just creating your mind, and you will not be able to reach Buddhahood. There are only two paths before us: samsara and liberation. Although the path to liberation has many difficulties, each step leads to clarity, freedom, and joy. Although the samsara path temporarily enjoys heavenly blessings, it ends up moving to the three evil realms, with boundless suffering from which there is no way to escape. Therefore, fellow practitioners should develop a strong mind and step straight onto the bright path of Bodhi. The scene of flowers blooming on the horizon of liberation will welcome you!

---o0o---

tom_tat: Regarding Bodhi mind, there are many explanations in the inner scriptures. Now I would like to quote just a few passages from the Avatamsaka Sutra so that fellow practitioners can understand.
noi_dung:
Section 11 - Instructions on Bodhi Mind

Regarding Bodhi mind, there are many explanations in the inner scriptures. Now I would like to quote just a few passages from the Avatamsaka Sutra so that fellow practitioners can understand:

• Hey good man! The Bodhisattva who aspires to Supreme Bodhi is: Generate great compassion to save all sentient beings. Start making offerings all Buddhas, to serve the purpose. Aspire everywhere to seek the Dharma, all without regret. Arousing great ambition, praying to Nhat Thiet Tri. Generate immeasurable great kindness and compassion for all sentient beings. Aspire to not abandon sentient beings wearing armor and vows to pray for Prajnaparamita. Start your heart without deceit, because you seek true wisdom. Start practicing as you say, to practice the Bodhisattva path. Arise not to lie to all Buddhas, for the sake of preserving the great vows of all Tathagata. Start praying to Nhat Thiet Tri to teach and transform sentient beings until the end of future lives. Bodhisattva used the Bodhi mind merits as many as the dust of the Buddha realm, so he was born in the Tathagata's house.

• Hey good man! Like someone learning to shoot, they must first practice standing, then learn how to shoot. Likewise, if Bodhisattva wants to learn the Tathagata's path of Universal Wisdom, he must first abide in the Bodhi mind, and then practice all Buddha dharmas. Good man! For example, although the prince is still a child, all the ministers must pay homage. Likewise, although Bodhisattva has just developed the Bodhi mind to practice Bodhisattva conduct, all the veterans of the Second Vehicle must respect and respect him. Good man! Like the crown prince, although he is not yet at peace with his servants, he has all the qualities of a king, his servants cannot compare, because of his noble birth. In the same way, Bodhisattva, although not yet free from all karma afflictions, still has the full Bodhi form, cannot be compared to the Second Vehicle, because thanks to its seed nature, it ranks first. Good man! Like a wooden robot, without the key, the separate body parts cannot function. Likewise, if Bodhisattva lacks Bodhi mind, all actions will be scattered and all Buddha dharmas cannot be achieved. Good man! Like diamond, all things cannot be destroyed. On the contrary, all things can be destroyed, but their essence remains undamaged. Bodhisattva's Bodhi mind is the same, throughout three lifetimes in countless lifetimes, he teaches and transforms sentient beings, practices asceticism, and does all the things that cannot be done in the Second Vehicle, but in the end he still does not get tired of reducing damage...

• Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said: - Good man! Bodhisattva, in order to subdue and educate all sentient beings, should develop Bodhi mind. To eliminate the accumulation of suffering for all sentient beings, one should develop Bodhi mind. To bring all sentient beings complete happiness, one should develop Bodhi mind. To eliminate the ignorance of all sentient beings, one should develop Bodhi mind. In order to bring Buddha wisdom to all sentient beings, we should develop Bodhi mind. Because we respectfully make offerings to all Buddhas, we should develop Bodhi mind. Because following the Tathagata's teachings makes all Buddhas happy, he should develop Bodhi mind. Because we want to see the perfect physical appearance of all Buddhas, we should develop Bodhi mind. Because you want to enter the vast wisdom of all Buddhas, you should develop Bodhi mind. Because we want to display virtues: The power and fearlessness of all Buddhas should generate Bodhi mind.

• Thus, in the Avatamsaka Sutra, the World-Honored One and the Bodhisattvas have extensively explained the merits of Bodhi mind. Above, we only summarize a few key points. sutra text also says: "The key to entering the path is to first develop your mind. When it comes to practicing, you should first make a vow."

If you don't develop a broad mind and make a strong vow, then even if you go through countless lifetimes, you will still be in the path of samsara; Even if you practice, it is difficult to be diligent and only work hard. Therefore you should know: If you want to study Buddha's way, you must develop Bodhi mind that cannot be delayed. Therefore, in the past, Great Master Am Province composed the Phat Bodhi Mind Text to encourage the four assemblies. In it, according to the wishes, He presented the development of the mind into eight ways: evil, right, true, false, great, small, heavenly, perfect. Please summarize as follows:

1. There are practitioners who do not seek to save their own minds, only follow the outside, or seek fame and profit, indulge in present happiness, or hope for future blessings and develop Bodhi. Developing such a mind is called evil.

2. Just like not seeking fame and profit, not being greedy for happy scenes and hoping for blessings, just to escape the cycle of birth and death, to benefit yourself and benefit others, you seek Bodhi. Developing the mind like that is called Right.

3. Each thought above is to seek Buddha's way, below is to save sentient beings, look at the long Bodhi path without fear, see sentient beings that are difficult to save but do not falter. A steadfast mind is like climbing a mountain determined to reach the top, like climbing a tower determined to reach the end. Developing such a mind is called Truth (truth).

4. There are sins that do not repentance, but on the outside they are pure, on the inside they are dirty, first they are diligent, then they become lazy. Even though he has a good heart, it is mixed with fame and fortune. He has good dharma but is contaminated by sin. If you develop your mind and still have these things, it's called Wei (lies).

5. When the world of living beings ends, only the wish will end; When the Bodhi religion is achieved, the wish will be fulfilled. Developing such a mind is called Great.

6. Viewing the three worlds as a prison, birth and death as injustice; I just want to quickly liberate myself, I don't want to save people. Developing the mind according to this concept is called Small.

7. Seeing that sentient beings and the Buddha path are outside of one's own nature, then making the vow to save one's life, the path of merit is not forgotten, the seeing and understanding do not end. Developing a mind like that is called Thien (deviation).

8. Knowing that sentient beings and the Buddha path are both self-nature, so when we pray to save them, we do not see that we have cultivated merit, and to save sentient beings we do not see that there are sentient beings saved. Developing a mind like that is called Vien (circle).

In the eight ways as above, Evil, Wei, Thien, Small should be abandoned, True, Right, Vien, Great should be followed. Only then is it called developing Bodhi mind properly.

In the text, Master Tinh Am advises the public to think of ten causes and conditions to develop their minds. Those ten conditions are: because of thinking of Buddha's gratitude, because of gratitude to parents, because of gratitude to elders, because of gratitude for almsgiving, because of gratitude to living beings, because of worrying about the suffering of birth and death, respecting the spiritual nature, because of repentance and eliminating karma obstacles, because of upholding the Dharma, because of praying for birth in the Pure Land. When praying for Pure Land, He quoted a verse of the Amitabha Sutra and said: "sutra text says: You cannot use your little merits and blessings to be born in that country. So you know, you must have many merits and blessings to be able to rebirth Ultimate Bliss. But many good roots are nothing more than developing Bodhi mind, many merits and blessings are nothing more than reciting the name. A moment of reciting the Buddha's mind is better than giving for many years; truly generating Bodhi's heart is better than practicing for many lifetimes. Maintain these two causes and conditions and decide to be born in Ultimate Bliss."

Through the teachings of Buddha, Bodhisattva, and Patriarch above, we see that developing Bodhi mind is very important on the path of practice.

---o0o---

Section C. Three Essential Facts For Bodhi Mind

noi_dung:
Section 12 - The Road to Life and Death is Many Danger

• The path to the enlightenment garden has many doors. Practitioners must first take the great Bodhi mind as the true starting point, then depending on their base of interest, it is good to follow any method they want to practice. On the path of practice, if we discuss "fundamentals" The Pure Land subject includes all three senses, upper, middle, and lower; Not only ordinary people, but also Bodhisattvas such as Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Ma Minh, and Nagarjuna all vow to be reborn. If discussing "weather" In this Dharma-ending age, most sentient beings have heavy mental hindrances. Pure Land is easy to practice and can achieve rebirth liberation in one lifetime. But, if we talk about preferences, Pure Land alone cannot satisfy everyone, that's why the Tathagata talks about many methods. In general, people with powerful minds and fondness for simplicity, directness and clarity, like to go to Zen school. Those who love mysterious supernatural powers and practice in Tantric Buddhism. Those who love theory need to analyze it thoroughly before they believe in it and follow it, preferring to practice Only Thuc Thuc Tong... In each sect, there are many different details, which each person practices differently.

However, in the age of the end of the Dharma, the practitioner has developed the great Bodhi mind, vowing to save sentient beings, and wants to ensure that that mind is accomplished and does not fall into loss; Even if you practice other disciplines, you should also practice Pure Land to pray for rebirth. Why? There are three essential events here, let's give an outline in order:

• In the samsara path of life and death, there are many dangers and obstacles to the path of practice. If you want to escape the danger of samsara to ensure that Bodhi's mind does not lose its way, you must pray to be born in the Pure Land. This is the first essential event that practitioners need to pay attention to.

• Immortal Virtue always reminds: "Nếu tu mà không chuyên cầu giải thoát, thì sự tu nơi kiếp này là mối thù trong kiếp thứ ba." The reason for this is because in the first life he practiced hard and endured hardship, so he was reborn in the second life and enjoyed the retribution of intelligence, wealth, and power. In this second life, due to wealth, it is easy to become addicted to the sight of nobility, a beautiful wife and children, and material pleasures in the world. Once you have tasted sensual pleasures, it is easy to become addicted, the more you become infected, the more you will go to a dark place of depravity, daring to do many evil things to consolidate your power and satisfy your ambitions. In the second life, having planted such causes, how can the third life avoid falling into the three realms?

Someone commented: "In the previous life, there was good practice and sowing good causes, is it possible that in the second life all the good roots of wisdom will be lost, leading to the fall?" - Please answer: "Even though the good roots are there, the evil karma from countless eons has not been eliminated. But in the mundane world, good deeds are as difficult to do as climbing a tall tree, evil deeds are as easy to commit as falling down a steep slope. Didn't the ancients say: Doing good all your life is not enough; One day of doing evil, will the evil be left over? Like the rich and powerful people we see now, in their past lives they all had more or less merit giving tu blessings to do good deeds, but there were not many who were inclined to the good path, and those who were passionate about fame, fortune, and glory were the majority. I wonder how many noble people who passed the home life would leave the home life, living an austere and frugal life, aiming for the noble goal of liberation? Even like people leaving the home life, when they don't have a position, they still practice patiently. When they have gained power, many people worship and respect making offerings, but are easily bound by the worldly world. Right now I see so many good and faithful monks and nuns who were diligent in their practice before, but then gradually became lazy and abandoned their practice or returned to secular life, let alone the next life?"

• — The human world is still like that. If we are born in the heavenly world, the realm of five desires is too magical, and it is even more difficult to practice! That is to say those who have blessings, and those who have few blessings live a very poor life and it is difficult to practice. Or even though they are middle class, in this world there are a lot of evil ways; In the Dharma, good and knowledgeable people are difficult to find, the path to liberation is not easy to find! As for sentient beings in the three evil realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals, practicing recitation is extremely difficult, because those beings are stupid and their bodies and minds are always in a state of suffering.

Samsara life has many such dangers. If you do not pray to be born in the Pure Land to escape, it will be difficult to ensure that Bodhi's mind does not rot.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Section 13 - Need for liberation in the present life
tom_tat: * In the Dharma Ending Age, if you only practice other disciplines and do not seek Pure Land, it will be difficult to achieve liberation in one lifetime. If this life does not achieve liberation and is lost in the path of samsara, then all wishes will become illusory. This is the…
noi_dung:
Section 13 - Need for liberation in the present life

• In the Dharma Ending Age, if you only practice other disciplines and do not seek Pure Land, it will be difficult to achieve liberation in one lifetime. If this life does not achieve liberation and is lost in the path of samsara, then all wishes will become illusory. This is the second essential event that practitioners need to pay attention to.

Practitioners who practice other methods, focus only on self-reliance, establish an eternal mind, and believe that in each life they should continue to practice, even if they do not achieve liberation in this life, in future lives they will attain enlightenment. But there is one thing to pay attention to: will the next life be guaranteed for us to continue practicing? Because when you are not yet enlightened, when you are reincarnated, you must be in a coma and easily forget your wish to practice in your previous life. In the mundane world, the conditions for progress are few, but the conditions for falling back are many. How many people left the home life when they were reincarnated and could not progress to practice, as the stories outlined in the first chapter.

Kinh says: "Bodhisattva was still in love when he was pregnant, Sravaka was still in love when he was pregnant."

"Warm way" is to spread from one warm body to another warm body. Just as the present body is the pre-sackal, the body that is reborn in the next life is called the post-swarm; experiencing such an alternation from the front body to the back body, the unenlightened Bodhisattva must fall into a coma. In the scriptures, there is another place where it says: "Ordinary people are in a coma when entering, staying, and leaving the fetus. The Holy King of Chakravarti, due to blessings, knows that when he enters the womb, he will be in a coma when he comes out of the womb. Every Sravaka can wake up when he enters the womb and stays pregnant, but when he comes out of the womb, he falls into a coma. There is only Bodhisattva who attains the Forbearance of Non-Birth, who is aware at the time of entering, remaining in the womb and leaving the womb." Sometimes ordinary people, due to special karma conditions, can remember their previous lives, but this is only a rare case in all. Or it is Bodhisattva who appears to let living beings know that there is samsara, otherwise all are confused when reincarnated. Once in a coma, all knowledge of morality and wishes in previous lives are obscured by ignorance and forgotten.

Browsing through literature and writers, I once heard someone recount that when I was young, I dreamed of flying freely everywhere; As I get older, I see myself flying lower and lower, and then I can no longer fly. In the book The Guide to Buddhism, there is a story about Mr. Yuan Thu Dong, who lived in Truong Son in China. When he was four or five years old, in the dark he saw objects as clearly as during the day. Over the next few years, the blurred vision decreased. From the age of ten onwards, he no longer saw, only occasionally waking up in the middle of the night and seeing clearly for a moment. After about seventeen years old, I only saw it once every two or three years, but it only flashed and then went out. These people all practiced cultivation in their previous lives, but when they reincarnated, they became deluded. Then, their contamination became deeper and their divine power decreased. There are people like the Thien Dai Ngu Tu in Nhut Ban and Wei Tich Phu in China, who sit in one place and clearly see the surrounding objects several dozen miles away. There are many people who can see things on the ground, things beyond walls, or things in people's pockets, which the world calls the heavenly eye, but they do not practice. Therefore, gradually things decline, the end is the same as usual. There are also people who read a book once, then close it and recite it without missing a word. Or they quickly write a book, become rich, open their mouth and become a poet, but refuse to practice, and sometimes return to rejecting Buddhism. The ancients commented that later people, in their previous lives, had practiced meditation to a fairly high level and had achieved something. But because those who practice according to the sect only recognize their own mind, they destroy Buddha view and Dharma view, meaning that their mind is empty and does not see Buddha and Dharma; So when you have not attained enlightenment, you must reincarnate again, relying only on your intelligence and not liking Buddhism. The ancients were still like that, how much do current practitioners have?

• As Buddha said: "There are many people who practice in the Dharma-ending age, but it is difficult for anyone to attain enlightenment."
