But when you have not attained enlightenment, if you still have karma as small as a thread of silk, you will be samsara. Although there are a few people who have attained enlightenment, enlightenment is not yet a realization. It is only due to the power of concentration to subdue the karma consciousness that it calms them down, so they are temporarily enlightened, but when they are reincarnated, they are still in a coma and cannot be free. In the next life, the fate of progressing to the path will be less and more than turning back, and the vow of liberation will be difficult to maintain firmly. Regarding the loss of enlightenment, the ancients had three examples:

Điều thứ nhất: It's like using a rock to press down on weeds. Even though the grass can't grow, its roots haven't rotted yet. If there's a different fate, the rock is overturned and the grass will still grow back as before.

Điều thứ hai: Like water in a jar, the mud settles down and lies at the bottom, but before it can be filtered out, when there is a disturbance, the mud floats up again.

Điều thứ ba: Just like pottery, although it is shaped, it has not been re-fired to make it firm, so when it rains it will definitely disintegrate. The situation of enlightenment when reincarnated is easy to lose, the same again.

In the Dharma-ending age, how many cultivators are enlightened? Gnosticism is not easy. Like in the old days, the meditation master Huong Lam used the practice for forty years to fuse it into one piece. Mr. Truong Khanh Nhan sat down and tore a dozen cushions to see his original nature. People in today's world, except for a few Saints who have appeared in their bodies to serve as models for the masses, in addition to others who practice meditation, can only temporarily calm their bodies and minds or see good realms! Even if you have attained enlightenment, when you reincarnate, you can still encounter obstacles like those mentioned above. The path of life and death has many dangers and concerns for those who have not yet attained enlightenment. So if you say you are not afraid of birth and death, that is only the way of thinking of a short-sighted person.

Moreover, now that the Dharma has gradually disappeared, in the world, wherever materialist influence has spread, Buddhism is no longer there. There have been many places where temples and pagodas were destroyed, scriptures were burned, monks and nuns had to return to the secular life, and good believers were not allowed to practice. Even if it is restored one day, a large part of it will still be transformed and consumed. Wishing to be reincarnated to continue practicing with a decaying religion, lacking the guidance of high-ranking monks, where can we find a good opportunity to progress towards liberation in the future? Therefore, if you want to ensure that Bodhi's mind does not rot, you must practice Pure Land. Even if you practice other disciplines, you should also recite Buddha making vows rebirth about Ultimate Bliss.

This is the general advice of virtuous people like you: Lien Tri, Ngau Ich, Kien Mat, „n Quang.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Lesson 14 - How to Achieve Bodhi Mind
tom_tat: * Having developed the Bodhi mind, thinking carefully about the current situation, what means must be used for that mind to be fully achieved? - If you want the Bodhi vow to benefit yourself and others to be complete, there is nothing better than praying for birth in the Pure Land. This is…
noi_dung:
Lesson 14 - How to Achieve Bodhi Mind

• Having developed the Bodhi mind, thinking carefully about today's situation, what means must be used for that mind to be fully achieved? - If you want the Bodhi vow to benefit yourself and others to be complete, there is nothing better than praying for birth in the Pure Land. This is the third essential fact that practitioners need to pay attention to.

A noble person of ancient times, after making great vows to practice, uttered the sentence:

The world and the world are in decline everywhere.

If you don't recite Amitabha, who will you recite?

(The world, the worldly thinking changes.

Not thinking of Amitabha's wings and lobes?).

Indeed, when looking at these words, then thinking and comparing from the method to the foundation and current circumstances, perhaps practicing Pure Land is the most complete and safe path.

Someone asked: - If you have developed the mind to save sentient beings, you should stay in the Saha world, because there are many suffering sentient beings that need to be saved. Why do you seek to be reborn in the West?

- Please try asking again: What conditions are needed for birth to be achieved? Is it necessary to have: merits and blessings, wisdom, eloquence, supernatural powers, good looks? (But in those aspects, do we have any part yet?) Just the point of breaking troubles or generating wisdom to avoid being deluded by the mundane world, is not an easy thing! The ancients said: "Destroying ants is as difficult as stopping a forty-mile stream!" So, what can we say about delusion, delusion and ignorance? Misconceptions, simply put, are afflictions that see attachment to the gross; thoughts or mental afflictions. From countless lifetimes up to now, we have accumulated in our minds the defilements of greed, anger, and ignorance, and countless misunderstandings. Can we destroy them all in a short time in this life? Today's practitioners, most of the blessings are thin and shallow, just one Amitabha Buddha sentence, the recitation is not easy to master, let alone the freedom to save sentient beings, which is a far-fetched task? Therefore, what is necessary right now is that we should seek rebirth in the West, first save ourselves from falling into samsara, and rely on the favorable conditions in that realm to diligently practice. Wait until you attain the fruition, have enough wisdom, eloquence, supernatural powers, and good appearance, then you will return to Saha to save birth, and then you will be at peace. However, for the duty and compassion of practitioners, it is not necessary to completely reject saving sentient beings in this life. But our current benefit to others is actually only in the situation of depending on the situation, like a person falling into a river of delusion, both wading to the shore and calling and advising others to follow.

• To further expand, even if one attains the fruition of No Birth, although if one wants to practice to complete the six degrees, one must stay in the evil realm, but in fact one cannot leave the Pure Land. Why? - As the sutras say, the First Ground Bodhisattva cannot even know where to lift and put his feet down on the Second Ground, let alone know the Tathagata's realm? For that reason, in the Avatamsaka assembly, after preaching the ten great vows kings, Lord Samantabhadra immediately used verses to encourage Bodhisattvas throughout the fifty-one positions: The Ten Faiths, the Ten Pillars, the Ten Virtues, the Ten Describing merits, the Ten Grounds and the Enlightenment seek rebirth in Ultimate Bliss. Because the Pure Land Buddha often appears, to enter the Tathagata's secret realm, Bodhisattva must often be close to the Buddha. Therefore, Bodhisattva beings must, on the one hand, appear in the Impure Lands to practice meritorious deeds, and on the other hand, appear in the nearby Pure Lands to learn from all Buddhas to seek progress in practice. Pure Land rebirth is very necessary for ordinary people from the Eighth Ground to the Enlightened Bodhisattva level.

Just like the three events above, the samsara path has many obstacles. If you have not yet attained the fruit of No Birth, when you change the world, you will easily fall into a coma and fall. Therefore, in order to ensure that the great Bodhi mind does not become lost and to achieve this contentment, not only ordinary people like us, in order to urgently solve the samsara problem of birth and death before us, need to pray for rebirth. And when it comes to the Bodhisattva super land, if you want to enter the Tathagata's secret realm and fulfill those great vows, you cannot leave the Pure Land.

-ooOoo-

---o0o---

Chapter III Third Essential - Reciting the Buddha's Name Must Eliminate Doubt

Khai De:

Faith is the primordial step,

But the world is so charming!

At first I thought the lotus was intoxicated with the Pure Land

Listen to the beautiful apricot tree and love non meditation again.

Bodhi cleverly cast the curse of enlightenment

Non-existence still clings to duality

Faith and virtue are like vows

Rain of field flowers strolls through the landscape of Tay Thien.

---o0o---

Section A. Trust, Gateway to Pure Land

tom_tat: Living beings in this Saha world, because they are in an evil life with five defilements, heavy afflictions, and fierce external circumstances, their practice is not easy to progress. Every time I reincarnate, I often feel lost, so attainment is very difficult.…
noi_dung:
Lesson 15 - The Importance of Trust

Living beings in this Saha world, because they are in an evil life with five defilements, heavy afflictions, and fierce external circumstances, their practice is not easy to progress. Every time I reincarnate, I often feel lost, so attainment is very difficult. Tien Duc Hang laments: "The number of people leaving the home life is as numerous as buffalo hair, but enlightened people are like rabbit horns." (leaving the home life like a cow, attaining enlightenment like a rabbit). This word can visualize what was just mentioned above. the Original Teacher Shakyamuni Buddha is someone who has experienced the path to Buddhahood, knowing clearly which paths are easy to walk and which paths are difficult to walk. That's why he mobilized his compassion and wisdom, and especially opened the Buddha Recitation method. Even though people who practice this method have not yet finished their afflictions, they can receive karma rebirth. When you return to the West, thanks to the many wonderful conditions of that scene, the process of cultivating and attaining enlightenment is as easy as picking up the object in front of you.

The World-Honored One had such great compassion, everyone should have been saved with this method, but why are there so few people who are reborn? That's because sentient beings have poor karma, or doubt the Buddha's words and refuse to practice, or even though they practice, their faith and vows are not sincere, or even though they recite the Buddha's name, the effort is not in accordance with the Buddha's teachings. Therefore, even though we practice, it still does not bring results. That is the fault of the person, not the dharma.

• Avatamsaka Sutra says: "Faith is the first step in religion, the mother of all merits. Faith cultivates good roots. Faith or Buddha's Bodhi." Therefore, for practitioners, faith is very important. If you lose faith, not only will the foundation for progress collapse, but all liberation efforts will also fail. This faith is not superstition, it is faith based on wisdom, it is full faith in the words of Buddha, Bodhisattva and the Patriarchs taught in the scriptures. Why, after relying on wisdom, do we still have to put our full faith in the teachings of those beings? - Because the Pure Land discipline belongs to the Mahayana dharma, it is a great dharma that speaks of many extraordinary transcendent realms, so there are things that ordinary wisdom cannot fathom. Once upon a time on the Linh Son Assembly, the World-Honored One spoke of the Lotus Sutra. There were five thousand Venerable Sravakas, who had attained from the first stage of Sotapanna to the fourth stage of Arhat, and withdrew from the Dharma state without confidence. Regarding the scene where the Buddha himself is still speaking the Dharma in his avatar, and with the Sravaka saints whose wisdom is already extraordinary, but there is still disbelief, we see that the Mahayana Dharma is not easy to believe and understand. Therefore, in the Mahayana Sutras, there are many places where the Buddha tells you not to tell people who have many attachments and lack of faith, because they are afraid that they will be contemptuous and guilty. When the Mahayana dharma was widely spread, the ancients advised Buddhist students when studying this type of sutra, wherever they use wisdom to understand it is of course good, wherever their meditation is not thorough, they should still place full faith in the words of the World-Honored One. That way we can avoid the sin of disrespecting the great dharma, and not lose any benefits.

In the Amitabha Buddhist Sutra, the Original Teacher reminded us about faith several times, such as the passages: "So Shariputra! You must believe and accept my words and the words of all Buddhas!... Shariputra! As I today praise the inconceivable merits of all Buddhas. The other Buddhas also praised my inconceivable merits, saying the following: 'Shakyamuni Buddha often does very difficult things that are rare! He was able to live in an evil life with five defilements: The defects of life, the defects of views, the defects of afflictions, the defects of sentient beings, the defects of life in the Saha world, the attainment of Anuttara Sammyak Tam Bodhi, because of the sentient beings, the Dharma that the whole world finds difficult to believe is spoken.' - Shariputra! You should know that I am doing the following difficult thing in the evil life of the five defilements, which is to attain the fruition of Anuttara Sammyak Tam Bodhi, for the whole world to speak this unbelievable Dharma, it is truly a very difficult thing!"

The World-Honored One, who had miraculous wisdom and said those words, knew that the Pure Land Dharma was unbelievable, and belief was very important! Many ancient monks also said: "Pure Land Dharma is very difficult to believe in, only ordinary people have planted the good roots of reciting the Buddha's name and Bodhisattva Bodhisattva can believe and receive it. In addition, other sentient beings, up to the level of the Second Vehicle or the Bodhisattva position, sometimes do not believe in this method." When looking at the above words, the writer was initially surprised and wondered: "Why don't Buddha's disciples believe Buddha's words? The Bodhisattva of the Second Vehicle and the Bodhisattva have transcendent wisdom, their cultivation level has reached a high level, so why don't they believe in the Pure Land dharma?" But later, when I saw that in the Leaving the Home Life group there were those who preached the teachings expertly, but did not believe in the Ultimate Bliss realm and refuted the concept of Buddha rebirth, only then did I recognize that these words were true. By the way, looking in the sutras, I found that the eyes of Arhat and Bich Chi Buddha were only within the three thousand great thousand worlds, including one thousand million solar systems. The Pure Land discipline belongs to the outer world of great dharma, the realm of Ultimate Bliss is outside the great thousand worlds, so how can the ultimate fruition of the Second Vehicle be seen and received? As for Bodhisattva Bodhisattva, he has not yet entered the realm of the great and equal, and has not seen the Pure Land of the ten directions, so some do not believe and accept it as a matter of course.

• The essential point of Buddha Recitation is: Faith, Prayer, Happiness. These three things are interrelated like a tree with three legs; if one is missing, it will collapse. Here, faith is the foundation. If this necessity is lacking, it is impossible to give birth to Vows and promote sincere practice. As for Credit points, there are roughly three things: First, you must believe what the World-Honored One said, and be sure that the realm of Ultimate Bliss, from human beings to realms, is real. Next, we must believe that Amitabha does not make false vows. Even if sentient beings have heavy karma, if they recite His name, they will definitely be led to rebirth. Third, we must believe that we recite the Buddha's name, pray to the Buddha's realm, and be determined to see the Buddha's rebirth. Whatever cause and effect cannot be wrong. These three things are just the basics, if interpreted broadly, they include six parts: Believe in yourself, believe in Buddha, believe in cause, believe in results, believe in things, believe in reason. The first thing includes believing Buddha's words and believing that Pure Land's truth and principles are true. The second includes believing in the great vows of Amitabha Buddha and his guiding power. The third thing includes believing in one's own mind, the power of one's vows, and the cause and effect of the practice of reciting Buddha's name. Be sure of the three things just said, then it is called deep faith. Deep belief is not a matter of external words or discriminatory meanings, but a recognition, a pure mind without a single point of doubt. So once upon a time, Mr. Vuong Trong Hoi asked a wise man: "How can we be sure of being born into Ultimate Bliss?" He replied: "If you believe deeply, you will surely be reborn." He noted and understood those words, and indeed, his wish was later fulfilled.

Such is the benefit of deep trust.

---o0o---

tom_tat: In the spiritual world, there are people who also advise reciting the Buddha's name, but instead educate them in a pagan way. There are also people who do not understand or misunderstand Pure Land, so they create negative comments. Roughly saying: -…
noi_dung:
Section 16 - Things That Destroy Faith

In the spiritual world, there are people who also advise reciting the Buddha's name, but instead educate them in a pagan way. There are also people who do not understand or misunderstand Pure Land, so they create negative comments. Roughly saying: - Pure Land is the practice of old men and women, people with low base - practicing Pure Land is relying on weakness, unable to self-liberate, must rely on the power of others - or reciting Buddha is a corrupt dharma waiting for death, only saving death but not birth. The above abuses and misunderstandings have the potential to lead the masses to evil paths and to change and destroy the faith of those who recite Buddha's name, so it is necessary to explain to clarify the Pure Land dharma. Please ignore those who do not believe in cause and effect, Buddha Dharma, but only consider those who are formally involved with Buddhism.

• There are people who are formally monks and nuns, and also live in temples or hermitages, but do not learn to understand Buddha's teachings, only practice according to the teachings. They are people who carry the guise of Buddhism and sell pagan groceries. These people have their disciples and secretly preach to each other. Many people, although they say they practice meditation, actually specialize in practicing meditation and do not understand what meditation is at all. For the Pure Land practice, they say you have to recite the Buddha's mantra from the simple field straight out the back, go up along the spine and then circle back down to the simple field, called turning the wheel of dharma. That is the way to practice opening the two channels of Nham and Doc, according to foreign sects, not of Buddhism. Some people teach you to hold your breath and recite Buddha's name in one breath, then swallow your saliva, called to strengthen your true essence. Some people spread the six words Namo Amitabha Buddha all over their body. Some people explain the Amitabha Sutra according to external theories such as: The seven-jeweled lotus pond is the stomach, the seven rows of precious trees are the ribs, the water merit bowl is the blood, marrow, and impure water in the body... Those who borrowed Buddha's teachings to practice this heretical religion are not true believers. How can they achieve rebirth liberation?

• Besides the pagans who rely on Buddha's teachings, the rest are the official disciples of Buddha. Here, there are many people who believe and understand Buddha's Recitation method and acknowledge Buddha's teachings on this subject, but Pure Land is not their favorite practice, so they practice other subjects. These people are all true practitioners of Buddha Dharma. However, there are also a few people who, because they follow the teachings of other sects, do not deeply understand Pure Land, and because of sectarian ideology, not only do they not believe in Pure Land Sect, but they also have the heart to slander.

For example, there are people who follow Zen school and have not been studying meditation for long, and are opposed to reciting Buddha's name. They do not know that many great virtuous monks in the past were like them: Vinh Minh meditation master, Tu Tam Tan meditation master, Thien Y Hoai meditation master, Vien Chieu Ban meditation master, Tu Tho Tham meditation master, Nam Nhac Tu meditation master, Phap Chieu meditation master, Tinh Tinh meditation master, Tinh Tu Dai Thong meditation master, Thien Thai Hoai Ngoc meditation master, Dao Tran meditation master, Dao Xuoc meditation master, Pi Lang Phap Chan meditation master, Co To Thu Na meditation master, Bac Nhan Gian meditation master, Thien Muc Le meditation master etc... are those who have transcended the Zen school and, after realizing the enlightenment of the mind and enlightenment, all return to Pure Land. For meditation, these people are great intellectuals propagating sects. For Tinh, they are famous and virtuous people who advise and recite the Buddha's name. This can prove that Pure Land and meditation are not obstacles to each other, so why do we have to slander them? Like a monk who recently passed away, monk Hu Van, everyone recognizes him as a super enlightened person; But when he was at the Meditation Hall, he taught about the ethics of meditation. At the Buddha Recitation Hall, he taught about Buddha recitation. With Pure Land, he not only did not object but also praised it. So let's ask those who have just started practicing meditation and quickly reject Buddha's name, are their learning, understanding and diligent practice as good as the noble ones above?

Again, like the followers of Duy Thuc Tong, who had just learned Duy Thuc not long ago, they objected to the Buddha's recitation. They did not know that the first Patriarch who enlightened the Only Thuc Thuc School in China was Mr. Xuanzang, whom they are currently studying, did not object, and even propagated the Buddha's recitation. The evidence is that when he returned from India to request sutras, he brought with him the Amitabha Sutra in Sanskrit, translated into a new version, titled Praise the Pure Land Sutra. Even the second Patriarch of the Duy Thuc School, Master Khuy Co, also composed one volume of Amitabha Sutra, and three volumes of Amitabha Sutra of Dispersion. And Master Tai Hu, a modern monk in China, everyone recognized him as a master of renaissance in Only-Thuc Tong. But when a Pure Land practitioner asked the great master to teach, he also preached about reciting the Buddha's name. His teachings about Pure Land Buddhism have seven chapters, which are currently in circulation at Thien Dao Pagoda in Taipei. Then we know that the virtuous people of Duy Thuc Tong not only did not refute Pure Land, but on the contrary, they also propagated and praised it. I would like to ask those who have studied Only Thuc for a long time and have opposed Pure Land, is their religious education as good as that of their predecessors?

The first step into Pure Land requires accurate understanding. Without faith, how can you make vows and practice? As above, we can see that there are generally three types of people who cause damage to the Pure Land doctrine. One is that worldly people do not believe in cause and effect, Buddha's teachings, so they should slander Buddha's name. Second, those who practice according to the open method abuse the form of Buddha Dharma and only teach Buddha recitation in the wrong way. Third, those in the Dharma, their awareness of Pure Land is still shallow and simple, so they look down on it and slander it. Those who recite Buddha's name need to know about these censorious things and identify what is evil, true, and false, in order to maintain confidence on the path of practice.

---o0o---

Section B. Explanation of Doubts

tieu_de: Section 17 - Common Doubts About Pure Land
tom_tat: The above things of disbelief, abuse and lack of awareness also belong to the aspect of standing on the outside looking in at Pure Land's door. Here we would like to mention those who truly want to practice, or have already initiated the practice. There are many people who sincerely want to…
noi_dung:
Section 17 - Common Doubts About Pure Land

The above things of disbelief, abuse and lack of awareness also belong to the aspect of standing on the outside looking in at Pure Land's door. Here we would like to mention those who truly want to practice, or have already initiated the practice. There are many people who sincerely want to recite Buddha's name, or have already practiced it, but because their understanding of the teachings is still poor, when they hear others argue and refute it, they immediately become suspicious. These doubts are many, now I will only point out three common points that many people often encounter. These points are roughly as follows: Thinking that Ultimate Bliss is a right theory, practicing Dharma is too easy to attain, suspecting that one is not blessed with blessings, it is difficult to rebirth. Please explain briefly as follows:

• 1- Someone saw in the scriptures that the scene of Pure Land was too solemn, and suddenly had doubts: - The realm of Ultimate Bliss is the Buddha's right to help people strive to do good and avoid evil, similar to the theory of heaven, hell or Penglai, to reward good and punish evil of other sects. How can there be a world made of land, trees, and buildings made of seven treasures like: gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, mother-of-pearl, red pearl, and agate? What about a human body made of pure jade and diamond, born from a lotus flower without aging, sickness or death, and all precious food and clothing appearing at the discretion of the mind? These are all stories that are out of place, far from the reality that is visible before our eyes, how can we believe it?

- To explain this, please answer:

- Those thoughts are still limited to what mortal eyes and ears can hear. People who want to study Buddha should not use ordinary wisdom to contemplate holy scenes. Don't go too far, right in Vietnam, when Mr. Phan Thanh Gian came back from an embassy to France, he said that over there the lights did not light but burned, and the carts and boats did not have horses to pull swimmers but ran on their own. He has two verses:

Ba Ban cunningly plans to bring together heaven and earth.

Only the power of birth and death to create and create!

These two sentences imply praising the French for hundreds of excellent deeds comparable to heaven and earth, only life and death are still under the creator's power to decide! When King Tu Duc and his court heard that, they did not believe it. Even Mr. Nguyen Tri Phuong, who is a close friend, also smiled and thought that Mr. Phan was talking nonsense after going away. Try asking: - King Tu Duc and his court all considered themselves to be educated people, so they did not believe that this incident was beyond their imagination. But do these things really not exist? Taking this small matter into account, we see that if we use prejudices based on what we hear and see and ordinary thinking to measure the holy scene, it will be wrong. Furthermore, if there was no Amitabha Buddha to guide them, why would many people recite Buddha's name when they were about to die, knowing the time and date in advance, seeing Western scenes, and Buddha and Bodhisattva appearing in person to welcome them? If the realm of Ultimate Bliss is illusory, why are there Pure Land practitioners who, at the present time, suddenly had a clear vision of the solemn Western scene just as the Buddha said? Disciples of Buddha or people who want to study Buddha but do not take Buddha's teachings in the sutras as a guideline, what else can they use as a refuge? Therefore, according to the Divine Word and Manifestation (a way of thinking based on Buddha's words and the practitioner's manifestations), we must believe that the solemnities in Ultimate Bliss are real.

• 2- Some people have heard that the Pure Land dharma practice is simple but achieves very quick and sublime results, then they suspect that: - Where is there such an easy way to become a Buddha? Because the common path of practitioners is Samadhi and Contemplation. When performing hands-on effort, first practice Chi, then Contemplation; or before practicing Contemplation, next practice. Gradually progress to "in Quan there is Chi, in Chi there is Quan." When you reach the level of "Contemplation without two, concentration and wisdom pass away" This is called entering the realm of self-consciousness. From then on, if you continue to practice diligently in every life, as the scriptures say, you will have to go through thousands of great kalpas to reach the throne of Unreturning. Why is it that just by reciting a Buddha's name, in this life, you can be reborn to the throne of Non-Return? Isn't it too easy?

Referring to this question, we should know that practicing other methods depends entirely on self-reliance, so it is difficult. The Pure Land path alone has two powers, the power of the mind and the power of the Buddha, so success is very easy. For example, for a person with weak legs, wanting to reach the top of a high mountain by himself is very difficult. But if that person is led forward by a great athlete holding his arm, then the result of being promoted will not be difficult! The same goes for Pure Land, when we concentrate on reciting Buddha, that is when our mental power develops. Reciting with one mind without chaos is when the mind's power is completely revealed. At that time, the force of karma was subdued and was no longer an obstacle. It was further guided by Buddha's force, so although karma was not completely eliminated, it was reborn. After being born in the West, living for an immeasurable and boundless number of kalpas, the irreversibility until becoming a Buddha is obvious and easy to understand.

• 3- Some people suspect that: The scene of Ultimate Bliss is immeasurably beautiful and dignified, and it does not require a few good causes and conditions to be born, merits and blessings. Looking back at myself, my good roots, merits and blessings are still small, my karma is too much, how can I hope that this life will have a good fate for rebirth?

- I respectfully advise you thousands of times not to doubt like that. Because when you recite the Buddha's rosary, your good roots of merits and blessings are already deep. Think about it, how many people in this world have not heard the name Buddha? How many people, although they have heard the great name of Amitabha, are always trying to gain fame and fortune, chasing after defilements, and refusing to recite the Buddha's name? Now that you have heard the Buddha's teachings and are reciting the Buddha's thoughts, don't you have great merits and blessings? In the Infinite Life Sutra, Buddha told Maitreya Bodhisattva: "If there is any sentient being who hears the Buddha's name and is filled with joy for even a single thought, one should know that he or she will receive great benefits and be filled with unsurpassed merits and blessings." This statement is enough to prove: Knowing Buddha's name means you already have many merits and blessings with good roots. In Pure Land Thanh Hien Luc, there is a story about people who committed extremely evil crimes such as Truong Thien Hoa, Hung Tuan, Duy Cung and animals such as Bat Kha birds, martial arts heroes, and Buddha's thoughts were all reborn. Your merits and blessings have surpassed those of evil people and animals. So there is no need to be afraid that in this life you will not be born into Ultimate Bliss!

---o0o---

tom_tat: In addition to the three common doubts as above, there are also doubts about Pure Land that affect morality from shallow to deep. These doubts are many, now I will only point out the important details to explain, in a question and answer style like...
noi_dung:
Section 18 - Reasonable Doubts

In addition to the three common doubts as above, there are also doubts about Pure Land that affect morality from shallow to deep. These doubts are many, now I would like to point out only the important details to explain, in a question and answer style as follows:

1) Ask: Pure Land is a basic dharma, only for ignorant people with low intelligence to practice. People with high instincts must practice meditation or Consciousness Only to make sense. Furthermore, a man must have the will to be strong and independent, so he must rely on his own strength for liberation; If you pray for strength, wouldn't you appear weak?

- Answer: With this question, first let's talk about the foundation, then answer the factor of self-reliance and forgiveness.

• The Pure Land method is not only for the middle and lower levels, but also captures the upper and upper levels. The middle and lower level people who recite the Buddha's name will end their afflictions and karma, generate blessings and wisdom, and gradually reach a state of concentration. Depending on their efforts, low and high, they will be reborn in the nine-level lotus of Ultimate Bliss. As soon as a person of superior ability starts reciting the Buddha's name, he immediately penetrates into the realm of concentration and wisdom, walking, standing, lying, and sitting all in the Samadhi of Buddha's Recitation, and when he dies, he is reborn in the highest level in the Federation. Among the immortals, there was someone who entered this realm, and reported with the sentence:

Nirvana arises in the book of continents and ends

Sanskrit incense is multi-timeless

Italy says:

Grasping the rosary and reciting it,

Suddenly he became Buddha a long time ago.

Therefore, the recitation of Buddha captures all three senses, for tall people it becomes high, for short people it becomes low.

Great intellectuals in Buddhism often comment: "Buddha's Recitation Dharma includes meditation, Teachings, Vinaya, and Secrets." Why does Buddha's Recitation method include all four subjects? - The reason for this is because when reciting Buddha stops all false thoughts and attachments, that is meditation. The six red words include countless meanings, countless meanings, all hidden and appearing from there, that is the Church. Reciting Buddha to a deep realm, the three karma are all pure and quiet, that is the Law. Buddha's recitation has the function of a mantra, or to clear injustice, to eliminate karma, to be satisfied, to destroy demons, which is Secret. Like Master Lien Tri, in a year of long drought, instead of reciting the martial arts mantra, he just went out in the fields to knock on Buddha's musk. Wherever he went, it rained. And Vien Chieu Ban meditation master, instead of participating in meditation, he only used the six words of the red name to realize his original nature and enter the Samadhi of Buddha Recitation. Just like this, to expand and deepen the experience, the Buddha's recitation also includes all five periods and eight teachings, including the six Paramita dharmas, as presented by Great Master Triet Ngo in the Hundred Verses of Buddha's Recitation.

In the sutra it says: "If you sincerely recite the name Amitabha Buddha, you will be freed from serious sins for eighty billions of births and deaths." If a person recites Buddha's name, if they keep their mind focused, they will certainly develop wisdom similar to the practice of other dharmas. Furthermore, if one recites the name Amitabha Buddha on concentration, then the elimination of karma obstacles and the birth of blessings and wisdom become higher and faster. Therefore, Master Lien Tri praised the Buddha's Recitation method as: great meditation, great wisdom, great merits and blessings, great sages. According to Quan Kinh: When a person commits the five or ten evil crimes, when they are about to die, the appearance of hell appears. If they sincerely recite the name Amitabha Buddha for ten recitations, he will immediately appear and lead them to Ultimate Bliss. From being an extremely evil person, using only ten thoughts to be reborn and immediately ascend to the throne of Unreturning is truly a very rare thing. „n Master Quang praised: "The extremely high Buddha's Recitation Dharma can be recited until one's mind is not disturbed, attaining Samadhi, the extremely low person can only use ten recitations successfully, it is a unique point that no other method has seen."

• Regarding the issue of self-reliance on the power of others, if you understand that the Pure Land practice only relies entirely on the power of others, you are mistaken. People who recite Buddha's name must use all their strength to eliminate afflictions and recite until the realm of their mind and the corresponding Buddha's mind. From that realm, the practitioner is now secretly receiving light from the Buddha, and when he dies, he will receive rebirth. The guidance is the main factor of other powers, because the world of Ultimate Bliss is ten thousand billion Buddha degrees far away from this Saha world, not even ordinary supernatural powers can reach it, let alone ordinary people! Therefore, it is necessary to rely on the power of others, the divine power of the Buddha or the saints, to guide us. For example, as a student, knowing how to try your best to study is of course something valuable. If, based on that specialization, you are taught by a good professor, your level of education will certainly be more profound, and passing the exam will be guaranteed. On top of the practitioner's own power, the same is true of the Buddha family's other power. So the fact that we ourselves have tried our best to practice, and yet pray for more power from others to get quick results, is it a weak mistake? The greatness of Pure Land, the Bodhisattva greats such as Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Ma Minh, Nagarjuna; Patriarchs such as Vinh Minh, Tri Gia, Triet Ngo, Lien Tri, and many other sects, all recommended rebirth. Criticizing the Buddha's Remembrance as inferior only for people of low ability to practice means criticizing the Bodhisattva, the Patriarchs and the noble ones mentioned above. Saying that Buddha is weak, only relying on other people's power, means not knowing anything about Pure Land.

2) Ask: An ancient poem has a saying:

The body is lightly trained to attain the bronze fairy crane

Ultimate Bliss is at its best.

Italy says:

Train your body lightly to get the same fairy crane,

Ultimate Bliss flies straight back!

Then we just keep practicing meditation, waiting until we attain supernatural powers, then we can go to Ultimate Bliss, or at will go to other Pure Land realms. So, why do we have to recite Buddha's name to pray for Ultimate Bliss?

- Answer: The above two verses mean that the realm of sympathy from the practitioner blends with the Buddha's divine power, not just the realm of supernatural powers. Please explain these two things in turn, first let's talk about the realm of supernatural powers.

• According to the sutras, the eyes and supernatural powers of the first level of Sotapanna belong to the scope of a small world, including four realms of evil beasts, four great continents, a Mount Meru, a sun and moon, six heavens of Desire, and a realm of initial meditation. The eyes and supernatural powers of the second level of Si Da Ham are within a small world; A Na Ham level, a middle world; Arhat, a great world. Bodhisattva, the first level of the path, sees one hundred Buddha realms and hundreds of Buddhas, attains one hundred Samadhi; Divine power can release light and vibrate one hundred Buddha realms, reaching all one hundred Buddha realms. The enlightenment and supernatural powers of the Second Bodhisattva level are within the circumference of a thousand Buddha realms; Bodhisattva Three Grounds, one hundred thousand Buddha realms. Just like that, it gradually increases until it reaches the tenth Bodhisattva level, belonging to the Dharma Cloud level, with supernatural powers, covering boundless realms. From this Saha world to Ultimate Bliss is ten thousand billion Buddha degrees. The number of billions in India in ancient times had three levels, but the average is one million now. Thus, if one takes ten thousand times one million (100,000 x 1,000,000), then Saha is one hundred thousand million Buddha degrees away from Ultimate Bliss. Regarding the Buddha land, which is the scope of a Buddha's transformational incarnation, there is the Buddha who takes a great world consisting of a thousand million solar systems as a Buddha land; There are Buddhas who take two, three or hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, millions of great thousand realms as one Buddha realm; There are Buddhas who take from one galaxy to many thousands of great thousands of worlds to make a Buddha realm. 'Not to mention the gaps between this Buddha level and that Buddha level. Thus we see that from Saha to Ultimate Bliss, not only the Arhats, but also the supernatural powers of the lower Bodhisattva beings are also difficult to find. Therefore, in the past, Maudgalyayana appeared in the Arhat throne, but in reality, Bodhisattva appeared as Sravaka to practice Bodhisattva conduct. He heard the Buddha speak the Amitabha Sutra, and at one point used his supernatural powers to seek Ultimate Bliss. But he couldn't find it, and finally got lost in the world of Buddha Tu Di General. Mount Meru is eighty-four thousand yojanas high, each yojana is on average sixty miles. Buddha Meru and the people in that world are as big as Mount Meru. When Maudgalyayana came to this world, he saw Buddha preaching to the crowd, so he walked around on the mouth of a monk's bowl. That monk told Buddha: There was a small, human-shaped worm crawling on the rim of my bowl. Buddha Tu Di General said: "That's not true, that's Sravaka, the most supernatural disciple of Shakyamuni Buddha in the Saha world, named Maudgalyayana." When Maudgalyayana heard this, he immediately appeared in a body as big as Mount Meru, equal to the body of the sentient beings in that realm, told Buddha the reason he had strayed to this world, and respectfully asked Buddha to use his divine power to bring him back to Saha land. Thus, we see that if it is based on divine power, the divine power is not vast and cannot reach Ultimate Bliss.

- In this time of the end of the Dharma, enlightenment is still rare for those who engage in meditation, let alone attain the Complete Sotapanna! When you have not yet attained the fruition, you must suffer samsara, and freedom from depravity is not guaranteed. Is it a fantasy to continue to practice each life through countless lives, waiting to attain the throne of Bodhisattva to be able to reach Ultimate Bliss? Even if you have enough supernatural powers to reach Ultimate Bliss, if you want to stay in that realm, you must respectfully recite the name of Amitabha to be able to stay. For example, there is a rich house with a beautiful flower garden. We can overcome the wall and enter it, but if we really want to go there and enjoy it, we have to ask the owner. Therefore, in the past, Vimalakirti used his supernatural powers to bring the beautiful and solemn seats of forty-two thousand yojanas high in Buddha Tu Di Dang Vuong's land to a pure place. Only the great Bodhisattvas who had once paid homage to making offerings to all Buddhas of the ten directions could sit up and sit. In addition, those who have recently developed the Bodhisattva idea up to the rank of Sravaka's great disciples, although they have supernatural powers exceeding forty-two thousand yojanas, cannot sit up. Venerable Vimalakirti knew that these lion thrones were due to the merit blessings reported by King Tu Di Dang Tathagata, so he immediately told them to pay homage to the Buddha, and then they could sit. So you know, if you want to return to the Western world of Ultimate Bliss, chanting Amitabha Buddha is a necessity.

• What is the state of self-consciousness that sympathizes with Buddha's divine power? Kinh says: "Amitabha Buddha often radiates light to receive all sentient beings reciting Buddha's name in the ten directions without missing it." Therefore, when we recite the Buddha's name, we immediately receive the Buddha's luminous vow power and silently accept it. When the practitioner single-mindedly recites the Buddha's thoughts, the karma power sinks, the mind power is revealed, the light of the mind communicates with the light of the Buddha, so now one can see the Western scene, or the gods roaming the Pure Land. The power of a practitioner's pure wish towards the West is called self-power, or self-power; Amitabha Buddha's power to radiate light to receive extradition is called the Buddha's receiving power, or other power. Thanks to those two powers, even though they do not yet have great supernatural powers, practitioners reciting the Buddha's name can be born in the West. When dying, the person recites Buddha depending on his merit, or sees Buddha coming to guide him, or sees Bodhisattva or the Holy Assembly coming to guide him. Although there was a person who could not see anything, due to the power of his vow and the guiding light of the Buddha, he was also reborn. Such is the importance of other power.

3) Ask: Pure Land practitioners need to attain Buddha Recitation Samadhi, or at least reach the realm of one-pointedness and undisturbed mind, to be reborn. So people of low ability may not be able to practice. So how can a lowly, stupid person be born into Ultimate Bliss? If a person with a lower base is stupid and cannot be reborn, why is it called the Buddha's Recitation method that captures all three senses?

- Answer: In fact, with today's capabilities, the realm of single-mindedness and undisturbedness at the present time, not many people have reached it, let alone the Buddha Samadhi! But, according to the Infinite Life Sutra, when the person who commits the five crimes against the ten evils appears at the end of his life, the appearance of hell appears, he wholeheartedly recites the name Amitabha Buddha from one to ten recitations, and immediately the Buddha appears to lead him to rebirth. So the rebirth of single-mindedness is only for the moment of death, not the present moment. If in normal times you recite Buddha's name and achieve single-mindedness, but then you change your mind to practice another method without praying for rebirth, how can you return to Ultimate Bliss? If you want to have one mind at the time of death, you must practice reciting the Buddha's words skillfully during normal times. Due to the normal practice of reciting Buddha, even though he has not yet achieved one-pointedness of mind, the seeds of reciting Buddha's recitation have accumulated many. When he is about to die, when the practitioner starts reciting Buddha's thoughts, he immediately discovers that he is strong and has one-pointedness of mind. Those who lower the Buddha's consciousness are reborn, often in that state.

4) Ask: Reciting Buddha's name is to eliminate delusions, stop afflictions, and reach a place of thoughtlessness. If that's the case, just keep your mind pure and gradually enter the realm of no-thoughts. Why do you need to recite Buddha's name to exhaust yourself?

- Answer: The ultimate point of the Buddha Recitation method is the Buddha Recitation Samadhi, witnessing the entire nature of Amitabha, which is the realm of Everlasting Light Pure Land. But the main and urgent purpose of the Pure Land sect is to pray for rebirth to ensure no more deluded samsara, to borrow the superior circumstances in the realm of Ultimate Bliss to practice, to quickly advance to Buddhahood. For that reason, Pure Land practitioners need to recite the name of Amitabha. The purpose of the Pure Land discipline is like that, there is no need to seek a realm without thoughts and quickly realize one's original nature like the Zen school.

However, when actually practicing this intention, the practitioner must recite Buddha's name to achieve one-pointedness of mind, so even though he does not pray for thoughtlessness, the scene of thoughtlessness still manifests itself. Furthermore, thanks to the merit of reciting Buddha's help to quickly eliminate karma, that realm is revealed even more quickly. — here we see another ray of light: If you want to quickly become thoughtless and soon realize your original nature, you need to recite Buddha's name.

Going deeper, if you are a person of Mahayana nature, you must understand that reciting the Buddha's name is to become Buddha. If we only understand that reciting Buddha's name is to prevent false thoughts, that means we have strayed into the Five Dinh Mind Contemplation of the Hinayana. Why is reciting Buddha to become Buddha? - Because as soon as the sentence of reciting Buddha is started, the past, present, and future are all lost. Even though there is a form, it is separate from the form, that is, form is empty, with thoughts and without thoughts, immediately entering the Tathagata's realm of self-consciousness without thoughts, can be Buddha, what else? If we think that having thoughts means remaining stagnant in the conditioned place, then when the World-Honored One manifests the conditioned signs such as eating, wearing robes, talking, preaching, walking, standing, lying, and sitting, all of them are stagnant in the conditioned place and is he not the Tathagata? Furthermore, if you think that reciting the Buddha is not yet thoughtless, then the Zen school's venerable monks, when giving talks, giving lectures, or sometimes chanting sutras, worshiping, repentance, and walking, all belong to physical appearance, not meditation? You should know that the principle of non-action is "to do all the actions without seeing the appearance of doing it", the same is true of non-thought; Not all actions and words are thoughtless! Because they do not understand this reason, many people disagree and think: Reciting the Buddha's name is like a cart carrying a heavier load, or like gold mixed with lead, rice mixed with sand, not light and pure, it's really wrong!

But reciting without reciting is the realm of a superior person; Here we just briefly discuss it to resolve doubts. For middle and lower level people, trying to recite Buddha's name proficiently is already very valuable!

5) Ask: The essence of all dharmas is emptiness, they have always been unborn and are equal and quiet. When our mind is pure, even in the Impure Land it will be pure; On the contrary, it seems impure, even though it is in Pure Land, it is still bustling with troubles. If there is birth, there must be death, or if there is birth, there is death. So is it not moral to leave Samadhi to seek rebirth in Ultimate Bliss?

- Answer: This problem has two meanings. Please follow the words of Great Master Tri Gia in the Ten Nghi Treatises and add a few comments to explain, divided into a general answer and a special answer.

As for the general answer, if you think that the desire to return to Pure Land is to leave here and look for another, it is not consistent with the principle of equality. Then if the Samadhi abiding does not seek to be born in Ultimate Bliss, is it not a mistake to abandon that attachment? As for saying: "I don't ask for that and I don't accept this", also making the mistake of annihilation. Therefore, the Diamond Prajna Sutra says: "Tu Bodhi! Don't think: It is said that generating the unsurpassed mind of Bodhi is to destroy all appearances of all dharmas. Why? Because of developing the mind of unsurpassed Bodhi, regarding all dharmas, there is no mention of cessation."

Regarding the special response, please explain the principle of non-birth and purity of mind.

No birth is also the principle of no birth and no death. Unborn are dharmas that are born of false causes and conditions, have no self-entity, and therefore do not truly have the appearance of being born. Because it is illusory and does not arise from somewhere real, it is called unborn. Immortality is when all dharmas perish, and do not have a self-nature, nor do we say that we perish. Because it has no real place to return or end, it is called immortal. Therefore, the principle of non-birth or non-birth and death does not exist "outside the dharmas of birth and death." Therefore, not wishing to be born in the Pure Land is called no-birth, or being born in Ultimate Bliss means there is death and destruction, contrary to the principle of no-birth! That's the argument in terms of logic, specifically in terms of things, people born in Pure Land will surely ascend to the throne without turning back, living for an immeasurable and boundless number of kalpas. During that time, his practice attained the fruit of non-birth. So there's no problem: There is birth and death, or there is birth and death, but be careful!

The same goes for a pure mind, using a pure mind in Saha to practice the path, and with a pure mind in Ultimate Bliss to practice, what is there to be afraid of? The Duy Ma Sutra says: "Even though I know the Buddha realms, along with sentient beings, I often practice Pure Land to educate and transform living beings." Therefore, although wise people diligently recite the Buddha's name to pray for birth in the Pure Land, they do not accept the appearance of birth, because it does not really exist; Even though we clearly know that the dharmas have always been pure and quiet, we have no qualms about seeking rebirth in the West, using the predestined conditions to practice and advance in order to educate and transform sentient beings. This is the true meaning of no birth, and also the true meaning of pure mind depending on purity. On the contrary, people with poor understanding are bound by the appearance of birth. When they hear about birth, they immediately think that there really is birth and death; I heard that there is no birth but I accept that I am not born anywhere. They do not know that birth is non-birth, and no reason for non-birth to hinder birth; If you have a calm mind, why bother asking for Ultimate Bliss? Because they do not understand that reason, they are filled with quarrels and gossip, and despise those who seek to be born in the Pure Land. How misguided they are!

---o0o---

tieu_de: Section 19 - Doubts Based on the Sutras
tom_tat: In addition to the above, there are many people who study Buddhism, based on world sutra text theories, and raise questions about Pure Land. By the way, please continue with the question and answer session to resolve doubts
noi_dung:
Section 19 - Doubts Based on the Sutras

In addition to the above, there are many people who study Buddhism, based on world sutra text theories, and raise questions about Pure Land. By the way, please continue with the question and answer session to resolve those doubts.

1) Ask: Diamond Sutra says: "All dharmas are conditioned, like dreams, illusions, shadows, and bubbles." Then the Saha world is illusory, and the realm of Ultimate Bliss is also illusory. Why don't you go straight to the true mind, why are you still asking for an illusory scene?

- Answer: In fact, the Impure Lands and Pure Lands in the ten directions all seem like a dream; But when one attains the Illusory Samadhi, one will see that it is false. If you haven't been like that, you still see it as real, are still influenced by it, still know suffering and joy, in the dry season you still feel uncomfortable about the heat, even the very small things like an ant or mosquito bite still cause pain. So why is it called an illusion? You should know that the Pure Land discipline is the Buddha's miraculous means, borrowing the illusory, happy scene to bring sentient beings out of the illusory, painful situation full of obstacles and dangers. Then, from that illusory state of happiness and joy, one can easily progress in practice, to quickly attain the realm of the true mind and everlasting peace.

To take an example, in this Saha world, the scene of a family or a noisy town is illusory, the scene of a pagoda or a deserted mountain place is also an illusion. But why do people who practice liberation leave their family life in the city to find a quiet temple in the mountains? Is it true that in a place with a busy family and noisy scenes, it is difficult to calm the mind, but in a temple or in a quiet mountain place, it is easy to practice? Therefore, the world of ordinary people and the world of saintly attainment are different. For ordinary people to put themselves in the world of saintly attainment, it is far away from reality. As for ordinary people, let's follow the fate of ordinary people and gradually progress in cultivation. Don't be too quick to look too high with the holy eyes, which will become false and harmful words.

In the past, there was also a meditation practitioner who believed that the realm of Ultimate Bliss was an illusion and that reciting the Buddha's name to pray for rebirth was useless. Master Triet Ngo heard this and immediately said: "It's not like that! From the Seventh Level Bodhisattva onwards, all practiced in dreams. As for the great dream of ignorance, the Fully Enlightened One is still asleep. Only all Buddhas can be honored as Great Enlightenment, those who are completely awakened. When you yourself are in a dream, happiness and suffering are still illusory, joy also feels happy, suffering also knows suffering, how can you call yourself a waking dreamer, the scene is an illusory dream? Then instead of being in the miserable dream of Saha, how about the happy dream of Ultimate Bliss! What's more, the dream in Saha is from dream to dream, attracted by karma's fate, forever living samsara and drowning in delusion. As for the dream scene in Ultimate Bliss, from dream to enlightenment, one will fully awaken and attain Buddhahood. Therefore, the illusory dream is still the same, but the conditions of the dream scene in the two real places are not the same. Then isn't it necessary to recite Buddha's name to pray for rebirth?

The ancient teachings explain it like that, then the quest for birth is clear. However, the verse in the Diamond Sutra mentioned that is still a means for sentient beings to leave the concept of attachment to ordinary life. Taking it a step further, as the Great Prajnaparamita Sutra says: "The Tathagata, because of the dark nature of people, speaks of dharmas as illusory and quiet, lest they give rise to wrong views; Because of those who have a bright nature, they speak of the good appearance of all Buddhas, because they are like lotus flowers, untainted by the world." Therefore, Tu Bodhi is the first to understand the principles of emptiness, with absolutely no famous appearance, but the World-Honored One predicted that he would later become a Buddha, named Famous General Tathagata. Then the wonderful principle has no name or form but is beyond name and form. All illusory dream dharmas are the Buddha's true dharma. And going deep to the point of perfection, as the Sixth Patriarch said, ordinary people are originally Buddha, afflictions are Bodhi, all ignorance and illusion are the true enlightenment of the Tathagata Treasury.

2) Ask: The Dharma Jewel Platform Sutra says: "Not reciting, reciting is right. There are thoughts, thoughts become evil." So, is reciting Buddha an evil illusion?

- Answer: Regarding the principle of no-birth, no-thought, the previous paragraph has talked about it. Here, I would like to answer frankly: - Isn't not reciting Buddha, not chanting sutras, called non-thought? Constantly reciting the Buddha chanting sutras, but the mind is empty, not realizing that there is any chanting, that is called non-thought. On the contrary, even though you sit quietly without thinking about anything, you still feel aware of yourself, there is sitting meditation, which is still called "having mindfulness". If you think "not thinking" is without reciting the Buddha, chanting sutras, preaching the Dharma, without thinking, then it becomes wood and stone; Wanting to avoid the error of clinging to existence, instead getting lost in the error of clinging to emptiness. That is contrary to the sutra's teachings. That's why the Sixth Patriarch continued: "Yes, No are both unbelievable. I can sit on a white cow far away." A noble person in Pure Land in the past, although constantly reciting Buddha to pray for rebirth, did not accept the form of reciting Buddha to pray for rebirth, so he wrote a verse:

There are thoughts and there are no thoughts,

Not being born means being born,

Don't bother moving half a step.

Come to Giac king citadel

But, the above is talking about the recitative style of a person of superior ability. For those with middle and lower capacities, you should try to recite the Buddha's name as much as possible, even if you still believe that if you have the thoughts and earnestly seek rebirth, that is also a good thing. Because if it is like that, when the end comes, we will be reborn to the West, then we will finally attain the realm of no thought and no birth, there is nothing to worry about! Otherwise, if you don't use your own strength and desire to be high, if you are attached to the above sutra text, you will not be able to do it with the thoughtless morality. With the sight of reciting the Buddha's name, if you seek rebirth, you will not want to practice it. In the end, both will fail, and you will still be just an ordinary person in the cycle of samsara suffering!

- Ask: In the Dharma Jewel Platform Sutra, the Sixth Patriarch said: "People from the East commit crimes, chanting Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the West. When Westerners commit crimes, they recite the Buddha's name and pray to be reborn in which world? So, the only way to eliminate sins is to recite Buddha's name to pray for rebirth?

- Answer: The Sixth Patriarch and the noble men of the Zen school stand in the position of propagating the doctrine of idealism, so every word must be based on their own law, point directly to the nature, and take the mind as the main rule. What He means is: If the mind is pure, then even in Saha, there is freedom; liberation; Even if the mind is not pure in the West, it still suffers from samsara. In fact, for Pure Land practitioners who understand the principles, the Patriarch's words only have the effect of encouraging progress, telling them to recite Buddha's name to a place where their mind is no longer attached to appearances; Not to refute the practice of reciting the Buddha's name to pray for rebirth. Venerable Thich Ton, all Buddhas in the ten directions, Great Bodhisattvas and Patriarchs all advise reciting the Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the West. The two Patriarchs of the Zen school in Thien Truc, Ma Minh and Nagarjuna, both advised reciting Buddha; and Nagarjuna himself attained the First Stage of Joy, rebirth to Ultimate Bliss. If the Sixth Patriarch really intended to refute Buddha's Recitation, wouldn't it turn out to be refuting Shakyamuni Buddha, all Buddhas, Bodhisattva, Patriarchs, and the two predecessors of his sect, Ma Minh and Nagarjuna? Therefore, if you misunderstand and then use these words to disparage Buddha's concept, it is to criticize and sow injustice against the Sixth Patriarch.

Again, every practice has its reasons and reasons. The words of the Sixth Patriarch are about reason, in addition there is also the general appearance of the path, which needs to be thought about. Let's try to ask the question again: "People who commit crimes in real life go to temples to shave their hair and fast, observe the precepts and find a quiet place to practice. Where can people who commit crimes at temples find a place to practice?" If you only follow your theory, then leaving the home life to go to a temple, fasting, observing the precepts, chanting sutras, reciting Buddha, reciting mantras, participating in meditation, are all mistakes? Pure Land practice is the same. In fact, Eastern people do not recite Buddha's name to seek rebirth in the West because they commit sins. Instead, when they recite Buddha's name and seek rebirth in the West, they want to borrow the predestined conditions to practice and quickly attain the fruit of Infernal liberation. Even if a person has committed many sins and knows how to repentance and recite Buddha's name to pray for rebirth, it is also because he wants to escape birth and death as soon as possible, still not outside of this purpose. As for people in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, they also do not commit crimes, because when they return to that realm, above there is Buddha Bodhisattva, below there are noble men and women, surrounded by the sounds of birds speaking the Dharma, the sound of music preaching sutras, and no longer having to worry about food, clothing, housing, illnesses, accidents, and hatred, the path only progresses, where is there any reason to commit crimes?

In conclusion, the Sixth Patriarch's saying should be understood as just teaching about pure nature to encourage progress, and should not be mistakenly used to refute things. Those who recite Buddha's words, hearing these words, should try their best to recite until the level of mind is empty, to be in accordance with the Patriarch's intention.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Lesson 20 - Need to Break the Way of Accepting Two Boundaries
tom_tat: There are still many doubts about Pure Land according to the above type. That's because Buddhist students still cling to both sides, unable to harmonize nature, existence, and reason. That's why we use nature to destroy appearances, to refute reason, to take emptiness...
noi_dung:
Lesson 20 - Need to Break the Way of Accepting Two Boundaries

There are still many doubts about Pure Land according to the above type. That's because Buddhist students still cling to both sides, unable to harmonize nature, existence, and reason. That's why we use nature to destroy appearances, to refute reason, to take nothing from yes, and vice versa, to cause disputes and doubts. They do not expect that truth is interrelated, that is, reason is truth, reason is truth. If divided and judged biased, then truth is not truth, reason is not truth; The same goes for nature, existence and emptiness, and other dual dharmas. That's why in the Vimalakirti Sutra we talk about the Non-Two Dharma, that is, the Non-Two Dharma, to destroy that two-sided attachment. Emptiness Two is to fuse everything to enter the essence, not one. This is the true state of idealism. In addition, the separate legislation on whether there is a gate or not a gate is still within the means of righting it.

Kinh says: "Getting rid of conditioned merit is karma. Greed for merit without action is also karma." The ancients also said: "The dharma is illusory, eliminating all karma is not possible. Even though the unconditioned Dharma is true, if you accept it, your wisdom nature will not expand." These words clearly demonstrate that on the path of practice, truth cannot be separated. The Madhyamaka Commentary says: "Because ordinary living beings are stuck in form, the sutras use the principle of emptiness to destroy it. If you just leave the disease of clinging to existence and fall back into the disease of clinging to emptiness, there will be no medicine left to cure it." Because the teachings of Prajna do not sound sublime and mysterious, when intellectuals come to these types of sutras, most often fall into the disease of "talking about reasons", theorizing everything, looking down on those who practice according to appearances, causing the error of arrogance and arrogance. Although their mouths say no, their actions are filled with yes, consistent with the saying:

The mouth speaks a hundred wonderful things.

There is not a single ceiling under the heel!

• In the past, great intellectuals often used the principle of emptiness to eliminate the disease of accepting existence, but the practice of them and the enlightenment of those people with proper qualifications and appropriate opportunities brought benefits. Such as the following story:

There was a meditation monk who practiced very diligently. He did not sleep at night and often sat and did not lie down. But after many years of hard work, the monk still has not attained enlightenment. In the temple, there was a novice monk who came from nowhere and asked to join the group. This man was often lazy and late, even when the bell rang late at night, he still lay down and did not get up. The meditation master found out and called and scolded him: "Why are you still lazy and lie down like that after entering the temple to practice? You didn't hear what the law said: If you hear the bell but still lie down and don't get up, will you fall into the body of a snake in the future?" The novice replied: "The teacher told me that if I lie down often, I will become a snake; As for me, if I sit forever I will become a toad, so I won't be able to realize anything?" After finishing speaking, the novice disappeared. But the meditation master became enlightened. It turned out that this novice monk was an enlightened being, the incarnation who came to enlighten the meditation master.

In addition, there is the story of monk Don Ha Thien Nhien riding on Buddha's neck and burning the wooden Buddha statue to destroy the concept of Buddha's attachment. Master Phap Dat, because he relied on himself, had recited three thousand volumes of the Lotus Sutra, so he bowed with his head without touching the ground, and was scolded by the Sixth Patriarch, to destroy the concept of clinging to the dharma and clinging to merit. After realizing the Great Samadhi of Great Freedom, Mr. Bac Thap wrote the names Manjushri and Samantabhadra on his loincloth to break the notion of clinging to the Holy Sangha.

In ancient times, the great intellectuals had high levels of cultivation and knew how to change the path depending on the opportunity. Furthermore, the practitioners of that time had many superior abilities, so the teaching of the principle of "emptiness" often beneficial. Nowadays there are many middle and lower level people, the way of teaching should be to harmonize reason and nature, so as not to cause doubts and rot the minds of Buddhist students. If the majority of people cannot take a step straight into the vacuum and reject form, it will inevitably turn into an accident of "having to destroy the raft before reaching shore", how can we avoid being immersed? Another thing to keep in mind is that if you say no but you don't get it yet, or don't have any qualms about the practice, it certainly won't be able to influence people, it will just become a useless dispute over victory and defeat. Previously, the author once witnessed that scene: A great monk who understood the teachings lived in a certain temple and taught the sutras. The abbot was old, diligent in chanting but was attached to the old ways. Seeing that the monk's free lifestyle seemed modern, he did not like it, so he said: "If you advise and teach the Dharma, day and night you can't recite a sutra or recite a Buddhist verse, so how can you provide a model for practice to the masses?" The Venerable replied: "There are many ways to practice. You have to follow the same form as the teacher, chanting every day at night. Is that called practice?"

Diamond Sutra says:

Weakness due to identity and ego.

The sound of the bridge falls,

Thi Nhan practices evil ways.

Impossible to see Tathagata!

"The Sixth Patriarch in the past did not chant Buddha's sutras, but he also attained enlightenment and became the Patriarch?" The abbot was weak and had to stay silent. In fact, the abbot was guilty of accepting formality; Although the Venerable spoke highly of the principles, in fact he was not interested in meditation and pure mindfulness, so he could not be alert and caused even more frustration for the monk.

Of the two ways of clinging to existence and non-existence, attachment to emptiness is very dangerous. The Lankavatara Sutra and Mat Nghiem both say: "It's better to accept existence like a Tu mountain, than to accept emptiness like a mustard seed." Accepting yes means always abstaining from cause and effect, fearing blessings, observing the precepts, chanting, doing good, although being constrained by forms cannot liberate oneself, but can create merit and good roots. If you still accept emptiness, you have not yet realized emptiness, and if you do not follow the form and diligently cultivate merit, you will definitely fall into samsara.

The writer examines himself, his karma is too much, his character is weak, he still does not want to discuss the sublime morality too much, for fear that his conduct will not be worthy of his words and will become false talk. But with the sincerity of wanting people to stop doubting and believe in Buddha's thoughts, I had no choice but to reveal more or less. Hang compares herself to a paralyzed person sitting at a three-way intersection. Even though she cannot walk on her own, she still tries to remind passengers to avoid dangerous paths and follow the wide, safe path. As for the argument to distinguish between right and wrong, I absolutely do not think about it!

-ooOoo-
