Section A. Prayer, the Prime Motive of rebirth

tieu_de: Section 21 - The Essential Characteristics of Making Vows
tom_tat: As mentioned above, the core teachings of Pure Land are Faith, Prayer, and Virtue. To enter this dharma door, the practitioner must first believe that the Ultimate Bliss realm is real, and that Amitabha always protects and is ready to guide all sentient beings to revere and recite...
noi_dung:
Section 21 - The Essential Characteristics of Making Vows

As mentioned above, the core teachings of Pure Land are Faith, Prayer, and Virtue. To enter this dharma door, the practitioner must first believe that the realm of Ultimate Bliss is real, and that Amitabha always protects and is ready to lead all sentient beings who pay respect and chant the six words of His holy name to call upon Him. Such belief is called Faith. After having faith, the practitioner must develop a sincere heart to seek escape from the Saha world full of suffering and obstacles, wishing to be born in the realm of Ultimate Bliss of peace and joy, immeasurable purity and solemnity, to practice and complete the goal of saving others. That's called Prayer. And when you have made vows like that, you need to sincerely recite Amitabha's name until the Buddha mind level is compatible, to be guided. This is called Hanh. The previous chapter said "Reciting the Buddha's name must eliminate doubts" is an explanation of Tin. This chapter discusses Vows. The next chapter continues to mention the practice part, that is, Conduct. Faith, Prayer, and Hanh are also known as the three pillars of Pure Land. For example, a person traveling far away must be equipped with a mosquito net, medicine, food, clothing, and money to have all the necessities while on the trip. Pure Land practitioners are the same. Without faith, they cannot make vows. Having Faith and Prayer without actually practicing it means cultivating the Virtue part, which is just Faith and Prayer. And if the conduct is complete but lacks faith and vows, then the practice is lost, without standards or guidelines. Therefore, Faith, Prayer, and Hanh are the thoughts of those who travel far to reach Ultimate Bliss. Regarding rebirth, these three things are interrelated; if one is missing, it will not be achieved.

• Great Master Nguoi Ich, a respected leader of Pure Land, taught: "Being reborn depends entirely on faith and vows, whether high or low, depends on the depth or shallowness of practice." He said again: "If you don't have faith and vows, even if you recite the holy name until the wind can't blow in, the rain can't fall, and it's as solid as a copper wall or an iron wall, you won't be reborn." People who recite Buddha's name diligently but lack Faith and Prayer, depending on the depth and breadth of their efforts, will only receive precious blessings from humans and heaven. When the blessings run out, they still have to suffer samsara as before. For example, in Vietnam, in the Later Le Dynasty, there was a monk at Quang Minh Pagoda. Although his practice of reciting Buddha was profound, because his vow was not sincere, when he fulfilled his destiny, he was reborn as an emperor of the Qing Dynasty in China. Later, the king used the well water of that pagoda to wash the lipstick marks inscribed on his shoulder from his past life, so he felt inspired to take some exams. There are two sentences in it:

Most Western Buddhists,

Van Ha falls in the royal family?

Italy says: I am originally the son of Amitabha Buddha in the West, why did I end up in the royal family like this? Although the king knew that in his previous life he was a monk chanting Buddha's name at Quang Minh pagoda, but because in his royal position, the blessings were too many, so he could not practice. Reciting Buddha without faith, May the result be like that! Therefore, looking closely at the words of Master Nguoi Ich, we see that high or low rank is not the problem, but the main problem is: "Is it possible to be reborn?" To be reborn, Faith is a must-have condition, and the most essential point is the word Prayer. The great master emphasized again: "If your faith is strong, when you die, just saying the name ten times or one time will still ensure rebirth. On the contrary, although the practice is as strong as an iron wall and a bronze wall, but the Faith in Prayer is weak, the result will only be the blessings of heaven and earth." This statement clearly states: It is better to believe and pray steadfastly, even if one's conduct is poor, one can achieve rebirth liberation. Looking here, we see how important the true and sincere Vows are for Pure Land practitioners!

---o0o---

tieu_de: Section 22 - sutra text Advice on making vows
tom_tat: Regarding the guiding force of the word Vow, the Samantabhadra Vows chapter in the Avatamsaka Sutra says: "When this person was about to die, in the last moment, all his senses were destroyed, all his relatives were separated...
noi_dung:
Section 22 - sutra text Advice on making vows

Regarding the guiding force of the word Vow, the Samantabhadra Vows chapter in the Avatamsaka Sutra says: "When this person was about to die, in the last moment, all his senses were destroyed, all his relatives were abandoned, all his power was gone. Only this king of vows does not leave each other, in all times, it leads ahead. And within a split second, that person was immediately reborn into the world of Ultimate Bliss."

Because he clearly sees the essential use of making vows, in the Amitabha Sutra, Buddha Thich Ton repeatedly repeats that point, through the following passages:

• "Again, Sariputta! Sentient beings in the land of Ultimate Bliss are all of the Abyss of Wisdom. There are many First Born Bodhisattva beings in there, the number is very large, it is impossible to calculate them with numbers, we can only speak of them using numbers that cannot be measured or increased in number. Shariputra! After hearing this, sentient beings should make vows to pray for rebirth in that world. Because why? Because we can gather together in one place with such noble people.

... Shariputra! I see that benefit, so I say this. If any sentient beings hear these words, they should make vows to pray for rebirth in that land.

... Shariputra! If there are people who have made vows, are making vows, will make vows, and want to be born in the land of Amitabha Buddha, those people have either been born, or are being born, or will be born, and will irreversibly attain the fruition of Anuttara Sammi Bodhi in that land. Therefore Sariputra! Good men and good women, if you have faith, should make vows to pray for birth in that land."

As above, we see Thich Ton repeating the words "making vows" over and over again. The comments are urgent. Until the end of the sutra text, He also repeatedly told us to make vows to pray for birth. Why? Because if you return to the realm of Ultimate Bliss, you will be in an extremely beautiful and solemn realm, have a diamond body with thirty-two good signs, and completely end the suffering of birth, old age, sickness, and death; to be close to Buddha, Bodhisattva monks and meet with noble people; attains the miraculous power of Samadhi and no longer regresses to the unsurpassed Bodhi fruition. Because the Buddha's wisdom saw so many benefits, he used compassion to save sentient beings and advised making vows for rebirth. The compassion of Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha is truly immeasurable.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Lesson 23 - Trying to Consider Rebirth Prayers
tom_tat: In the Infinite Life Sutra, Thich Ton briefly mentioned how many Bodhisattvas in the fourteen realms were born in Ultimate Bliss. In this Saha world alone, there are sixty-seven billions of Bodhisattva Bodhisattvas who have been reborn, and the number of minor Bodhisattva and...
noi_dung:
Lesson 23 - Trying to Consider Rebirth Prayers

In the Infinite Life Sutra, Thich Ton briefly mentioned how many Bodhisattvas in the fourteen realms were born in Ultimate Bliss. In this Saha world alone, there are sixty-seven billions of Bodhisattva Bodhisattvas who have been reborn, and the number of minor Bodhisattvas and sentient beings who practice some beneficial merits who have been reborn is countless! — The other thirteen countries are the lands of the Buddhas such as: Far-Reflecting Tathagata, Treasure Store Tathagata, Infinite Sounds Tathagata, Nectar Taste Tathagata, Dragon-Winning Tathagata, Superpower Tathagata, Lion Tathagata, Fragmented Light Tathagata, Virtuous Hand Tathagata, Wonderful Mountain Tathagata, King of Humanity Tathagata, Supreme Flower Tathagata, Fearless Tathagata; Each level has from ten billion to countless Bodhisattva rebirths of Ultimate Bliss. These are only the great Bodhisattva; As for the Bodhisattva and ordinary people, they are too numerous to describe! the Buddha said: "That is a summary of the fourteen realms. If we had to count all the Bodhisattvas in the ten directions of worlds born in Ultimate Bliss, then even if we talked about it night and day in one lifetime, it would not be enough!"

• Someone asked: - How can the realm of Ultimate Bliss be so accommodating?

- Please answer: According to the sutras, there is a Buddha who takes a great heaven as a Buddha land. There is a Buddha who takes many thousands of thousands of great worlds as one Buddha realm. As the Lotus Sutra says, Phu Lau Na will later become Buddha with the title of Invention Tathagata; This Buddha takes countless thousands of great worlds as a Buddha realm. The Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha is the leader of a great universe called Saha, consisting of a thousand million small worlds. He incarnated into a thousand million Shakyamuni Buddhas in those small worlds, appearing from birth until Nirvana to preach the Dharma. Then the realm of Ultimate Bliss can include from billions of millions to countless thousands of great worlds, so there's no need to worry about not having enough space to accommodate it! Again, retribution depends on the right retribution to appear. If the number of reborn people is large, all realms will appear accordingly. The power of Amitabha Buddha's wishes and blessings are boundless, depending on the number of rebirths, he can adorn a pure state.

- Ask again: According to the Amitabha Sutra, in each of the ten directions of the world, there are countless Buddhas in their respective lands praising and teaching the Pure Land method, advising living beings to attain Ultimate Bliss. Thus, it is possible for countless sentient beings to be reborn at the same time. How could Amitabha Buddha continue to guide them?

- Answer: Just like there is only one moon in the sky, from many oceans, rivers, ponds and lakes, down to every small dew drop, there is a moon shadow and is imbued with moonlight. Depending on their locality, everyone sees and receives the cool moonlight. The old saying:

Flowers bloom regardless of hunger or poverty.

The moon shines brightly across the river.

Amitabha Buddha is the same, with his pure and clear mind, he can release immeasurable light, receive blessings from the great Bodhisattva to sentient beings with many sins, confess and recite the holy name, and at the same time appear in numberless bodies like dust particles to lead countless sentient beings in the ten directions to be born to Ultimate Bliss.

• As above, we see that there are countless sentient beings of Ultimate Bliss, more than countless drops of rain. But in general, in terms of their wish to be born, we can divide them into three categories:

The first class is the lowly but sincere ordinary people who do not understand the merits and solemnity of the Pure Land. They only feel that life is full of hardships and hardships, the Saha world is full of depression and anxiety, so they wish to be born in a pure and happy land.

The second class, although they are also ordinary people, have great wisdom and aspirations, and want to be born in Ultimate Bliss to ensure escape from the path of samsara, quickly attain enlightenment, and fulfill their aspirations of saving others.

The third class, from the minor saints who have escaped the cycle of life and death to the Enlightened Bodhisattva, because they want to quickly advance to the upper world, want to learn the wonderful dharma and become Buddha, should make vows of rebirth.

Thus, we see that people who seek Pure Land are not only people who are bored with the suffering of the five defilements, but there are also people who, out of compassion, want to save sentient beings in the Saha world; to the monks on the Buddha's path, under the delusion of the masses in all ten directions of the world. Even though the aspirations are low and high, when one is born in Ultimate Bliss, they receive the same benefits, meaning everything is irreversible, reaching the goal of becoming a Buddha and benefiting birth. The ancients said: "The Pure Land Dharma is very profound and mysterious, only the Buddha and the Buddha can know it all, because the Enlightened One still vows to be reborn, the First Born Bodhisattva still has to stay in the Ultimate Bliss domain to learn. Mahayana sutras such as: Hoa Nghiem, Phap Hoa, Dai Bao Tich, etc. both praised Pure Land and mentioned rebirth." The Dharma method has brought so many wonderful benefits. Although countless sentient beings in the ten directions have been reborn in Ultimate Bliss, Thich Ton is not satisfied and wants to give even more believers and rebirth vows. Therefore, in the Infinite Life Sutra, he lamented and encouraged:

Infinite Life Buddha Land

Sravaka row, Bodhisattva

merit and wisdom

Can't praise it!

Back in that country

The mystery is extremely joyful.

Such purity,

Why don't you try to make up?

But reciting the Tao is natural?...

Everyone must be diligent

Try your best to make your own wishes

rebirth in the realm of Peace.

Socks are super great

Cross the five evil paths

Evil paths naturally close

Ascension is endless.

Easy birth without people!

The other world has no adversities

Move forward naturally.

Why don't you let go of your life?

Diligently practice morality?

To have a long life

Longevity and joy are endless...

Also in the Infinite Life Sutra, to show the great appreciation of Pure Land, the World-Honored One said: "Suppose there was a great fire burning throughout the three thousand great thousand worlds. In order to listen to this Dharma, we had to pass through that place. We should also joyfully believe and pray, so that we could accept, uphold, read, recite, and practice according to its teachings. Why? Because there are many Bodhisattvas who want to hear this sutra but cannot hear it. If any sentient being hears and accepts this sutra with faith, they will definitely not turn back from the Supreme Way."

The Dharma is precious and has so many benefits, so the World-Honored One once advised that after his nirvana, one should not have doubts about this dharma. But unfortunately, there are those who have not studied Buddha thoroughly and do not believe, but instead interpret this sutra in a way that accepts the truth, thus distorting and slandering, how pitiful and sad! Ancient elders said: "For Pure Land, there are only two types of people who benefit. One is the most ignorant but sincere person who only listens to the teachings and immediately believes and accepts them and practices them. Second, there is a person with deep wisdom who has good roots in the Pure Land, understands the nature, clearly understands the merits of reciting the Buddha, and is determined to believe and serve. As for ordinary intellectuals, if they understand deeply, they cannot understand it, but they cannot believe it like an ignorant person. Therefore, it is difficult for this class to receive benefits."

But, everything has a cause and effect. I only hope that those who are blessed with this subject, after listening to the above explanation, will strengthen their faith and vows.

Section B. Introducing the Making Vows Text of Tien Nhon

tieu_de: Section 24 - Making vows by Venerable Lien Tri and Tu Van
tom_tat: During each Pure Land session, after reciting, the practitioner immediately pays homage to the Buddha to pray for proof, then kneels down and reads the prayer dedicating merit. This part is very important, because it is when you use your thoughts to bring the merit you have cultivated towards...
noi_dung:
Section 24 - Making vows by Venerable Lien Tri and Tu Van

During each Pure Land session, after reciting, the practitioner immediately pays homage to the Buddha to pray for proof, then kneels down and reads the prayer dedicating merit. This part is very important, because it is when you use your thoughts to direct the merit you have cultivated to the place you want. Like a boat drifting, whether driven by the rower or the engine, it reaches its destination depending on the helmsman. The making vows part of Pure Land practitioners is the stage of using the mind to steer the boat of reciting Buddha towards the West. But there are many affiliated friends who do not pay attention to this point, instead proclaiming to read texts that are more of an exhortation than a prayer. Basically like the articles: "A peaceful place to live and nourish nature" or "The mundane life is so boring". The lives of the living beings gathered together for a few minutes." for example. Reading it like that is wrong with the Pure Land practice ritual.

Now, I would like to introduce here some Pure Land essays by ancient virtues. Regarding making vows, some people like long words so that they can have a sincere heart, while others like short words that are full of meaning to pray for birth. Therefore, the writer would like to choose two articles according to the above criteria, hoping to partly meet the interests of related customers.

• Making vows essay by Master Lien Tri:

Bow down to the West of An Lac

Leading sentient beings, the Great Teacher,

Now I make vows, vowing rebirth

Thank you for your compassion and mercy!

Now I pray for the four graces of the three realms and the dharma realm of sentient beings, seeking Bodhi, the Buddha's One Vehicle; Concentrate on reciting the name of all virtues, Amitabha Buddha, vowing to be born in the Pure Land. Again because of us, karma is heavy and blessings are slight, obstacles are deep and wisdom is shallow, the mind is easily affected by impurities, and pure virtue is difficult to achieve. Now for Tu Ton, respectfully sow the five qualities, expressing one-heartedness and sincerity of repentance. I and sentient beings, up to now, have been ignorant of the original pure mind, let go of greed, anger and ignorance, contaminated with the three karmas, immeasurable and boundless, the sins committed, immeasurable and boundless, unjust karma have been committed, vowing to destroy them all. Vow from today, make deep vows, stay away from evil dharma, vow to no longer create, diligently practice the holy path, vow not to be lazy and retreat, vow to attain enlightenment, vow to save sentient beings. Dear Compassionate One, please use the prayer of compassion to know my heart, have mercy on me, and bless me. I pray that when meditating, or dreaming, I can see the golden body of Amitabha Buddha, can play in the pure world of the Teacher, and thanks to the Venerable, nectar sprinkle my head, light illuminate my body, my hands will rub my forehead, my clothes will cover my body, allowing us to self-eliminate old obstacles, grow good roots, quickly eliminate afflictions, quickly destroy ignorance, achieve enlightenment of the color of the mind, bright and open, the true view of peace, often manifest. At the time of death, know the time and day ahead, the body is empty of all illness and suffering, the mind is free from all attachment and delusion, the senses are happy and beautiful, mindfulness is clear, letting go brings peace, like entering meditation. Buddha Amitabha, Avalokiteshvara, together with the Sages, the good light to guide them, the precious hands to guide them, the halls of garlands, the heavenly music and strange scents, the Western Buddha scene, clearly displayed. Makes sentient beings, those who see and hear, rejoice and praise, and develop Bodhi mind. At that time, my body, sitting on the Vajra platform, flying behind the Buddha, about the tip of a finger, was born in the precious lotus, in the Seven Jewels pond, in the Western world. Then when the flowers bloomed, they saw Buddha Bodhisattva, heard the wonderful Dharma voice, attained the Endless Forbearance, the moment passed again, in favor of all Buddhas, thanks to the grace of prophecy. After receiving the prediction, the three bodies and four wisdoms, five eyes and six powers, immeasurable hundreds of thousands, Dharani, all merits, are all achieved. From then on, never leaving An Duong, returning to Saha, countless emanations, throughout the ten directions, using supernatural powers, freedom from thought, and other means, to liberate sentient beings, all causing them to leave defilements, attain purity of mind, be reborn in the West, and ascend to the throne of Non-Return.

With such a great vow, the world will not end, sentient beings will not end, karma and afflictions will not end, my great vows will also not end. Now I pay homage to the Buddha, making vows to practice, please bring merit, give back to sentient beings, four graces everywhere, thanks to all three realms, sentient beings in the dharma world, together become wisdom.

• Making vows essay by Master Tu Van:

One-hearted surrender, the world of Ultimate Bliss, Amitabha Buddha. Please bring your pure light to illuminate my body, use the vow of compassion, and take care of me. Now I am mindful, calling myself Tathagata, for the sake of Bodhi, praying to be born in the Pure Land. Once Buddha took an oath: 'If any sentient being wants to return to my country, believes with all his heart, and recites my name for ten recitations, if he is not born, he will not become a Buddha.' Now I vow to rely on the opportunity to recite the Buddha's name and enter the sea of oaths of the Tathagata. Thanks to the power of the World-Honored One, I can eliminate my sins and increase my good roots. I vow to die, knowing the day and time in advance, with my body free from illness and suffering, my mind free from attachment, and my mind free from confusion, like entering meditation. Buddha and the Holy Order, holding the golden pedestal, came to welcome me. In a moment, I returned to Ultimate Bliss, flowers bloomed, saw the Buddha, heard the Buddha Vehicle, understood the Buddha's wisdom, saved all sentient beings, and fulfilled my Bodhi vow.

Please bring the merit of reciting this

dedicating merit to four graces and three realms

May all sentient beings throughout the Dharma world

All give birth to Ultimate Bliss and become Buddha.

---o0o---

Lesson 25 - making vows is urgent

• If people are illiterate, have poor memories, and cannot remember long sentences, it is recommended to teach them to memorize the following making vows: "Day... month... year..., disciple... I vow to use this merit to pray for the Buddha to guide me to Ultimate Bliss to attain Buddhahood and save sentient beings." A brief prayer accompanied by the date and year as above has the effect of creating a strong consciousness, causing the person chanting Buddha's thoughts to always turn to Ultimate Bliss, always remembering rebirth. This small detail is also a means to make the wish stronger and more durable.

When making vows, you must say them earnestly from the bottom of your heart. If you just read them casually, your heart is not sincere, and reciting Buddha's name will be difficult to be sincere. Master An Quang said: "Sincerity is the factor to reach one mind without chaos. There is a part of sincerity, a part of sin karma is eliminated, and a part of blessings and wisdom are born. Having ten parts of sincerity, eliminating ten parts of sin karma, giving birth to ten parts of blessings and wisdom." The ancients also said: "If you are sincere in your intentions, the gold and stones will open up"; mean: Wherever one's sincere effort is directed, one can split mountains and destroy gold. Determination is very powerful. The author remembers that in a book there is a story about a young doctor in France, a widower, who sadly went to the countryside to relax. While staying at the blacksmith's house, he saw that the homeowner's daughter was beautiful, so he told the truth, asked her to be his wife, and was accepted. But before the wedding, the doctor had sex with the girl and then left for the city. The blacksmith saw that his daughter's belly was getting bigger and bigger, he was as miserable as a red bird's wing, thinking that he was from a poor family and was too weak to sue. He was so angry that every afternoon he used a hammer to hit the iron plate and called out for the doctor to have his head broken, to relieve his anger. But in the capital every afternoon, at five o'clock, the doctor suddenly held his head and groaned, but with all the treatments he could not cure him. After the doctor's friend was visiting his hometown in the afternoon, when he passed by the blacksmith's house, he heard the sound of banging iron and called his friend's name to scold him, so he went in to ask. When you clearly understand the situation, reflect on the cause of your friend's illness. He advised the doctor to apologize and marry the blacksmith's daughter. After the wedding was completed, the doctor's illness was cured.

The mind has such invisible power. If you are aware of the above story and sincerely make vows to recite the Buddha's name, why worry about not receiving sympathy! In short, believing in prayer is an act of wisdom, reciting the Buddha is an act of practice; Wisdom is like the eyes, practice is like the feet. Truth and vision must depend on each other, vows and actions must be earnest, only then can one reach the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Section A. Buddha's Remembrance with the Four Virtues and the Four Virtues

tieu_de: Lesson 26 - Professional conduct is also an indispensable point
tom_tat: As mentioned above, the essential point of Buddha Recitation is to make vows of rebirth. If you think: "I just pray and recite Amitabha Buddha's name of all virtues a lot, and naturally I will have countless merits; Even without rebirth,…
noi_dung:
Lesson 26 - Professional conduct is also an indispensable point

As mentioned above, the essential point of Buddha Recitation is to make vows of rebirth. If you think: "I just pray and recite Amitabha Buddha's name of all virtues a lot, and naturally I will have countless merits; Even if you don't rebirth, that merit won't be lost." Thinking like that is a dangerous mistake and lacks wisdom. Because if you have virtue and do not pray, that merit will turn into blessings in the next life. In the second life, having enjoyed the blessings of ignorance, it is easy to create karma. In the third life, you will definitely fall into the three realms. That is a mistake and a dangerous thing! That's why above we call faith and vows "wisdom".

• Having enough Faith but lacking Virtue, like a boat with a steering wheel but no oars, it cannot be reborn. Someone heard: "As long as you have sincere faith and prayer, when you are about to die, ten thoughts or one thought will definitely give you birth in the West", then you immediately think: "If that's the case then there's no need to rush. Just recite Buddha's name when you're about to die!" This idea is also wrong, because it too underestimates the practice of Buddha Recitation. You must know, the important point for rebirth, according to the sutra text is: "That person's heart does not go crazy when he is about to die." (When a person's mind is not crazy, that is, he attains the rebirth Amitabha Buddha Ultimate Bliss - Amitabha Buddha's Sutra). If the heart does not go crazy at the time of death, even if you recite ten thoughts or one thought, you will be reborn. But who dares to say: When I'm about to die, my heart won't go crazy? If in normal times you don't diligently apply effort, then at the end of your life the four great elements will separate, your karma will be overwhelmed, your body and mind will be frightened and confused by suffering, I'm afraid you won't be able to practice even a single thought, let alone ten thoughts? As if to ensure some assurance at the time of death, during peaceful times the practitioner must diligently recite Buddha's name a lot, and try to practice the level of "single-mindedness and non-distraction". Just wait until you're about to die to recite it. In theory, it's certainly clear, but I'm afraid in reality it's not that simple. Therefore, practitioners of reciting the Buddha's name must try their best, do not neglect and despise their practice, which will lead to failure.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Lesson 27 - Reciting the Buddha's Name with the Four Points
tom_tat: The Buddhist rebirth discipline is a Dharma teacher who cuts down on the Mahayana, because practitioners take the enlightenment in the earth realm as the starting point in the human realm. From an ordinary person in the four realms of existence and six paths, thanks to the Buddha's guidance, he ascended to the throne of Non-Return, on par with...
noi_dung:
Lesson 27 - Reciting the Buddha's Name with the Four Points

The Buddhist rebirth discipline is a Dharma teacher who cuts down on the Mahayana, because practitioners take the enlightenment in the earth realm as the starting point in the human realm. From an ordinary person in the four realms of existence and six paths, thanks to the Buddha's guidance, he ascended to the throne of Non-Return, on the same level as the superior Bodhisattva; If it wasn't Buddha himself saying it, who would believe it? Because in order to enter the position of First Tru and ascend to the throne, people who practice other sects must go through a thousand lifetimes, and in each lifetime they must continuously practice diligently. If we talk about taste that doesn't rot, conduct that doesn't rot, and thoughts that don't rot, it's even further! Regarding the Pure Land practice, the practitioner who believes in other powers uses all his own power, all cultivators and all people are reborn, transcending samsara and no longer regressing.

If we use Buddha's Recitation practice to discover the mind and realize the original nature, then the Pure Land sect is no different from other sects. As for using Buddha Recitation to rebirth the Buddha realm, this sect is somewhat special.

Ancient virtue said:

1. Birth is determined by birth, return is truly non-returning: is to win scenes, not people.

2. Regarding all determination, birth does not really exist: is to steal people, not scenes.

3. Returning is truly non-returning, birth is also truly not born: Scenes and people both win.

4. Regarding all decisions, birth also decides birth: is that neither objects nor people can take it away.

Above are the four simple sentences and the Four Virtues of Pure Land. The word "win" means: physical clarity. Because the entire dharma world is one mind, people and scenes are like illusions, if you see someone reborn, there is a scene to be born into, you still accept the person and the dharma, distinguishing here and there, so it is called not taking, that is, not understanding the physical body. And on the contrary, that is, to win. Tien Duc said: "There are thoughts and there are no thoughts. Not being born means being born. Don't bother moving half a step. Come to Giac king citadel", that is, this idea.

Both people and scenes are captured, which is the highest level of a practitioner reciting the Buddha's name. But according to the three Pure Land sutras and the Celestial Body Sutra (Buddha Sutra on Amitabha Theory, Amitayus, and Infinite Life Contemplation - Celestial Body Sutra i.e. rebirth Sutra or Infinite Life Sutra), one should take "neither people nor objects." as a tone, it fits the meaning of the word "rebirth". Because the Tathagata knows that ordinary people in the realm of the five impurities, especially in this time of the end of the dharma, have deep and heavy karma obstacles, setting up a scene and form for them to follow and practice with their mind, is it difficult to have results, let alone leaving the form? Ordinary people in the Dharma-Ending Age are able to maintain their form and practice all the vows that are easily urgent, and the result of rebirth is also easy to achieve. When you return to the West, why are you worried about not being able to attain the state of no birth and no form? If you are not a person of superior intelligence and are in a hurry to seek a higher level of love and abandon your appearance, practice with all your heart and mind without relying on anything to give birth to urgent thoughts. If you wish, there is no way to achieve rebirth. No rebirth to escape the suffering of samsara? "If you want to be fast, it will become slow. If you want to be tall, it will become short. If you want to be clever, it will become clumsy!" Many people love to talk about mysteries, often refuting: "Reciting the Buddha's name to seek rebirth is to accept appearances outside the mind and seek dharma, not understanding that all dharmas are mind-only." These people have mysterious intentions, but in reality they are short-sighted! Because they don't understand that if Saha is idealistic, Ultimate Bliss is also idealistic. Where does everything exist but the true mind? So, reciting Amitabha Buddha is reciting the Buddha in your mind, about Ultimate Bliss, which is about the realm of your own mind, not outside? Both Saha and Ultimate Bliss are not outside the mind, so in Saha to suffer the chaos of samsara, to be burned by the fire of the five defilements, how can it be better than returning to Ultimate Bliss to be happy and enjoy the peaceful and carefree landscape? You should know that the right place to worship and idealize Pure Land must be someone who has realized the Dharma nature and can be free in all circumstances. At that time, whether it is Saha or Ultimate Bliss, it is Pure Land, idealism, and liberation. Otherwise, even if you speak magically, you still won't be able to escape the coma when you're away from home, and then it's up to karma samsara to suffer!

---o0o---

tieu_de: Lesson 28 - Reciting Buddha With the Four Virtues
tom_tat: The interests and faculties of sentient beings are often different, so even though we practice Buddha Recitation, our practice cannot help but have some differences. Therefore, on the Pure Land path, ancient people roughly divided it into four practices: meditation…
noi_dung:
Lesson 28 - Reciting Buddha With the Four Virtues

The interests and faculties of sentient beings are often different, so even though we practice Buddha Recitation, our practice cannot help but have some differences. Therefore, on the Pure Land path, ancient people roughly divided it into four practices: meditation Pure, Teaching Pure, Secret Pure and Pure Pure.

1. Those who take reciting the Buddha's name as primary and meditation as secondary, belong to the practice of Pure meditation. This is also the practice of Pure Land meditation, but it takes the Pure Land rebirth as the final weakness, and seeing the nature of enlightenment is only dependent on conditions.

2. Those who take reciting the Buddha as their main focus and chanting sutras as their secondary practice are called Giao Tinh practitioners. Regarding the sutras, some people like chanting the Vajrayana sutras or Amitabha; There are people who like to recite Avatamsaka or Dharma Flower, or the Samantabhadra or Universal Virtue Vows, for example.

3. Those who take reciting the Buddha's name as their main focus and reciting mantras as their secondary practice are cultivating the practice of Secret Purity. In reciting mantras, each person has their own preference for each Dharani subject, such as: Great Compassion, Chuan De, rebirth, Bao Son merit, Manjushri Five-Things mantra, Six-Sided Dai Minh mantra-words, or other Dharanis.

4. Those who only specialize in reciting the Buddha's name, without any other distractions, belong to Pure Purity practitioners.

Here, those with high capacity follow the Sixteen Contemplations, while the vast majority only specialize in the practice of reciting the name.

• Venerable Thien Dao and meditation master Vinh Minh in China, it is said that they are both reincarnations of Amitabha Buddha. But Venerable Thien Dao only taught to recite Buddha's name; Vinh Minh meditation master appears every day, in addition to reciting ten thousand verses of the Buddha's name, he also practices other practices, all including 108 disciplines. „n The Light Mage criticized: "He teaches about Pure Land, but Thien Dao's teaching style is to guide the middle and lower level to specialize in practice. As for Mr. Vinh Minh's teaching style, it is reserved for encouraging people of superior ability and belongs to practitioners." Most of the people in the Dharma Ending Age are of middle and lower level. Therefore, with the above four virtues, if you want to be sure of rebirth, you should probably practice the Pure Path. But having said that each person's preferences and aptitudes are different and cannot be forced, then even though they practice other practices, Pure Land practitioners also need to pay attention to the two main parts and assist in clarifying. The main part must always outweigh the supporting part. Only then will the path of practice not lose its goal and rebirth will not be hindered.

---o0o---

Section B. Overview of Buddha Recitation Methods

tom_tat: Reciting the Buddha's name is not just about reciting it with your mouth, but using your mind to remember it, which is also reciting the Buddha. Therefore, in Buddha Recitation, in addition to the method of reciting the name, there are three other methods: Reality, Contemplation and Contemplation
noi_dung:
Section 29 - Four Buddhist Recitations

Reciting the Buddha's name is not just about reciting it with your mouth, but using your mind to remember it, which is also reciting the Buddha. Therefore, in Buddha Recitation, in addition to the method of reciting the name, there are three other methods: Reality, Contemplation and Contemplation.

1. Truly the Buddha's Remembrance,That is, entering the first meaning of the mind, which is remembering one's own original Buddha nature. This is the contemplation of Buddha's true form of the Dharma body, the result will be the realization of True Samadhi. This method still belongs to meditation, but the realm revealed by the meditation mind is Pure Land, so it also returns to Pure Land. This Dharma does not include the middle and lower levels, and if one does not have the upper or upper level, one cannot comprehend it. Therefore, in the Pure Land sect, there are few proponents, but the propaganda part belongs to those in the Zen school. But in my humble opinion: When you are still on the path of practice and have not yet reached the state of enlightenment, all dharma methods belong to the means, reciting the Buddha is also a means and practicing meditation is also a means. According to the three Pure Land Sutras, Buddha Thich Ton opened a means to show Amitabha Buddha's Ultimate Bliss realm, advising sentient beings to recite Buddha's name to pray for rebirth in that world so that they will no longer be subject to samsara, and to borrow the wonderful predestined conditions to continue practicing quickly to reach Buddhahood. Practicing Buddha Recitation diligently also achieves enlightenment like the Zen school, but the main point of Buddha Recitation is to pray for rebirth, and how much enlightenment one can achieve is also a secondary part. Therefore, the Dharma of the Buddha's True Form, discussing the final destination, still belongs to the Pure Land. But if we talk about the means of rebirth, it still does not officially belong to Pure Land, as the meaning of the three Pure Land sutras that Thich Ton proposed. Perhaps because of this point, the Patriarchs of Tinh Tong only mentioned it to expand on the meaning of Pure Land, but did not expand on Hsuan Hua to advise practitioners?

2. Buddha Memorial Temple, is according to the Infinite Life Sutra, to visualize the right retribution in the realm of Ultimate Bliss. In this sutra, there are sixteen ways of contemplation taught. If the practice of contemplation is mature, then when the practitioner opens or closes his eyes, he will see the scene of Ultimate Bliss mentally roaming in the pure realm. When he dies, he decides to be reborn. The merit of this dharma is inconceivably great, but because the contemplation scene is so subtle and profound, few people can practice it successfully. Because there are five difficult things in there. First, if the senses are dull, it will be difficult to achieve. Second, if the mind is rough, it will be difficult to achieve. Third, if you don't know how to skillfully use rotation while practicing, it will be difficult to achieve. Fourth, if the impression is not deep, it will be difficult to achieve. Fifth, if your energy is weak, it will be difficult to achieve. Of these five conditions, few people can fully satisfy them, so the Revisited Contemplation technique also belongs to a subject that is difficult to practice.

3. Buddha Recitation Statue, is the method of placing an Amitabha Buddha statue in front of you, noting all the features of that statue, then visualizing until even without the statue, when you open and close your eyes you can see the Buddha image clearly appearing in front of you. This method is also difficult, because it requires strong mental energy, deep memory, and skillful means. There have been people who have applied this method, but because they were not skillful in using the means of change, the fire broke out and caused headaches that were difficult to treat. But considering the method of Contemplation for rebirth, it is not mentioned in the sutra. This is just a way to assist in reciting the name Buddha, so that the practitioner's mind will not be distracted and it will be easier to be mindful. If the practitioner, with a sincere heart, can also be inspired, eliminate karma sins, give birth to blessings, and from the false image, see the true form of the Buddha and be reborn.

4. reciting the name Buddha Recitation,is the method of reciting out loud or silently the four or six words of the name "Namo Amitabha Buddha." Reciting the four words "Amitabha Buddha" Gaining advantages makes it easier to focus; Maintaining all six words will gain benefits and easily generate feelings of respect and gratitude. This method in the Amitabha Buddhist Sutra, proposed by Buddha Thich Ton, is currently the most popular.

• Looking at the four methods of reciting Buddha's name, the True Form method and Contemplation of Images are not mentioned in the three Pure Land sutras, only the Samadhi Reciting Buddha Sutra, the book Samantabhadra Samantabhadra and a few other sutras mention it. But both are only secondary means, to further expand on the teachings of Buddha recitation, not the official path of the Pure Land discipline that the Patriarchs of the Lien Tong Sect always promote. Dharma True Form only has the effect of deeply deducing the meaning of Buddha's name, but it is too profound, does not cover all three senses, straying to the side of meditation. The Contemplation Method is only a supplementary method, and it is not easy to practice. For Pure Land practitioners, those two subjects are not suitable. Although the method of Contemplation was praised by the Buddha, it has immeasurable merits, but it is only reserved for people of superior ability, few people in the Dharma-ending age can practice it. In short, reciting the name Buddha Recitation covers all three senses, is effective quickly, and anyone can practice it. If reciting the name, if you are pure, you will have a feeling. Right now, you will immediately see the correct retribution in the realm of Ultimate Bliss. You will realize your original mind. Even if you have not yet realized your true form in this life, you will definitely be able to realize it after rebirth. Therefore, Master Quang, the thirteenth Patriarch of Lien Tong, praised:

Only reciting the name can authenticate the form,

No need to contemplate to see the West!

The Ancient One also commented: "The Pure Land discipline is a shortcut to attain enlightenment in all dharma disciplines, and the reciting the name method is a shortcut in the Pure Land discipline." Currently, this method is the most popular way in Buddha Recitation.

tieu_de: Section 30 - Ten Methods reciting the name
tom_tat: As mentioned, reciting the name is the most popular Pure Land practice today. But reciting the name is also applied in many different ways depending on each person's nature, which the writer would like to filter through several methods such as
noi_dung:
Section 30 - Ten Methods reciting the name

As mentioned, reciting the name is the most popular Pure Land practice today. But reciting the name is also applied in many different ways depending on each person's nature, which the author would like to filter through the following methods:

1. Ban Van reciting the name: - In this method, the mouth chants and the ears listen in, controlling each word and each sentence so that it is clear and distinct from sentence to sentence. There are two ways to listen, either using headphones or using your mind to listen. Even though I hear inside, I don't stay anywhere. I gradually forget everything inside and out, until I forget all the realms of body and mind, time and space, leaving only the Buddha's name. The counter-text method makes it easier for practitioners to eliminate delusions and quickly achieve single-mindedness. The Shurangama Sutra says: "The true teachings of this method are pure by hearing the sound. If you want to attain Samadhi, you should practice like that"; is the idea above.

2. So Chau reciting the name: - This is the way of reciting the prayer with the mouth and hands while praying the rosary. Initially, the thoughts are still tied to the rosary, and after letting go, they reach the state of one mind. The pearl book method makes the power of mindfulness strong, like a person with weak legs going up a mountain, relying on a stick to keep going higher and higher. Reciting this way requires recording how many sentences each time or day is. Recording numbers has the advantage of forcing the practitioner to keep the number fixed, eliminating the disease of laziness; But you need to be careful not to be too greedy and greedy so that your thoughts cannot be clear. Although the ancients recited a lot, they were still clear, thanks to two points: mature and focused. Great Master Ich Ich, the ninth Patriarch of Lien Tong, once taught: "If you want to reach the realm of one mind without chaos, there is no other miraculous way. First, the practitioner needs to recite the rosary and write down the number, reciting clearly and clearly, every day for three thousand, five thousand, up to ten thousand sentences, keeping the course of decisions without missing, vowing to not change for the rest of his life. Reciting like that for a long time and gradually getting better at it. If you don't recite it, you can still recite it yourself. At that time, you can write down the number or not write down the number. And reciting like that, accompanied by a fervent prayer, without rebirth, all Buddhas of the three generations will be guilty of lying. Once reborn, all methods are visible. If initially, because of seeking superiority and self-reliance, wanting to show that you are not in front of appearances, wanting to learn the way of perfect contentment and freedom, that is not a deep faith in your vows, and your practice is not done with all your strength; Even if you preach twelve parts of the teachings and understand one thousand seven hundred koans, you are still on the brink of life and death."

This advice is truly a guide for those who recite Buddha's name.

3. Tuy Tuc reciting the name: - Reciting the Buddha's name silently or reciting it will make a sound, depending on the breath, each breath in and out has a Buddha's name; That is the meaning of Tui ie reciting the name. Because human life is related to the breath, if you know how to rely on this and recite, then when you live forever, you will never leave the Buddha. When you die, your breath will die and immediately return to the Federation realm. But it should be noted that once this method is practiced, you need to recite it out loud, not just silently. Only then will the power of mindfulness be strong, and the wish for birth can easily arise. Otherwise, the idea of rebirth will be difficult to take seriously and I'm afraid I will get lost in the uses of the Five Dinh Mind Contemplation of Hinayana.

4. Truyen Danh reciting the name: - When using this method, you should recite in a low voice, each word and each sentence succeeding each other closely, forming a pattern where the next word follows the previous word, each sentence overlaps the other, so it is called Truy Danh. Applying such a method, thanks to the discreetness and durability, the intermediary does not interfere, so random thoughts have no place to creep in. Using this method, the emotions are tense, the mind and mouth are brave, the power of mindfulness covers everything, causing the karma of ignorance to temporarily subside, the light of Samadhi erupts and shines far away. Since ancient times, people who have practiced purifying karma when their thoughts are in turmoil have often used this method.

5. Giac Chieu reciting the name: - Reciting according to the Enlightenment Illumination is on the one hand reciting Buddha's name and on the other hand reflecting the light back to one's true nature. By reciting like that, the practitioner will enter the realm of sublime emptiness, only feeling that his body and mind are condensed into one with Buddha's true mind, bright and round, full of vastness. At that time, all the things in the house were hidden, and even my four-element body didn't know where it fell. Reciting according to this, the retribution body has not yet been completed and will have passed away. The Buddha's name has just been declared and he will immediately enter Samadhi. Taking your ordinary body and participating in the holy scene is really no faster than the above method. However, it's just a pity that if you don't have superior ability, you probably won't be able to comprehend and practice it, so the potential of this method is still small.

6. Li Bai reciting the name: - This method is to bow and chant Buddha at the same time. Either recite one verse and bow once, or chant one verse and bow on the other, without commenting on how much or how little the Buddha verse is. The way to pay homage to the Buddha must be very gentle and slow, chanting in parallel, body and mouth in unison. If we add to that a sincere and sincere intention, then the three karma are all concentrated, apart from the Buddha's name there is not a single thread of false thoughts. This method has the ability to eliminate drowsiness and has great merit and effectiveness, because the practitioner uses all three karmas to recite. Layperson Vuong Nhat Huu used to apply the above method in the past. Every day and night he chanted an average of a thousand prostrations. But it seems that this is a special way of reciting for people who are diligent in their mental energy. Without that ability, it is difficult to be steadfast, because when bowing for a long time, the body becomes tired and easily becomes depressed. So normally, this method is only suitable for dual uses and is difficult to use.

7. Ky Thap reciting the name: - This is the way to chant numbers, take every ten sentences as a unit. People who are a bit short can recite it in two sets, each with five sentences; Or divided into three parts, two paragraphs with three sentences and one paragraph with four sentences. After reciting all ten sentences, each turn through a rosary. Reciting this way, the mind already recites Buddha, and also has to remember the number. So even if you're not a specialist, you still have to specialize. If you don't specialize, the number of entries will be wrong. Therefore, this dharma is essentially a means of coercion for dedicated practitioners, and is very effective for those with many distracting thoughts. „n Master Quang often advises his associates to apply the above method.

8. Lien Hoa reciting the name: - Take the four colors of lotus flowers, blue, yellow, red, white, chanting and thinking at the same time, circulating and passing on, is the name of the above method of reciting. When the practitioner recites the first Buddha's name, he imagines that a large blue lotus appears in front of him, emitting blue light. The second sentence, imagine a golden lotus releasing golden light. Until the third and fourth verses, it's a red lotus, a white lotus, whichever color releases that light. Next, continue to think of the blue lotus flower, circulating like that forever. At the same time, when the flowers appear, you think there is a gentle lotus scent wafting around. Because there are many practitioners in the Padmasambhava sect who use every method of consciousness but still have difficulty stopping random thoughts, the ancients invented this way of chanting. This is the way to use changing form to force the mind to be single, and this form takes the form of the lotus flower in the seven-jeweled pond in the Ultimate Bliss realm "One Amitabha sentence, one precious lotus", because the Pure Land lotus that appears is inseparable from the merit lotus of the Buddha's mind. And when death occurs, the practitioner's consciousness will rely on that precious lotus flower to be born into Ultimate Bliss. If you feel you have an affinity with the above method, you should apply it to quickly enter the Buddha's Recitation of Wonderful Lotus Samadhi.

9. Quang Trung reciting the name: - Because there are practitioners who, when they close their eyes and recite the Buddha's name, often suddenly see impure appearances or dark, disturbing colors emerging, so the ancients taught this method. This is the method of reciting Buddha while thinking that you are sitting in the middle of a large, transparent area of ​​light. When the mind has stabilized in that area of light, the practitioner feels a cool, clear mind. Not only are impure thoughts eliminated, but all impure and evil appearances are also dissipated. Then mindfulness is thus lasting, and Samadhi is also gradually achieved. Although this is a special means to eliminate impure and evil appearances, even if one does not have that karma disease, if one wants to have a peaceful spirit to go deeper into Buddha Recitation Samadhi, the practitioner should also apply this method.

10. Buddha restaurant recitals the name: - The method of visualization in the Contemplation Sutra is very important and has great merit, but it is not yet a common means for sentient beings of the end of time to practice the Dharma. But because they did not want to give up the special merit of contemplation of the Dharma, the ancients used the sixteen methods of contemplation, choosing the easiest way to practice, taking reciting the name as the main, contemplation of Buddha as secondary, called Contemplation of Buddha reciting the name. Every day, after reciting the Buddha's name, the practitioner sets aside a quiet time to contemplate the surrounding appearance of Amitabha Buddha. This Buddha contemplation is selected from the thirteenth contemplation in the Contemplation Sutra. Imagine Amitabha with a body six feet tall, pure golden color, standing on the bank of a seven-jeweled pond. If one has not yet visualized the seven-jeweled pond, the practitioner can imagine the Buddha standing in the light area in the middle of nothingness before his eyes, his left hand raised across his chest to make the auspicious mudra, his right hand hanging down in the following position. If you want to meditate on the Buddha for success, you should first visualize the whole body, then concentrate on contemplating the appearance of white hair between the eyebrows. This white line is as empty and transparent as white jade, has eight edges, turns to the right, and forms five high circles. The white line is the basic form among the thirty-two signs. When this form is achieved, due to chance, the other signs will appear one after another. However, if you want to be certain, you should also review the sutras to clearly remember the Buddha's thirty-two good signs before applying. The reason for the above method is to reciting the name in the main part, because if the visualization fails, there is still the reciting the name part to ensure rebirth. But in fact, reciting the name also helps visualization, visualization in turn supports reciting the name, these two parts together bring the practitioner to parallel achievements. Although this method is somewhat more difficult than the above methods, if accomplished, the merit is boundless, so I would like to give it last as a condition to encourage progress.

• As above, the ten ways of reciting the name are outlined, which are also the ten essential methods to treat the mental illness of people reciting Buddha. In the Pure Land books, dozens of ways are given such as: Cao Thanh reciting the name, De Thanh reciting the name, Mang Trung reciting the name, Nhan Trung reciting the name, etc., but those are just ways of reciting high and low voices, sometimes urgent, sometimes urgent, and cannot be called a method of reciting Buddha. Therefore, the writer has selected and drawn out ten basic methods, which can be called "methods", to treat the obstacles of lethargy and chaos, and can be common to a large part of the current nature. Among the ten methods above, you can experiment, and finally apply whichever way of thinking is most suitable for you...

---o0o---

Section C. Entering the True Way

tieu_de: Section 31 - The Four Doors of Samadhi
tom_tat: When people recite the Buddha's name, when they reach the ultimate peak, there is only one form, the Buddha's Recitation Samadhi. This is a scene of illusory light and calmness, illusions are dissipated, the practitioner only remains focused on the good form or the Buddha's name. But even though…
noi_dung:
Section 31 - The Four Doors of Samadhi

When people recite the Buddha's name, when they reach the ultimate peak, there is only one form, the Buddha's Recitation Samadhi. This is a scene of illusory light and calmness, illusions are dissipated, the practitioner only remains focused on the good form or the Buddha's name. But although it is said to exist, it is actually non-existing, because sound and form are illusory, which is empty. What is that form of Samadhi like? - According to Master Lieu Du, when the practitioner concentrates on reciting the Buddha, he forgets all the external worlds, time and space, until the moment of extremely pure energy, right where he is reciting, false thoughts suddenly disappear, his mind brightens, and he enters the realm of no thoughts, no thoughts. That scene is like empty space, clouds disappear, the sky is blue, thinking but not thinking, not thinking but knowing, not seeing is true seeing and knowing, seeing and knowing is the joy of the world. At this point, the green and silver waters are all the ultimate truth, the chirping streams and singing birds express the wonderful vehicle, the mind's light encompasses all images but does not abide in one dharma, it is still shining, it is shining but it is still gone, everything remains and is lost, it is completely perfect...

The realm of Samadhi is basically like that, it is difficult to describe in words, only by witnessing can one experience it. Reciting Buddha Samadhi is still one form, but to enter that state of concentration, the ancients based on the sutras, the meaning and the dignity of practice, and divided it into four subjects as follows:

1. Eight Chu Samadhi: - Bat Chu means Buddha Lap. Practicing this Samadhi, there are three powerful supporting powers: The power of Buddha, the power of Samadhi, and the power of merit of practitioners. When actually practicing the Eightfold Samadhi, you must take ninety days as a period. During that time, day and night the practitioner only stands or walks, thinking that Amitabha Buddha appears standing on his crown with thirty-two good appearances and eighty beauties; Or the mouth often recites the Buddha's name, the mind often thinks of Buddha without any interference. When successful, in the Samadhi the practitioner sees Amitabha and all the Buddhas of the ten directions appearing before him, encouraging and praising him.

The Eightfold Path is also called the Everlasting Way. When practitioners walk, with every step and every sound, they never leave the Buddha's name. The three karmas practice without interruption like a flowing stream. This Dharma has very high merit, but only those with superior ability can practice it. Middle-class people with weak energy cannot practice it.

2. Nhat Hanh Samadhi: - Nhat Hanh means specializing in one practice. When cultivating this Samadhi, the practitioner often sits and concentrates only on contemplating, or chanting the name of Amitabha. Even though he only practices one practice, he fully understands all practices, so Nhat Hanh is also called Vien Hanh. From this Samadhi dharma to the following two subjects, all three levels of foundation can be practiced.

3. Dharma Flower Samadhi: - This is one of the sixteen Samadhis as narrated in the Dharma Flower Sutra of the Wonderful Sound Bodhisattva. According to the will of Thien Thai Tong, the three ultimate truths are the Dharma, the true power is the flower. For example, when the petals (rights) of a lotus flower have not yet bloomed, the lotus mirror (real) has already formed, the mirror and petals are at the same time; In a flower, it contains all the meanings of power and truth.

According to the Pure Land sect, mindfulness is Buddha, form is mind; One Buddha chant includes all three truths, including true power. If you understand this principle and recite the Buddha's name, it is called cultivating the Dharma Flower Samadhi. When cultivating this Samadhi, the practitioner uses the two postures of sitting and walking, alternately contemplating the Buddha or reciting the Buddha, until he attains the right concentration. This practice ritual is somewhat easier than the Nhat Hanh Samadhi above.

4. Samadhi according to one's own will: - This method means depending on the mind whether walking, standing, or sitting, constantly reciting Amitabha's name to practice and attain Samadhi. This practice is also called "Liu Thuy Niem Buddha". For example, the water in a river continues to flow forever, even if it encounters a stone blocking it, it only bounces back and then finds a way to flow. Normally, people who follow this practice, every late night, bow to Amitabha Buddha forty-eight times, Avalokitesvara, Theravada and Hai Sang each seven times, then kneel down to repent. Then from then until evening, when walking, standing, lying down, and sitting, recite the Buddha's name, or pray the rosary to write down the number, or simply recite, until before going to bed, pay homage to the Buddha again and practice merit during the day, making vows dedicating merit rebirth. While practicing, if you come into contact with conditions, when they pass, you still return to reciting Buddha. Although this method of practice is easy and convenient, you must be skillful in avoiding conditions and have a persistent mind to achieve success.

---o0o---

noi_dung:
Section 32 - Three Parts of Practice

Regarding the Pure Land ritual, if it is complete, there must be five parts or five doors, also called the Five Mindfulness Doors. These are: Prostrations, Praises, Remembrances, making vows, and dedicating merit. For simplicity, I would like to summarize it into three parts: Praising the Ceremony Gate, Reciting Remembrance Gate, and making vows dedicating merit Gate. The practitioner can choose from the ten methods of reciting the name mentioned above, depending on the appropriate place to practice. If there are reciting mantras or chanting sutras, they should be recited before reciting Buddha. Regarding making vows dedicating merit, you can also freely choose one of the previous vows. Regarding Praise Ceremony, the Pure Land books provide more or less prostration rituals, depending on the preferences of each nature.

According to the order of Pure Land rites, the starting point is the Praise Ceremony. Before worshiping, the practitioner should recite the text praising the Buddha's merits, and then come to the bowing part. This is called Tan Le Mon. Next, continue reciting mantras or chanting sutras and then reciting Buddha, or just concentrate on reciting Buddha. This stage is called Tri Niem Mon. And finally, after reciting Buddha, the practitioner kneels down and recites the prayer dedicating merit, then bows three times and retreats. This part is called making vows dedicating merit Subject.

The worship part can also be changed a bit arbitrarily. Some people first bow many times, then only bow three times to the Three Refuges or the Western Three Saints. Some people are afraid to first bow to a tired body and recite the Buddha's name not to be pure, so they only bow three times normally, wait until after reciting the Buddha, then bow many times to pray for blessings, then kneel down to read the original text. Finally, the three bows are over.

Pure Land ritual has three levels: upper, middle, lower to suit the fundamentals. Here, I would only point out the Praise Ceremony subject of the three levels, and in the following two subjects, practitioners can increase or decrease according to those three levels depending on the part.

tieu_de: Lesson 33 - How to Treat Depression and Distraction
tom_tat: Practitioners sometimes feel lost in a state of confusion and want to sleep; That is the hindrance of lethargy. Or sometimes, although the mouth recites Buddha's name, the mind wanders and thinks about other things; That's the chaos of false predestined relationships. Depression and chaos…
noi_dung:
Lesson 33 - How to Treat Depression and Distraction

Practitioners sometimes feel lost in a state of confusion and want to sleep; That is the hindrance of lethargy. Or sometimes, although the mouth recites Buddha's name, the mind wanders and thinks about other things; That's the chaos of false predestined relationships. Torpor and distraction are two very dangerous obstacles, because they destroy the practitioner, making it impossible to enter right concentration.

Many people, while practicing, suddenly quiet their delusions, the Buddha's chants are still heard regularly, their thoughts are calm and they forget the heat, or the bites of mosquitoes. This state usually lasts from half an hour to an hour, sometimes sweating and soaking your shirt without even realizing it; When I suddenly woke up, I felt hot and uncomfortable. Practitioners seeing this should not rush to rejoice that their mind is at peace and that their efforts have had some success. Actually, it is just a state of drowsiness that belongs to the subtle and gentle part. The ancients said: "A gentle, undetectable kiss. All day long, the ghosts make a living!" In this case, the practitioner must raise his spirit, use effort to cut and split, chant and look inside to destroy it. According to experience, roughly when drowsiness is about to set in, the first thing that will happen is scattered thoughts. There are also times when drowsiness and delusion arise at the same time. But this is a crude phenomenon, very easy to detect. When the subtle drowsiness is about to appear, first a kind of subtle delusion arises, the practitioner feels that there is a point of confusion from the back of the head to the top of the head, then down to the eyes and finally into the heart. Wherever the drowsiness goes, that place is affected, like when the head is slightly lowered, when the eyes are closed, the eyes are closed; When it comes to the heart, the mind becomes confused. Regarding mild lethargy, one must have a subtle mind to comment.

• Delusional thinking also has two parts: rough and subtle. Everyone knows the gross delusion, because the action of thinking is very clear. The ancients said: "New practitioners are afraid of delusion, long-term practitioners are afraid of drowsiness." This statement is only partly true, not very helpful, because it only talks about the scattered part of gross delusion. As for subtle delusions, even mature practitioners have to be afraid. Because when reciting the Buddha's name, we use careful and discreet efforts. Of course, the gross and floating thoughts must be quiet, but it is very difficult to perceive the back and forth of the subtle delusions. For example, in a pond with turbid water, only when the foam rises to the surface of the pond do we notice it. As for the small, light gas from the bottom of the pond that is stirred up, it either boils to the surface of the water, or when it reaches the halfway point it cannot come up. To see it clearly, it is necessary to have a pond with very clear water. People who recite Buddha's name for a long time, until the state of mind is clear, can see subtle delusions. The White Saint Mage, one morning, walked from his bed to his chair. In about three seconds, he discovered that dozens of different false thoughts arose in his mind. Only then did He prove the words in the Buddha Sutra: "One thought has ninety moments, one moment has nine hundred births and deaths." This is delusion of the subtle type.

• By the way, I would like to repeat a story about subtle delusions, to give fellow practitioners more awareness: Quang Hue and Gioi Dien are two meditation masters who both attained enlightenment. One day while sitting in meditation, a thought of lust arose in Gioi Dien's subconscious mind, which he immediately eliminated; But on the other side, Zen master Quang Hue already knew. After coming out of samadhi, Mr. Quang Hue wrote a poem with the intention of teasing Mr. Gioi Dien. The meditation master was sad and immediately entered nirvana. Mr. Quang Hue regretted and called his disciples to his office and said: "While meditating, my friend had a thought of love for form, and then became attached to form; Because of bothering me, he passed away, and later he will destroy the Sangha Treasure. That mistake is partly my fault. If I do not follow the transformation, I will definitely face the consequences." After giving instructions, he passed away as well. After that, Quang Hue transformed himself into a meditation master Buddha „n; Gioi Dien reincarnated as To Dong Pha. Dong Pha, because he had practiced in his previous life, became an official. He was intelligent and wise, but also multi-talented and sentimental. He had up to seven concubines, and often used his intelligence to question the meditation masters. Later, after being persuaded by the Buddha, he returned to the Buddhist path. That's why false thoughts are so subtle that people who have practiced for a long time have to be afraid of that. Tien Duc has a saying:

Effort is neither lacking nor surplus.

All lifetimes of greed and ignorance are easy to cure!

So, when cultivators have some good realms, they should not rush to boast and be proud, they should look at the example of Gioi Dien. And don't be too quick to criticize others, but look at the example of Buddhist monk Quang Hue.

• Lethargy and subtle delusions, long-time practitioners know how to remove them. Here, we only briefly discuss how to treat the rough part. Normally, when there are many disturbing thoughts, the practitioner should sit still and meditate on Buddha. When drowsiness comes, you should stand up and meditate while walking. If you keep changing these two postures, over time these two obstacles will be eliminated. According to experience, listening to clearly note the words and phrases reciting the Buddha's name in the style of Reciting the name is probably the most effective method to counteract distractions. And, the Ceremony of reciting the name is the ultimate method to deal with the heavy hindrance of torpor.

But, each practitioner has their own experience and suitability. Above are just a few points of view to contribute to the benefits.
