noi_dung:
Section 47 - Tri Tri, Reason Tri

Reciting Buddha has Retention and Retention. According to Master Random Ich: "Retention is believing in the realm of Ultimate Bliss and Amitabha Buddha, but has not yet achieved this mind to become a Buddha, this mind to be Buddha, only deciding to pray for rebirth, earnestly reciting it like a child misses his mother and never forgets. Reasoning is believing and understanding Amitabha Buddha in the West, created by our own mind; Use the words of your mind that are ready and created by your mind as an obligatory reminder, without being distracted for a moment."

To put it simply, Recitation is the recitation of those who do not know anything about the meaning, only believe in the realm of Ultimate Bliss and Amitabha Buddha, and then sincerely recite Buddha's name to pray for rebirth. Reasoning is a way of reciting people's thoughts that also works in the same way as the above method of reciting, but the understanding of Pure Land and Amitabha Buddha are both in the true mind, due to the pure merit of the true mind.

So, what is the difference between Retention and Retention? - Of course there is. Because those who practice the Buddha's teachings see that Buddha is outside the mind, so they have the ability to deal with them and have not yet been able to understand them. People who practice according to the Doctrine of Wisdom, by realizing the true mind, are able to completely attain the form and function, that is, mindfulness is Buddha, that is, mindfulness is mind, blending with the mental scene. Let me tell you a story:

The writer's leaving the home life friend had a dream one night and saw a yellow-robed monk coming and asking: "People chant Buddha, but what is Buddha?" - Answer: "Buddha is the mind". The monk continued asking: "Try to explain to me how Buddha is the mind?" In the dream, his friend spontaneously read:

Each Buddha rosary sentence is the mind

Buddha clearly knows the mind, it's a waste of searching!

The Buddha tank harmonizes the mind with the scene

Heaven and mind are equal and Buddha is born together

Abandon your mind to follow Buddha and still dream

Accepting Buddha is an imperfect mind.

Mind and Buddha are both illusory

Buddha, the mind is extinguished to perfection.

The friend above has understood how to maintain and integrate Buddha's chant into his mind.

• There is a wrong way of thinking, which those who are inclined towards mystical theory, claiming to practice according to reason, also need to justify. Many people ignore reason, often clinging to reason: "Amitabha's self-nature, idealistic Pure Land," then deny the realm of Ultimate Bliss and the conduction of rebirth. These people theorize the scriptures about the Pure Land and say: "Amitabha is our Buddha nature; The Pure Land is a pure scene within the mind, why look outside?" This is a huge mistake in natural theory. They accept the truth and give up things, favor nature and forget appearances, rejecting the phenomena of conventional truths, not knowing that the two sides cannot be separated from each other.

According to the Mahayana Arising of Faith, the true mind has two parts: nature and form. The nature part is called the door of Truth, the appearance part is the door of birth and death; True Suchness is not separate from birth and death, birth and death is True Suchness. Therefore, Ma Minh Bodhisattva calls the part of True Suchness the Storehouse of Suchness which is truly empty, the part of birth and death the Storehouse of Suchness which is truly non-empty; Both share the same true nature. For example, the sea surface is large and wide, we cannot only accept the water but ignore the foam; Because having such an attachment means being mistaken about the phenomenon of the sea, but also not knowing what the sea is? Therefore, if one abandons the unreasonable and does not succeed, rejecting the appearance, the nature of emptiness cannot stand. Many people who have little worldly education, when studying the Mahayana sutras that talk about the Prajnaparamita principle, because they do not understand it thoroughly, often suffer from the disease of accepting "emptiness" hey. Therefore, they take the sutras that talk about appearance, such as the Pure Land Sutra or the Ksitigarbha Sutra, to theorize everything. They consider these sutras about appearances to be a means to lead the lowly ignorant people, those who believe in Pure Land or hell, to be superstitious; but in fact, it is they who are mistaken! By the way, I would like to cite a few passages of scripture to justify it, to circumvent that error of emptiness.

As the Heart Sutra says: "... Without knowledge, there is no attainment. Because he does not possess it, Bodhi Tat Doa follows Prajnaparamita, his mind is not troubled. All Buddhas of the three generations followed Prajna Paramita, so they attained the fruit of Anuttara Sam-mi-Bodhi." First he followed the ultimate truth and said "no attainment", then he followed the conventional truth and said "attainment". Feeling "good" is the attachment to having, seeing "not attaining" lost in the attachment to emptiness, so Buddhist students must skillfully understand the meaning of the sutra to enter the middle path.

In the Diamond Sutra, the Buddha said: "Whoever uses form and sound to see and seek me is following an evil path." But then He said: "Tu Bodhi! Don't think that the Tathagata did not use the form of Pācācā to attain the fruit of Anuttara Tam Mieu Tam Bodhi. Tu Bodhi! If you think: Arousing the mind of Anuttara Sam-mi Bodhi means talking about the cessation of all dharmas. Don't think like that! Why? Because of developing the mind of Anuttara Sammyak Tam Bodhi, regarding all dharmas, there is no sign of cessation." First, Buddha taught not to follow sounds and forms to find the way; but next He reminded again; Also, do not abandon sound, form, or destroy all dharmas to develop the mind to seek enlightenment. Thus, we see "the Way" neither belongs to "form", nor belongs to "emptiness"; Looking for one side is wrong. Buddhist monk Thanh Nguyen Duy Tin said: "Thirty years ago, when the old monk had not yet entered Buddhism, he saw rivers as rivers and mountains as mountains. When I met a wise man who taught me the way to practice, I saw that the river was not a river, and the mountains were not mountains. Today, when we realize enlightenment, when we enter a quiet place, we see that the river is still a river, and the mountains are still mountains. Another meditation master also described:

The sound of chickens is really the sound of the square.

The original mountain form is the pure dharma body!

Here is the hint: Forms and sounds are inherently great, we should use our minds to accept them without discrimination, neither accept nor reject them, then look for the path in emptiness. Therefore, the sentence "Amitabha's self-nature, idealistic Pure Land," It is not to deny the Pure Land and Amitabha, but to say: capture the appearance of nature, bring the application to form, to reveal the First Principle of Emptiness. In the First Meaning of Emptiness, Buddha did not even establish it, let alone other dharmas.

Tien Duc said: "Even though the principles are suddenly enlightened, the facts must be practiced step by step." Therefore, although the Zen school is said to be a practice of direct concentration, while still meditating, still focusing on the mind, still engaging in meditation, and entering and exiting concentration, all are still within the circle of expediency. And actually, the internal evidence also has steps from low to high. Only when one reaches the level of non-cultivation will one no longer use expedient methods and one can say that all dharmas are empty. If it were not like that, then even a dharma as small as a speck of dust would be real; Because near the fire you still feel hot, in the middle of snow and frost you still feel cold, a small thorn that penetrates your flesh still feels pain, what is nothing? Therefore, those who like to promote the sublime "Amitabha's self-nature, the idealistic Pure Land," Then rejecting the form of reciting the Buddha's name to pray for rebirth belongs to "Practice", you will fall into the following situation: "before stepping ashore, he quickly broke the raft," all could not help but drown in the water. In the past, those who had a deep understanding of Reason also focused on Truth, because Truth represents Reason.

The ancients said: "With the Pure Land discipline, only the wise can penetrate the nature and understand it to the end. Otherwise, it's better to practice and cling to appearances, the more you cling to it, the more miraculous it becomes!" Because the more you cling to the form, the more earnestly you pray for rebirth. Once you are born in the West, why worry about not being able to realize the true form? The issue of understanding nature and form is not the same, but if you understand one, you will understand them all. I hope you guys think wisely to avoid mistakes on your spiritual path.

Writing here, a Buddhist came to visit and asked: - "Teacher, I heard some highly advanced meditation practitioners say: The realm of Ultimate Bliss is a powerful theory, an illusion of Buddha's means of speaking, so that lowly people rely on it to believe and admire, and develop their hearts to single-mindedly recite the Buddha's name to reach the realm of one-mindedness. For example, a father has two children, one is smart and knows how to study without needing to be reminded; One of the kids was lazy and late, so his father had to persuade him, telling him that if he tried to study hard and passed the exam, he would get a nice car. A beautiful car is an illusion or a means, studying well and passing the exam is the true goal or end. Therefore, Pure Land is the practice of the ignorant common people, while the intellectuals are interested in meditation. If you understand this, then a wise person should only meditate on the mind, there is no need to follow the illusion of reciting the Buddha's name and make it a little tiring. Let the empty vehicle drive gently, don't transport it too heavy! I heard that but don't know how to answer, I hope you can explain."

The fake pen replied: - In the above hearing, there are three topics:

1. For Ultimate Bliss is an illusion, a theory.

2. Pure Land is a practice that belongs to the lower class of ordinary people.

3. Given the goal of eliminating the illusion of single-mindedness, it is said that the method of reciting the Buddha's name is as tiring as a heavy truck, not as gentle and elegant as the practice of meditation.

Regarding the first point, Ultimate Bliss is not an illusion or a theory, but a real world like this Saha world; Because Buddha never lies, and there are many people who recite Buddha's name and are reborn, now or at the time of death, and have seen that realm, as recorded in the rebirth story and Pure Land Thanh Hien Luc. In this volume, in the previous paragraph, the three quantities were explained to explain, at a glance it will be clear, there is no need to argue further.

Regarding the second point, if you think that Pure Land is not the practice of intellectuals, you are only afraid of "intellectual" wisdom. Those people just aren't strong enough to understand Pure Land. Just like when the Buddha spoke the Lotus Sutra in the past, there were up to five thousand Venerable Sravakas who testified from the First Fruits to the Four Fruits. Because they could not believe and understand, they withdrew from the Dharma assembly. These people have entered the ranks of saints, they are not ordinary people, but in the face of the sublime truth, they have no choice but to fail. If it is said that all intelligent intellectuals must practice meditation and recite Buddha's name to save the ignorant and ordinary people, why would the fourteenth Patriarch of the Zen school, Nagarjuna Bodhisattva, after attaining the First Stage of Joy, recite Buddha's name "to pray for the birth of Ultimate Bliss?" And why are there so many masters at Zen school, such as Vinh Minh, Triet Ngo, and Lien Tri, who, after participating in meditation and gaining enlightenment, turned to seek Pure Land? You must know that Buddha's Recitation is a sublime and mysterious dharma, consisting of three senses, from Buddha Thich Ton to the great Bodhisattvas such as Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Ma Minh, and Nagarjuna. Therefore, when Shakyamuni Buddha spoke the Amitabha Sutra, all the Buddhas in the six directions appeared with wide and long tongues and praised it. And in the Avatamsaka Sutra, after Lord Samantabhadra said the ten great vows, he immediately advised Bodhisattvas in the Ten Faiths, Ten Pillars, Ten Virtues, Ten Directions, Ten Grounds, and Enlightenment to all make vows to pray for rebirth in Ultimate Bliss? If the scene of Ultimate Bliss is an illusion and not real, and the Pure Land is ordinary, why do they seek rebirth? Therefore, Master Quang said: "The sublime mystery of the Buddha's Recitation method, the Patriarchs said that only Buddha and Buddha can fully understand it. Those who despise Buddha's Recitation, do not only despise the old men and women who practice Pure Land, but also despise all Buddhas and Great Bodhisattvas such as Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Ma Minh, Nagarjuna!"

Regarding the third point, please explain more clearly. The ultimate place of meditation is the True Samadhi. The ultimate point of Pure Land is Buddha Recitation Samadhi. True Samadhi is like solid gold, Buddha Reciting Samadhi is like bracelets, bracelets and beautifully carved ornaments, in which the bracelet already contains gold. Therefore, when realizing Buddha Samadhi, it includes the True Such Samadhi. True Samadhi is purely in terms of wisdom, Buddha Reciting Samadhi has wisdom and also includes merits and blessings; Because Pure Land practitioners also take pure single-mindedness as the basis, on top of that single-mindedness, there is the additional merit of reciting Buddha. But True Samadhi with Buddha Recitation Samadhi does not have to be practiced in one lifetime to achieve, it needs to be continuously practiced for many lifetimes; Especially for sentient beings in this Dharma-ending age, it is difficult to hope. Therefore, although Buddha Recitation Samadhi is the ultimate goal of Buddha Recitation, it is only secondary, and the prayer for rebirth Pure Land in one life to be irreversible is the main and necessary tenet of this sect. Therefore, the Buddha Recitation method is called the Pure Land sect. That's why, after enlightenment, meditation practitioners know that the path to enlightenment is still far away, fearing that their human life will be short and that when samsara enters another life, they will be lost, so they turn to reciting the Buddha's name to pray for rebirth. Reciting the Buddha and paying homage to the Buddha, although it is difficult, receive additional merits and blessings due to the cultivating power of both body and speech karma. Like the car from Da Lat to Saigon, the driving is not necessarily light, but if it also carries flowers and vegetables, it will return to the Capital and also have more goods. Use your diligence to recite Buddha's name to receive more blessings. That is the natural reward and reward according to the law of cause and effect. There is no need to be disadvantaged. But if there is any fatigue, it is only when you first practice. When reciting the Buddha is so mature that you become mindless, there is no fatigue at all!

The above question is also necessary, so even though it is not a decisive part, I would like to continue writing it here. There are still a lot of misunderstandings about Pure Land. Because I'm afraid of making mistakes, I'll stop writing about the justifications.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Section 48 - The One Mind, The Reason for One Mind
tom_tat: People who recite Buddha's name must diligently work hard. In the absolute state of both world and non-self, one cannot see the body or mind. In addition to cutting off all the forms of emptiness and lust, there is no realm left. Only one Buddha sentence clearly appears. Use…
noi_dung:
Section 48 - The One Mind, The Reason for One Mind

People who recite Buddha's name must diligently work hard. In the absolute state of both world and non-self, one cannot see the body or mind. In addition to cutting off all the forms of emptiness and lust, there is no realm left. Only one Buddha sentence clearly appears. This extreme use of effort, as the ancients raised the question: "In front there are fierce tigers, behind there are wolves, on the left is a high cliff, on the right is a deep abyss; In that situation, which path should the practitioner take? Tinh Tong also said: "The seven-jeweled lotus pond in front, the cauldron of oil and fire behind, the person chanting Buddha must go in the same direction." When I practice, I don't see any progress, because I'm still weak and lazy. Also in that situation, in the past, Mr. Dong Son severely reprimanded the crowd:

People now studying religion think and complain

Outside the door, wondering how many thousands!

Think of the Jade Kinh Dynasty of the Holy Lord

In the middle of the road, stop at Dong Quang pass!

If one uses effort to the extreme, without interruption for a long time, the practitioner will reach the state of one mind. This state of one-pointedness and undisturbed mind has two shallow and deep levels, called One-pointedness and One-mindedness.

• What is single-mindedness? - When the practitioner concentrates his attention on the six words of the holy name, for a long time all distracting thoughts will stop. When lying down, sitting, walking or standing, only one Buddha sentence appears, called the realm of One-pointedness of mind. This is the state of concentration of Pure Land practitioners, and is on par with the concentration of meditation practitioners.

• What is the principle of one mind? - On the One-pointedness of mind, if we go one step further and apply effort to the extreme, one day the mind will be completely empty, completely free from the mundane roots and realize the true form. At that time, the present is the West, but there is no need to worry about the realm of Ultimate Bliss. Your nature is Amitabha, and there is no need to worry about Amitabha. This is the realm of One Mind. This position is the scene of "single concentration and wisdom". of people chanting Buddha, on par with the level of enlightenment in Zen school.

• With the theory of One Mind and One Mind, Great Master Nguoi Ich has clearly distinguished it. He said: "There is no question of retention or reason; Thinking to subdue afflictions, views or thoughts or not appearing, is the realm of Single-mindedness. Without discussing the practice or reason, meditate until the mind opens, clearly see Buddha's nature, which is the realm of One Mind. One-pointedness of mind is not subject to views, thoughts or chaos. The principle of one mind is not disturbed by two boundaries." (Second side: yes, no - paragraph, often etc.)

So, there is nothing to say about the principle of single-mindedness, with single-mindedness it is not easy for people in today's world to come to this. However, with the merit of Buddha's recitation plus diligent practice, with each recitation, a part of ignorance will be destroyed and a part of blessings and wisdom will be eliminated, and gradually one will reach a good realm. And if you practice for such a long time, why don't you reach the point of enlightenment with each thought, and get a good state called "One phase starts, one phase changes"? (One time a thought arises, another time a new scene is revealed).

Therefore, even though our nature is at its end, if we really apply our efforts and level of knowledge, the One Mind Principle is not completely hopeless for us...

---o0o---

Section C. Realm of Discovery

tom_tat: On the path of cultivation, if you don't diligently apply effort, that's all. If you diligently apply effort, you will definitely have a realm. This realm has different insides and outsides. First, let's talk about the internal part, which is the Internal Scene
noi_dung:
Section 49 - Inner Realm

On the path of cultivation, if you don't diligently apply effort, that's all. If you diligently apply effort, you will definitely have a realm. This realm has different insides and outsides. First, let's talk about the inner part, which is the Inner Realm.

The inner realm is also called the self-mind realm, because this realm does not come from the outside, but is discovered by the use within the mind. People who do not clearly understand the principle "all dharmas depend on the mind" Thinking that all realms come from the outside is a wrong way of thinking. Because when the practitioner applies effort to the point of compatibility, cutting off external conditions, the seeds of the dharmas latent in the store of consciousness immediately arise. For those who recite Buddha reciting mantras, the functions of the Buddha's name and secret mantra go deep into the heart, inevitably encountering the reaction of good and evil seeds in the store of consciousness, the realm of discovery is very complicated. These scenes often appear in dreams, or even when awake while chanting Buddha's name. The Buddhists call this state "Alai da transformed."

• In a dream, if discovered by evil seeds, the practitioner either sees worms crawling out from inside him, or sees multi-legged creatures like scorpions and centipedes in his body, five or seven of which he pulls out every night; or see ghostly animals, the sights are so numerous that they are indescribable! In general, people with a lot of karma are greedy, stingy, and malicious, and often see men and women, snakes and centipedes, or other types of white color. People with a lot of karma and anger often see tigers, leopards, or strange red colors. People with a lot of delusional karma often see animals, shellfish, or other black colored creatures. However, this is only an estimate, not everything is definitely like that.

If discovered by good seeds, the practitioner sees tall trees with strange flowers, lush and solemn landscapes, nets of pearls; or find yourself eating delicious things, wearing precious clothes, in a precious palace, or gently flying through the air. In short, in the minds of sentient beings there are enough seeds of the ten dharma realms; When the good seeds appear, you will see Buddha, Bodhisattva, Nhon, and Heaven; Evil seeds appear, seeing the suffering of the three sinners. Like people who have practiced paganism in their previous lives, they often find themselves emitting a stream of magic, or going out in their souls to roam around, coming into contact with sounds that talk about Thanh and national affairs. Or sometimes when the mind is pure, in the dream you can clearly see what will happen a few days later, or five or seven months later. In general, people from previous generations practiced, and when they recited Buddha's name, they immediately saw a good realm. As for those who have a lot of karma and poor merits and blessings, when they first recite Buddha's name, they often see evil realms; If you recite for a long time, the evil signs will disappear and you will see good omens one after another.

• Regarding the scene while awake, if the practitioner uses the practice to the point of maturity, there are times when delusions suddenly stop, body and mind are free. Sometimes I chant Buddha for up to four or five hours, but I find that the time is very short, about a couple of minutes. Sometimes while reciting, strange good signs appear. Sometimes, unintentionally, the spirit suddenly feels great pleasure. There are times when we are in a peaceful state, seeing that all minds and scenes are empty. Sometimes, in a moment of seeing and hearing, I immediately realize the truth of suffering, no impermanence, no self, completely cutting off the appearance of self and others. Such appearances are indescribable!

There was a Buddhist who was sitting awake in the dark chanting Buddha's name. Suddenly, he saw two types of red and white flowers sprouting from the ground all over the house, reaching up to the edge of the bed. In the sky, the flowers fell like rain. Someone was kneeling and reciting the Buddha's name when he suddenly saw a red lotus flower appear in front of the Buddha's table, slowly blooming from the bud, then disappearing about fifteen minutes later. There was a Buddhist who was reciting Buddha's name. The surrounding world suddenly disappeared. In front of his eyes appeared a vast sea of ​​water, calm and without waves. On the surface of the sea, countless multicolored lotus flowers grew, all of them huge; Next, the sea disappears, revealing lush mountains, grass and flowers, lush ancient trees, and a magnificent pagoda; Next, the form of the mountain pagoda disappears again, revealing the scene of a pearl net, woven then broken, broken then woven again. There are a lot of scenes like that, because the writer has heard stories from fellow practitioners, but now I will only mention a few stories to clarify.

• Such scenes, called the Inner Realm or Self-Mind Realm, appear due to a light thought of peace, or due to the good seeds of the merit of reciting Buddha reciting mantras. These scenes disappear immediately when they appear. Practitioners should not accept them as real but let their minds linger on them. If you have regretful thoughts, thinking how gentle and peaceful that realm is, how dignified and beautiful it is, then dreaming about it and making it unforgettable, hoping to see it again next time, that is a huge mistake. Ancient people criticized this mindset as "scratching first and waiting for the itch." Because those scenes are only temporarily manifested by the effective use of effort, and are not real. You should know that when a person cultivates to a certain level, that realm will naturally appear. For example, every time a traveler passes a road, a different scene will appear. If a traveler has not yet reached home, but is attached to the scenery on the roadside and refuses to leave, he will definitely be afraid of the journey, and will be stranded on the road, not knowing when he will reach home and rest. The same goes for cultivators, if they are attached to the temporary realm, they will not be able to attain the real realm. If you accidentally dream to the point of delusion, you will definitely be destroyed by demons, ruining your entire life of practice.

Diamond Sutra says: "All appearances are illusory; If you see appearances that are not appearances, you see the Tathagata." (Whatever possesses the appearance of illusion; weak view of all non-appearances, i.e. view of the Tathagata). "There are generals" not "the generals have" belongs to the dharma of creation and destruction, because those appearances do not tell themselves whether they exist or not, whether they are real or false. It is only because people who have not yet realized the principle of moving thoughts and thoughts distinguish and accept that they exist, do not exist, are real, or are false, so they become false. When you enter meditation, you see a vast, empty, transparent state of concentration, free and at ease, and then give birth to thoughts of liking; or when one realizes a sublime principle and then joyfully embraces it, it also belongs to "having appearance." And already "has a general" that is, there is false hope. "Seeing the generals" is to see the appearances: good, bad, beautiful, ugly, dirty, clean, yes, no, Buddha, sentient beings, up to the five skandhas, six senses, etc. "Non-appearance", meaning to see without attachment or denial, just let it be natural. Why shouldn't it be denied? - Because although appearances are illusory, they are not empty; For example, although the shadow of the moon at the bottom of the water is not real, it does not have the illusory appearance of the shadow of the moon. Therefore, while cultivating, if you see signs appearing, don't pay attention and continue to practice; For example, a traveler sees a scene on the road, but still moves forward to quickly get home. "Seeing the Tathagata" is to see Buddha's nature, to see the way.

• In conclusion, from the above-mentioned signs to the Oneness of Mind and Oneness of Mind, all are the Inner Realms. This realm has two aspects: similarity and evidence. Similar scenes are seen temporarily and then disappear. The stage of realization is once achieved forever, because one has realized a part of Truth. Regardless of the Internal or External scene, everything similar is not the True Realm, but is called Insight Tieu That, meaning to penetrate part of the information of the true mind. People who truly seek liberation should not take the form of Thieu Tieu Tuc as the True Realm. "Understanding the Meaning" For example, in a dark and gloomy sky, suddenly there is a gust of wind that causes the dark clouds to temporarily part, revealing a bit of sunlight, then the dark clouds obscure it again. Just like the ancients rubbed a tree to get fire, before the fire flared up, there must have been the appearance of smoke. "True Realm" Like the bright sunlight in the clear sky and like a palm tree that has caught fire. However, do not underestimate Thieu Tieu Tic, because having this form, only proves that there is a True Realm. So if you work diligently from that level, the True Realm is not far away.

---o0o---

tom_tat: The external realm is a scene that does not appear from within, but comes from the outside. Or there are practitioners who see Buddha or Bodhisattva appearing in person, preaching the Dharma, exhorting and praising them. Or there is a practitioner who, while reciting the Buddha's name, suddenly opens his mind and sees...
noi_dung:
Section 50 - Outside Realms

The external realm is a scene that does not appear from within, but comes from the outside. Or there are practitioners who see Buddha or Bodhisattva appearing in person, preaching the Dharma, exhorting and praising them. Or there are practitioners who, while reciting Buddha, suddenly open their minds and immediately see the realm of Ultimate Bliss. Or there are practitioners who are meditating and see the gods coming, clasping their hands and circling around to show respect, or invite them to go for a walk. Or there are practitioners who see ghosts coming to ask for refuge. Or there are practitioners who, when their cultivation level is high, are challenged and disturbed by external demons...

• Once upon a time, there was a Buddhist who had a dull nature, but often revered and recited Avalokitesvara. One night I dreamed that Bodhisattva came to tell me so I often studied the following verse, and over time I would be enlightened:

Great wisdom arises in the mind

Where to look in the heart?

Accomplish all meanings

No neck, no needle!

• As recently as the Republic of China, there was a layperson in Jiang Am Nam who, in the third month of the year Ren Than (1932), saw the scene of Ultimate Bliss when he was sick. He struggled to write a letter to his brother, layman Giang Diet Vien, roughly as follows: "I'm in serious pain. At about three o'clock in the morning on the twenty-fifth of March, after a thunderstorm and heavy rain, the sky was as clear as day. In the West, the world of Ultimate Bliss suddenly appeared, immeasurably bright. I see seven solemn treasures, treasures, stupas, and countless precious signs. Buddha sat in the middle of nowhere and told me to come and pay my respects. But when I arrived in front of the Buddha, the golden form of Amitabha Buddha gradually moved away, the echoing voice was very small, and all the realms disappeared. It's probably because my concentration is still weak, but from now on I'm confident that the scene of the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss is real..."

• Also during the Republic of Korea period, there was a layperson Liu Kainan, nicknamed Mr. Tay Tieu. Before his rebirth, the gods invited him to U Minh to apply for office; Next, when they saw the gods inviting them to heaven, the lay people strictly refused, saying: "Being an official easily creates karma, heaven's blessings come to an end. I only wish to be reborn in Ultimate Bliss." A few days later the layman was reborn.

• A nun familiar with pseudo-monastic writing near Da Lat. After reciting mantras, she was sitting quietly when she suddenly saw two messengers with the demeanor and attire of gods coming to respectfully invite them up to the mountain to visit the scene. In concentration, the nun asked: "I'm tall, I'm weak, how can I walk?" A messenger replied: "Don't be shy, I have a way." Immediately took a tree branch like a willow branch, lightly hit the nun's body and told her to follow. She suddenly felt her body floating above the tip of the blade of grass, at the last moment moving up the mountain. Coming here, we see scenes of elegant and graceful peacocks, peacocks spreading beads and dancing, and in the distance there is a palace with cascading floors. Just then, the housekeeper in the back house dropped something with a loud noise. The nun suddenly woke up, her senses disappeared, and she felt her thighs still sore and tired.

The general characteristics listed above are all called the External Realm. Someone asked: "Seeing Buddha and seeing lotus flowers, is that a ghost scene?" Please reply: "If cause and effect match, it's not a ghost scene. Because the Pure Land sect belongs to the "right door", people who recite Buddha's name when they first develop their mind enter from the place where the appearance exists, praying to see the holy realm in the West. When you see a good appearance, it is the effect that comes to respond to the cause, cause and effect are compatible, is it not a demon scene? On the contrary, like Zen school from a place of "no subject" When you enter, when you develop the mind to practice, all appearances are swept away, even the Buddha appearance and the Dharma appearance are all destroyed. The meditator does not seek to see the Buddha or the lotus flower, but the appearance of the Buddha and the lotus flower appears, which is an inappropriate cause and effect. Indeed, there is no cause to discover, that is the true demon scene. Therefore, practitioners of meditation always raise the sword of wisdom, demons come to kill demons, Buddha comes to kill Buddha, entering the void, not tolerating any form at all.

However, that is only said to new practitioners, especially those who practice high meditation, sometimes they see signs but they are not demons. Because those who have practiced meditation for many lifetimes, when their minds are opened, they can see the evil realms and paradise to the Pure Land and Impure Land of the ten directions; Because the worlds in all ten directions are in the light of the true mind. And Pure Land practitioners sometimes see signs, but they are ghost scenes, which the following section of the Demon Realm will clearly explain.

In conclusion, the Inner realm and the Outer realm are estimates based on the level of the person still on the path of practice. When one has attained enlightenment, the mind is the scene, the scene is the mind, all things are one with us, there is no inside or outside.

---o0o---

tom_tat: As mentioned above, people who recite Buddha's name sometimes see appearances that are actually demons; This is only for cases where cause and effect do not correspond. For example, a person who is contemplating Buddha's appearance suddenly sees the appearance of a beautiful woman. Those who diligently recite…
noi_dung:
Section 51 - The Demon Realm

As mentioned above, people who recite Buddha's name sometimes see appearances that are actually demons; This is only for cases where cause and effect do not correspond. For example, a person who is contemplating Buddha's appearance suddenly sees the appearance of a beautiful woman. Those who diligently recite the Buddha's name hope to see beautiful landscapes in the West, but suddenly they see an area of filthy houses, men, women, and animals running back and forth. The person expected to see a precious lotus flower, but suddenly saw a small carriage. Because cause and effect do not match like that, we know it is a ghost scene. There are five cases to distinguish between ghost scenes and real scenes as follows:

1. The cause and effect scenes are inconsistent, contemplating one form but seeing another, seeking one form but showing another, as just mentioned above. And again, the scenes that appear are not the same as described in the sutras, they are all ghost scenes.

2. All Buddhas, Bodhisattva's heart is pure and compassionate, so even though the appearance of demons and spirits comes as a challenge, we still feel peaceful and pure. On the contrary, the original karma of demons is evil affliction, so even though the appearance of Buddha comes to advise, we feel agitated, impatient, and restless.

3. Buddha's light makes us feel soft and cool, without shadows or glare. The ghost's light makes our eyes painful, restless, and shadowy. Therefore, the Lankavatara Sutra says:

Buddha ground is supreme

Pure and dignified color

The signal is like a blazing fire

Light comes everywhere

Brilliant without hurting the eyes

Rotate the three realms.

4. The teachings of the Buddha, Bodhisattva, are in accordance with the scriptures and follow the truth. The ghost's words are contrary to reason and not in accordance with the Buddha's teachings.

5. When the ultimate form appears and wants to test it, the practitioner only recites the Prajnaparamita Heart Sutra with the right mind, or with the mind reciting Buddha's mantras. If it is a holy scene, the more you recite it, the clearer it becomes, because real gold is not afraid of fire. If it is a demonic realm, if you recite it for a while it will disappear, because evil cannot encroach on righteousness.

• You must test all five things above, not just one or two things. Because there are heavenly demons or gods who follow foreign sects and want to lead us towards their path, they pretend to appear as Buddha Bodhisattva to preach the Dharma. Although their practice is not the path to liberation, they have good karma, or quite high meditation power, so the aura emitted also makes us cool and gentle. Their preaching style sometimes also advises doing good, observing the precepts, fasting and reciting Buddha's name, but there are a few discrepancies that are not consistent with the Buddha's scriptures. You have to carefully evaluate and understand the teachings to know. For example, they also advise being vegetarian and chanting Buddha's name, but they teach to practice Buddha's chanting throughout the whole body called "turning the wheel of dharma". to open the Nham and Doc channels, and open Ne Hoan Cung. This is the teaching style of pagan demons. Or there are ghosts that appear as noble monks: "Bronze Buddha and cement Buddha cannot hold water, because when they enter the water they must sink; Buddha statues and wooden Buddhas cannot withstand fire, because when exposed to fire, they will burn; Only Buddha's mind is not damaged by anything. To cultivate Buddha's pure mind, there is no need to cultivate body and speech; So even if you eat meat and drink wine, have a wife and children, it is harmless. Practices of body and speech such as observing the precepts, fasting, chanting sutras, reciting mantras, reciting the Buddha, are useless, restrictive ascetic practices." This is the teaching of the long-term enchantress, or the demon of desire. There are pagan demons who have quite high cultivating abilities and can use the power of meditation equipment to help the practitioner's body and mind be at peace within seven days, or twenty-one days. But their way of preaching the Dharma is not transcendent, ending up in a circle of ego.

• The ancients said: "Seeing that a ghost is not a demon, the demon immediately self-destructs; Seeing that the monster is not a monster, the monster will defeat itself." This sentence means: If you see a ghost but your heart is not disturbed by fear, you keep your mindfulness steadfast, or even think of Buddha, that ghost cannot do anything and will go away on its own. Not only should you be like that when you see ghosts and ghosts, but even when you get some results from your practice, or see a winning form, you should not be too sad, surprised, or happy. For example, if we have a pearl that we dropped at the bottom of a lake, because the water is turbid, we search for it forever and still find it missing. Now that the water has settled and been found again, that pearl was originally owned, so why should we be surprised and happy? If a cultivator's mind is not calm and is too sad, he will be haunted by the ghosts of compassion, making him cry endlessly. As if he was too happy, he was possessed by a demon of joy, making him laugh like crazy. Again, even though the practitioner recites the Buddha's name, he also hopes to see the holy scene, but he should not be too dreamy and wishful thinking, because reciting means he has already prayed. You should keep a calm state of mind, "pray without praying, don't pray but pray", so as not to be disturbed by your wishes. If you just recite the Buddha's mind for a long time, if you recite the pure path for a long time, you will be able to see the holy scene. If you keep wishing, that is delusion, and demons will take the opportunity to creep in and destroy you.

• Around the end of the Qing dynasty and the beginning of the Republic of China, in China there was a man named Wei Tich Phu, who was a meditation friend of the layperson Duong Nhan Son. Wei Tich Phu practiced meditation for nearly thirty years, and one day he suddenly gained the Divine Eye. Initially, he saw things outside the walls, then clearly saw things around a few dozen miles as if they were right in front of his eyes. Knowing that he had attained the Divine Eye, he was very surprised and happy! At first I could only see it, then I could clearly hear the sounds of people and animals in the distance. That is Thien Nhi Thong's discovery. You can see and hear things thousands of miles away. After that, he still saw, heard and understood clearly the things that had not yet been discovered. This is the testimony of Tuc Mang Thong. At that time, Hong Tu Toan's faction of the Taiping Thien Quoc group had not yet begun to attack the Qing Dynasty, but Wei Tich Phu foresaw that the war that happened in Guangxi would gradually spread to Suzhou, with countless people dying. Because he witnessed many tragic states of death, he was so moved that everyone he met cried and said: "The great chaos is about to arrive. The people will suffer pitiful suffering. What can we do?" At that time, when everyone heard him say that, everyone thought he was crazy. Layman Duong Nhan Son at that time was often close to him in the capital, so he knew this well. Then the enemy actually happened. When the chaos was over, the layman Duong Nhan Son met Wei Tich Phu in Duong Chau several times and saw that he was still crying. Later Nhan Son met layman Dinh blessings Bao, narrated the incident and said: "It's a tragic scene haunted by ghosts. When cultivating effectively, the Thien Eye Insight accidentally discovers, so one should reflect on one's own nature and not let the physical world sway it. You should know that our supernatural powers are still available to us, and we should not be too happy or surprised, thinking it is strange."

• In Truc Song Tuy But Luc, Master Lien Tri recounted the story:

- A meditation monk built a monastery near a stream. One night while meditating, he heard two demons sitting on the bank of a stream talking to each other: "Tomorrow in the late afternoon, if someone wears an iron crown and crosses this stream bridge, I will drown him instead." The other demon said: "I'm happy for you to be able to escape. I still have to endure the cold and wait for another two years before someone takes my place." The meditation monk listened and took note. The next afternoon, a heavy rain fell, the water flooded the bridge stream. It was raining again, and sure enough, someone was wearing a cast iron pan on his head, trying to cross the stream bridge to get home. The monk immediately returned and explained clearly what he had heard. This person returned in shock. That evening, the yogi heard the demon say: "I was about to escape but this monk sabotaged me. Tonight I have to take revenge!" After listening, the monk immediately regained concentration and saw the ghost coming in and out and walking around the hut several times as if searching for him. Due to his concentration, the demon searched and could not find the meditation master, and finally, discouraged, left.

Above are two "tragic" stories. and "reject ghosts". Please write this down for all of you to be more aware on the path of meditation.

---o0o---

tom_tat: The three classes Internal Realm, External Realm, and Demonic Realm had just been written. A visiting friend saw that the author was reviewing it and asked to read it to him. After hearing it, this person asked to explain more about the types of ghosts so that...
noi_dung:
Section 52 - Types of Demons

The three classes Internal Realm, External Realm, and Demonic Realm had just been written. A visiting friend saw that the author was reviewing it and asked to read it to him. After hearing about it, this person asked to clarify more about the types of demons so that his fellow practitioners could know and prevent them. Actually, in the above three sections, we talked about the realms in general, including the demon realm; If the practitioner grasps the essence, he can maintain his mind and deal with all destructive conditions. But according to that request, I would like to briefly present the types of ghosts as follows:

"Ma" In Sanskrit, it is called Ma La, and in Chinese it is translated as Sat, because it often steals merit and kills the wise life of practitioners. "Ma" It also points out the destructive conditions that cause the practitioner to lose his or her mind, become hysterical, lose mindfulness, or give birth to wrong views, do evil, and end up falling into depravity. Things that give rise to the merit of wisdom and bring sentient beings to Nirvana are called Buddha things. Things that destroy good roots, causing sentient beings to suffer and fall into the samsara cycle of life and death, are Demonic deeds. The longer one practices, the higher the path becomes, and the more powerful and dangerous demons become. Although there are many demons, there are only three main types: Demons of Afflictions, Demons of External Demons and Demons of Heaven.

• The Demon of Afflictions refers to the afflictions of greed, anger, ignorance, delusion, contempt, doubt, and evil views; until the ghosts: five warms, six nirvanas, twelve senses, eighteen precepts. This type of demon is also called Inner Demon. It is caused by confusion and confusion, so we must use enlightenment to eliminate it with a true, clear mind. Ordinary people themselves have their own karma, and because of the karma they live in the same environment, the people around them have many evil personalities and karma obstacles, so they can easily give rise to afflictions. Some people cannot stand the attraction of the five senses, so they fall. Some people are saddened by adversity and their will to progress is destroyed. These events cause people who practice lightly to become sad and resentful, causing illness; If it is severe, you will become discouraged and abandon your religion, or become frustrated and self-destruct; Even more dangerous, everyone who leaves the home life lay loses all beauty, avoids hatred, gives rise to disdain and criticism, does not believe in cause and effect, does evil and then falls into the third realm.

To treat this demon, practitioners must consider afflictions as illusory, agitated, hot, binding, dark, and only cause suffering to others and themselves. By eliminating afflictions, we will return to our true mind, freedom, liberation, coolness, calmness, clarity, and mysterious joy. For delusion from the five skandhas up to the eighteen precepts, you should also contemplate like that. In the Lotus Sutra, the Buddha said: "You should not be greedy for sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, or coarse dharmas. If you indulge in greed, you will definitely be burned by it." Once upon a time Lord Manjushri asked a goddess: "How do you view the eighteen precepts?" The goddess replied: "It's like seeing a fire burning the world!" These are words of caution to eliminate the demons of afflictions.

If the demon of affliction or the Inner demon cannot be subdued, it will definitely attract the external demon to destroy it. The old saying: "Inside the door there is a little man, outside the door there is a little man coming. Inside the door there is a gentleman, outside the door a gentleman comes." Just like when a thief digs into a corner and wants to enter the house, the homeowner often calmly reprimands him, so he must be afraid and leave. If the homeowner is frightened and begs, that is the attitude that advises bringing thieves into the house.

• Foreign Demons are demons that love the outside world. When a cultivator has a little practice, he will be challenged and disturbed by it. This species can be divided into three classes: Dad Ma, Ai Ma and Nao Ma.

1. Father Ghost is a ghost that likes to terrorize people. This ghost often takes the form of a tiger, wolf, snake, hiss, or other strange ferocious animals, or a terrifying devil to scare the practitioner. These appearances are infinitely illusory, or have no head, many heads, many arms, many eyes; either a human body with an animal head, an animal body with a human head, or holding a weapon, or breathing red fire. If the practitioner is frightened, it will destroy his mindfulness and sometimes cause him to go crazy. Encountering this scene, you should think that all appearances are false. Demons can only destroy the illusory body but cannot destroy the true mind. Thinking like that, then calm down without fear of death, calmly concentrate on reciting Buddha or reciting mantras, it will withdraw on its own.

2. Ai Ma is a demon that incites desire and lust until the mind is corrupted by the five senses. They took the form of beautiful naked men and women; or pictures of parents, brothers, and loved ones; until Buddha's body, Bodhisattva's good and dignified appearance to encourage. If people like delicious food, they will turn into mountains and seas with fragrant flavors and offer them; People love treasures, they appear as strange animals with pearls in their mouths to offer. Depending on what the practitioner likes, it will immediately appear. They can use magical power to help practitioners gain evil concentration, evil wisdom, eloquence, and magical powers to know the past and future. Those who do not understand believe that they have attained enlightenment; they are all convinced; But in reality, the other person's mind was crazy and he specialized in doing magic to bewitch the world.

There was a Vietnamese monk who lived at Bang Long Pagoda in Laos. While meditating, he saw a group of naked beauties holding hands and dancing. The monk could not calm his mind, so he sincerely recited the Buddha's name, and that appearance disappeared.

Once upon a time, at Chung Nam mountain temple in China, there was a monk who was engaged in meditation. When it was cold and hungry, he thought about eating; Suddenly I saw a young woman bringing food to making offerings. The young woman knelt down and put the food into the bowl, asking the monk to eat it immediately so it wouldn't get cold and lose its taste. The monk was hungry and wanted to eat it right away, but he thought it was not yet time to eat it, so he patiently told him to put it aside for now, wait until the right time and then eat it. When the young woman heard this, she seemed angry and left. Giây lâu sau đúng ngọ, sư giở bát ra thấy trong ấy toàn là dòi bò lúc nhúc. Only then did he wake up, knowing that as soon as he had false thoughts, he immediately received a demonic state; Luckily, thanks to a little concentration, I was able to avoid eating dirty food and breaking the precept of killing.

Another monk also practiced meditation in the mountains. Seeing that he was alone and lonely, he had the delusion that he wanted a few people to stay with him for fun. Just then, an old woman led two beautiful young girls, claiming to live at the foot of the mountain in the village, to the hermitage to pray for religious teachings. The monk initially had no doubts and immediately taught the Dharma. After going back and forth like that for a long time, one day the old woman asked for two girls to be her attendants to take care of the food and water to help the monk feel less tired. When the monk heard this, he suddenly felt strange and immediately refused. Those three people seemed embarrassed and left. The monk secretly watched around a corner and suddenly lost sight. When he came to see, the road had ended, and there were no houses. He only saw three ancient trees, one big and two small. He thought and knew that this was an ancient goblin acting as a monster; I want to cut it down with a hammer or burn it with a fire to end the disaster. Just thinking about that, I suddenly saw three people appearing, praying for repentance and asking for their lives.

Therefore, knowing that when the mind is calm and still, illusions arise, practitioners must remember this.

3. Brain Demon is a type of demon that specializes in disrupting and confusing practitioners. There are celestial species, each coming at its own time. Roughly, there are three species every hour, and at twelve o'clock there are thirty-six types of celestial beasts. When the Tiger comes, all will be tigers, leopards, and bears; Now that America is coming, it's cats, rabbits, and foxes; When the Dragon comes, there will be dragons, fish, and dragons... According to Zazen Meditation, there is a demon named Du La Kiet Chi in China called Doi Dich, with a head and face like a pipa, four eyes, two mouths, and often likes to stir up trouble for practitioners. They wait while people are chanting, turning into worms, or crawling all over their heads and faces; or stick to your mouth, nostrils, eyes, or ears; or crawl into the practitioner's armpit or abdomen and bite or sting. Sometimes they ring into the ears, making a loud, painful noise; Or suddenly hug someone and search but can't find them. They also turn out that the five senses are either favorable, unfavorable, or unfavorable, changing unpredictably, causing the practitioner to become confused and unable to perceive, easily losing concentration. If you want to deal with the thirty-six species of star beasts, reprimand them according to the time they call their names; With the Doi Dich ghost, you should recite the three rules and five precepts or the duty precepts, because they are demons that commit the crime of breaking the precepts. By doing so, they immediately disappear. Or the general treatment is to focus your mind on right concentration, or concentrate on reciting Buddha's mantras, they will disappear.

Encountering too many demonic obstacles, the ancients also had the method of buying two mirrors, then entering retreat for forty-nine days, specializing in chanting the Great Compassion mantra or Chuan De blessing mantra into the mirror. When finished, hang two mirrors high up and tilt down where you usually sit and recite, one in front of you, one behind you. If a ghost comes and is immediately captured and appears in the mirror, then the practitioner can chase them away or punish them as they wish. This magic mirror needs to be cleaned with a clean cloth and blessed with mantra once in a while. Doing so not only reminds of spiritual purity, but also increases fulfillment. This is the way to use mirrors to treat internal and external demons according to the experience of predecessors.

To further expand, foreign demons are also demons from the pagan sect. According to the observations of the author and many of his companions, those who practiced paganism in their previous or current lives then returned to Buddhism; or those who only rely on the Three Jewels, but in the past their parents and grandparents all followed the family, and are often disturbed by external demons. Because the practice of pagans does not leave behind the afflictions of existence, but is still within the cycle of self-centeredness and greed for power and fame, pagans often gather in cliques and do not want people who are more or less connected to their faction to practice other religions. The author has a friend who leaves the home life, has a gentle and gentle nature, but when he practices, he is constantly destroyed by foreign demons. It's a pity that this friend still has the seeds of paganism and does not have the will to use Buddha's Dharma to deal with evil Dharma. While suffering from demonic destruction, he went to many places to seek salvation with practitioners of other sects. In the end, he completely strayed back to paganism, on the outside he was a monk, but on the inside he specialized in cultivating the sutras, rejecting the payment of homage to the Buddha chanting sutras, calling it attachment to appearances.

There was also a female Buddhist who had a very good character, but was often harassed by external demons. One day, while practicing, she was surrounded by pagan demons and heard voices saying: "Your parents were all practitioners of our Five Elements sect, why don't you return to your original roots and follow Buddhism?" She was so scared that she recited Buddha's words. With each sentence she recited Buddha, she felt a light emitting and covering her body. The ghosts could not do anything. They angrily said: "Don't rely on Buddha's magic to become arrogant, our elders will come here to show you the tricks!" Having finished speaking, they immediately retreated. Then she suddenly heard the voice of a good angel saying: "They are jealous because she took refuge in the Three Jewels, not following the religion of her ancestors but worshiping them. Right now, both of your hands should form the Vajra Fist mudra, press your thumb on the base of your ring finger and clench it tightly. Just keep it like that and sincerely recite mantras or recite Buddha's name forever, because in a moment one of their elders will come here, use the five lightning magic to beat and capture her soul. There were so many of them, I only helped a little, because I couldn't chase them away. Your strength is limited, I'm afraid I won't be able to fight back for a long time. It's better to go to a temple to practice to avoid disaster." She immediately followed the instructions, clasped her hands in the mudra and recited the Great Compassion mantra. Suddenly, a loud noise was heard, then there was a lightning strike from above, as heavy as a hammer, burning and tingling all over the head. She immediately let go of all thoughts, tried her best to recite the mantras, no longer knowing what the outside world was like. After a while, listening to the silence around her, her body and mind returned to a normal, peaceful state.

After that, the girl went to the temple, but because her relative was old or sick and no one took care of her, she was forced to return home to take care of her livelihood. After a long time without seeing each other again, the writer heard that she often talked about nonsense, and claimed to be sick. Knowing that she couldn't resist, she was possessed by a ghost. He secretly lamented and lamented! Therefore, those who were previously associated with foreign sects and later returned to practice Buddhahood should look at the above example and pay careful attention.

• Thien Ma is a type of demon in the world of Tha Hoa Tu Tu, belonging to the sixth level of the Six Desires heaven. This type of ghost has blessings, enjoys the highest mystical joy of the five senses, considers it a scene of absolute pleasure, holds power over lust, and does not want anyone to escape that scope. When the practitioner reaches a fairly high level of cultivation, the light of the mind is revealed, the light shines through the Tha Hoa heaven, causing the demon palace to vibrate. They immediately discover it and, fearing that someone will be liberated and their relatives will be reduced, they seek to destroy it. They appear in many scenes, either threatening, or persuading, or supporting evil concentration, evil wisdom, and magical powers in order to deceive; They took turns stalking each other, never leaving for a moment, waiting for a convenient opportunity. If the practitioner has a single flaw, they will immediately be possessed by them, incited to do immoral things, and the monastic life will be considered ruined. In the Treatise on the Origin of Faith, Ma Minh Dai Si once advised:

"While practitioners meditate, they are often disturbed by heavenly demons, pagans, or demons. They appear in horrifying forms to terrorize, or as beautiful men and women hoping to seduce. Sometimes they embody Buddha, Bodhisattva or Devas with all good and solemn appearances; or say Dharani subjects; or say the Dharma giving, maintaining the precepts, patience, diligence, meditation, wisdom; or say that all dharmas are equal, empty, formless, wishless, praising the state of having no resentment, no body, no cause or effect, empty ultimate goal, and saying that this is true Nirvana... Or they help the practitioner know his/her past life, all the way through the past and future (satisfaction of life), clearly understand everyone's thoughts (perception of other minds), to the point of achieving unhindered eloquence. They cause cultivators to be greedy for worldly fame and fortune, have an erratic personality, often get angry, laugh often, love to sleep, have many illnesses, be easily hurt by emotions, sometimes be very diligent, and sometimes be lazy and lazy. Or they cause the practitioner to have doubts and disbelief, to worry too much, to abandon the basic practice and return to practicing miscellaneous practices, to indulge in negative things in the world. Or they make the practitioner somewhat similar to Samadhi, being able to stay in concentration from one day to seven days, with a happy body and mind, not knowing hunger or thirst; But that is due to the power of pagans' evil enlightenment, not true Samadhi. Or it causes the practitioner to eat and drink in moderation, sometimes more, sometimes less, and his face changes. When encountering scenes like the above, practitioners must use wisdom to observe, try to maintain mindfulness, and not give rise to attachments that lead to getting lost in the net of evil. You have to be persistent like that to be able to stay away from evil obstacles."

• In conclusion, if we put it more simply, there are only Inner Demons and Outer Demons; Heavenly demons also belong to the External Demon species. But the reason for creating Heavenly Demon into a separate category is because we want practitioners to pay attention to its subtle and dangerous destruction. In addition to the Demon of Affliction, the Demon of External Evil, and the Demon of Heaven as above, in the scriptures there is also talk of the Demon of Sickness and the Demon of Death. Because the pain of illness often causes the practitioner to reduce his or her practice, but if he or she has not practiced very well, death can cause the person to lose the path and fruition, so it is called "ghost". But the Demon of Disease and the Demon of Death, the general idea of the obstacles of illness and death of the four elements on the path of practice, do not have the destructive nature of causing trouble to kill the spiritual mind in the sense of "demons". honest. Therefore, it is not briefly mentioned here.

The cultivating power of people today is mostly destroyed by the Demons of Affliction or External Demons, not enough for the Demons of Heaven to take action. This type of demon only comes to highly cultivated people. If Heavenly Demon decides to destroy it, those with mediocre cultivation will have no hope of escaping. In the Shurangama Sutra, because the path of practice has many dangers, the Buddha advises practitioners engaged in meditation to simultaneously maintain secret mantras, so that thanks to divine power, they can escape evil and achieve true concentration. „n Master Quang said: "At first glance, it seems that the Shurangama Sutra has a different point of view than Pure Land, but when you think deeply, you see that this sutra invisibly praises Pure Land. Why? Because those who have attained the third holy fruit of Ana Ham, can still be corrupted by demons; then reciting the Buddha to pray for birth in the Pure Land becomes even more important, in the light of Amitabha's protection there are no more evil spirits."

Therefore, considering the path of practice, when one has not yet been born into Ultimate Bliss, cultivating Pure Land can also cause demonic obstacles. But most of it is because the practitioner does not understand the teachings and does not treat the mind well, allowing the Inner Demons to arise, attracting the External Demons to destroy them. If you can keep your mind calm, then with the power and merit of the good name, external demons cannot do anything, and afflictions will gradually be eliminated. Therefore, people who practice Pure Land, if they have any demon realms, are very few. On the contrary, people practicing meditation show many demons because they rely only on self-reliance. A meditation practitioner must meet the following five conditions to achieve success: One, is pure morality; Second, the nature is quick and clear; Third, we must clearly understand morality and skillfully distinguish good, evil, true, and false appearances; Four, strong will and steadfastness, and five, one must rely on a good person who is well-versed in the scriptures and has many years of experience practicing meditation to ask for guidance. If you lack those five conditions, you are susceptible to disaster. Tien Duc said: "Dry Moc Tang Tien Tu Tu Da!" This sentence means: In meditation, there are many opportunities to go astray. Therefore, if you want to practice meditation to be successful, you must be a person with superior wisdom. The ancient masters of the meditation sect, when transmitting the Dharma, also advised: "Non-superior and superior. Don't promise and accept easily." (Non-superior. Kidney animals despise promises). This statement is enough to prove the above comment.

In the Treatise on Arising Faith, after combining the general essence of the Mahayana dharma and presenting the path of practice, Ma Minh Bodhisattva said: "The Saha world is filled with afflictions and strong, true faith is difficult to maintain, it is not often that we meet the Buddha and listen to the Dharma, the path of practice is filled with many dangers and obstacles. You should know that the Tathagata has superior means, teaching you to seek rebirth in the Pure Land in other places. As the scriptures say: If you concentrate on reciting Amitabha Buddha and practice dedicating merit to seek rebirth in the West, you will return to the world of Ultimate Bliss. You will often see the Buddha listening to the Dharma and will no longer regress. If the practitioner follows this path of practice, he will definitely enter the right concentration."

As above, we see that concentrating on Buddha's thoughts is a miraculous means to escape evil and quickly achieve right concentration.

-ooOoo-

Chapter VIII: Eighth Essentials - Reciting the Buddha Must Be Long-lasting Without Interruption

Khai De:

It's sunny and rainy again

Drowning in joy and sadness

The world's injuries are lost!

Remember my childhood

Ancient tree next to the house

Play and sing with the children.

Then ask Hoang Mai

Find the Lotus path

Medium blue hair with silver streaks.

A stick of incense

A Western ideology

Waiting in the sky to hear the music!

The human body is easily lost

Buddha's teachings are difficult to listen to

Diligent advice on the path to liberation.

Reciting is not difficult

It's difficult to last long

Pray to be reborn in Ultimate Bliss.

Long lasting is not difficult

It is difficult to stay single-minded

You will see lotus flowers on the upper floors!
