Section A. Weaknesses of Pure Land

tieu_de: Section 53 - Must Remember Your Will To Be Diligent
tom_tat: Reciting the Buddha's name, if you want to maintain lasting diligence, you must have a solid stance. That stance is: Remember the purpose of your practice. For example, farmers, for the purpose of having a lot of rice or crops to feed their families, should...
noi_dung:
Section 53 - Must Remember Your Will To Be Diligent

Reciting the Buddha's name, if you want to maintain lasting diligence, you must have a solid stance. That stance is: Remember the purpose of your practice. For example, farmers, for the purpose of having a lot of rice or crops to feed their families, should endure hard work in the sun and rain, deep plowing and hoeing. Scholars, for the purpose of passing high exams, to make their parents look good and have glory in life, have to stay up late and get up early to diligently study, even though they are tired, they are not discouraged. The same goes for practitioners, today's deeds are to reach the goal of self-liberation and salvation for others in the future. Master Triet Ngo, a master of virtue and thorough knowledge of both teachings and sects, gave sixteen words, which can be called the core of the Pure Land discipline. Those sixteen words are as follows: "For the sake of birth and death, develop the heart of Bodhi, take deep vows, and recite the name Buddha." We are in the path of samsara and are subject to many sufferings, so we must quickly seek escape from the cycle of birth and death. This urgent issue has been briefly discussed before. But our own liberation is still limited; We need to develop the mind to seek the Supreme Bodhi, to save ourselves and all sentient beings to the ultimate liberation. In the past, Shakyamuni Buddha preached the Dharma for forty-nine years and discussed the sutras for more than three hundred conferences, and this was no exception. Because of the birth and death of Bodhi, the easy way without danger to quickly bring us to that goal is nothing more than "taking deep faith and vows, reciting the name Buddha."

Those who don't know morality can't help it. A person who knows this principle, but does not try to practice it, is not betraying Buddha's great grace and is wasting his spiritual nature in vain! Therefore, we must diligently practice reciting the Buddha's name for a long time, and not gradually interrupt it. The ancients said:

This body is not counted in this life.

How long do we have to wait to save ourselves?

If we promise to practice in our next life, is it any different from someone who is addicted to talking about dreams? In terms of the world, it's like someone who, for the sake of lust, has to wade through the cold wind and fog, cross the dusty fields, regardless of danger, to find a date. It's like a gambler who, because he's passionate about winning, gives up food and sleep, forgets heat and cold, and sometimes dares to sit for two or three days and nights. Ordinary people are still like that because of a little lust; Those who practice for a noble purpose, are they not as good as those people? Therefore, when practicing, if we are still lazy and interrupted, still afraid of hardships and hardships, and greedy for pleasure and sleep, it is because we have not maintained a firm stance and are not sincere in helping ourselves and others.

Years pass quickly, impermanence is unpredictable, human life is easily lost, Buddha's teachings are difficult to hear; Practitioners must remember this point, bringing the word "suffering" and "die" Stick it on the eyebrows to often stimulate self-attack.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Section 54 - Dharma Door to Escape Birth and Death in One Lifetime
tom_tat: Throughout the ten directions of the world, there are roughly only two segments: Pure Land and Ue Do. Pure Land is the pure and solemn realms of the Buddha. Once born, they will definitely end the cycle of birth and death and will gradually attain sainthood. Ue Do, are the…
noi_dung:
Section 54 - Dharma Door to Escape Birth and Death in One Lifetime

Throughout the ten directions of the world, there are roughly only two segments: Pure Land and Ue Do. Pure Land is the pure and solemn realms of the Buddha. Once born, they will definitely end the cycle of birth and death and will gradually attain sainthood. Impure Land, the realms from the realm to the body and mind of sentient beings are impure, sentient beings there still have to go up and down in the six realms, suffering samsara.

Human beings in this Saha and Impurity realm, if they only practice the five precepts and ten good deeds and other good deeds without reciting the Buddha's name, they will be as unlucky as the Buddha. Because of lack of affinity with the Buddha, the anasrava seed in the eighth consciousness lacks the ability to originate, so even if one cultivates good karmas, at most they will only be born in heaven, not return to the Pure Land. Although the lifespan in the heavenly realms is long, it is still limited. When the blessings expire, a period of life and death ends, and depending on karma, one is reborn elsewhere. If there is still good karma belonging to the top ten good qualities, depending on being born in the lower or higher heavens. Ten good middle-class karma, birth in the human world. Low-rank ten good karma, born in the Asura world. If the bad karma belongs to the lower ten evil karma, then one will fall into the animal world. The ten evil karma of the middle level is born in the realm of hungry ghosts. High-rank ten evil karma, falling into hell.

Living beings are rooted in ego, from which good and evil karmas of the six paths arise, so depending on the maturity of each type of seed, they must undergo ups and downs of samsara. In the samsara life, karma is easy to create, good conditions are difficult to cultivate, so the time to fall into the evil path is very long, and the time to be born into the heavenly path is very short. the Buddha lamented: "Sentient beings often take the three evil paths as their homeland!" Therefore we can predict: "All sentient beings, if they do not return to the Pure Land of all Buddhas, must remain in the Impure Land. Being in Ue Do, with bad and evil circumstances and many obstacles, with the end of human life, sooner or later one must fall into the evil path. And, if you want to be born in Buddha's Pure Land, you must recite Buddha's name."

• Someone asked: "The path of liberation has many paths, so why must we recite Buddha's name?" If you reflect on this point, you will understand it yourself, but please answer more clearly:

- In the past, although the Tathagata was nirvana, the Dharma was still pure, sentient beings had light karma and pure minds, so no matter what method they practiced, they could achieve success. If we reduce to the time of the Dharma, we are far away from Buddha, the situation and human mind become more and more complicated, hundreds of thousands of people practice, or luckily only one or two people attain enlightenment. What's more, now we're deep into the age of the end of the Dharma, morality is in decline, and there are still very few people who truly practice, let alone attain fruition? Because nowadays sentient beings have heavy mental confusion, life and social organization are more difficult and troublesome than before. In addition, war, famine, and natural disasters often continue, pornographic scenes of shooting and killing are promoted, and religion and morality are considered a drug game and an outdated story. With so many internal and external obstacles affecting each other, if you practice by yourself according to other methods, of course it will be difficult to achieve success. Furthermore, if you want to escape samsara, you must get rid of delusions and delusions. But according to the ancient saying: "stopping ants is as difficult as stopping a strong stream of water from forty miles away," let alone eliminating, and then ending, all delusion? Therefore, in the time of the end of the dharma, if we want liberation, there is only Buddha's Recitation method. Because this discipline has used up all its own power, and thanks to the additional power of others, whether karma or not has ended, it is thanks to the Buddha's power to guide it that it achieves karma rebirth. Once you have returned to Ultimate Bliss, you will no longer be able to permanently regress and escape samsara.

The World-Honored One is a person of profound compassion, about the foundation of the end of the Dharma and the effectiveness of the Pure Land method. He has secret knowledge before the Mahaparasika Sutra and Infinite Life, as the first chapter said. Then you know, in the time of the end of the Dharma, when the effectiveness of the manifestations of all sects is weak, to prolong the Dharma fortune and save sentient beings, there is only the Buddha's Recitation method. Other sects such as meditation, Buddhism, Vinaya, and Tantra, although still circulating and having many practitioners, only have the ability to come down as supporting conditions, and cannot separately be effective on the path of liberation. In a letter sent to a monk, Master Quang said: "— Deep in this Dharma-ending age, if you practice according to other disciplines, talking about sowing good roots and being the cause for attainment in the future is possible, talking about achieving liberation in the present life is not."

Due to what has been explained above, we can conclude: "— at the end of the Dharma, only Buddha's Mindfulness is the only way to escape birth and death in one lifetime."

---o0o---

tieu_de: Lesson 55 - Buddha's Recitation Don't Be Afraid to Smile, Don't Wait for an Appointment
tom_tat: There are many people who want to practice Buddha Dharma, but are afraid of being laughed at as negative, corrupt, and superstitious. Therefore, when reading the sutras, one secretly does not dare to openly show them to others; Or even if you eat vegetarian and recite Buddha's name, you don't dare tell anyone. So…
noi_dung:
Lesson 55 - Buddha's Recitation Don't Be Afraid to Smile, Don't Wait for an Appointment

There are many people who want to practice Buddha Dharma, but are afraid of being laughed at as negative, corrupt, and superstitious. Therefore, when reading the sutras, one secretly does not dare to openly show them to others; Or even if you eat vegetarian and recite Buddha's name, you don't dare tell anyone. You should know that Buddhism is not only a religion, but also a very profound philosophy, many learned and practiced scholars from East and West. Buddha's path is a clear path that leads people from evil to goodness, from ignorant ordinary people to the position of fully enlightened saints. Therefore, those who have had the good fortune to study Buddha's teachings should be happy that they have received good blessings, and should freely advise others to follow them, without having to be afraid. Those who criticize Buddhist practice are negative, corrupt, and superstitious, just because they do not understand.

Again, in the world of practicing Buddha Dharma, there are people who have just read the high sutras and quickly conceit themselves to be Mahayana practitioners. When they see someone who is vegetarian and recites Buddha's name, they immediately consider them to be of low caliber, only imitating the dark and ignorant old men and women. You should know that the Pure Land sect is the complete Mahayana Dharma. Saying "Mahayana", because this dharma takes the Buddha's name as the cause and the status of Full Enlightenment as the result. Say "pill" Because this subject encompasses all five sects and eight sects, as the ancients have discussed. Say "chop" Because this means of bringing from the level of ordinary people to the throne without turning back, from the elementary level to the Supreme Bodhi, is very straightforward and quick. Therefore, all Buddhas in all six directions praise this method, Bodhisattvas such as Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Ma Minh, and Nagarjuna all make vows of rebirth. To despise and despise the Buddha's concept is not only not to have a deep understanding of Pure Land, but also to despise all the Buddhas and the Saints mentioned above. Therefore, reciting the Buddha means that you have actually practiced according to the Mahayana dharma door. You should not be afraid of the ridicule of people who do not understand.

• If you want to seek liberation, reciting the Buddha's name must be considered very urgent. Knowing when to practice it right away, not waiting for an appointment. Buddha once taught that human life is only short in breath; Because the breath goes out but does not come in, it means you have entered another life. So the years, months, days, hours, and even every moment, there is an unexpected death waiting for us in there; No one dares to determine how long their life will be. An ancient poem has a saying:

In the past, there were horses at the beginning of the road.

Today the sarcophagus lies still!

Or sentence:

Don't wait until you're old and recite Buddha's name.

The wilderness of children's graves is crowded with people.

These are true things. Therefore, to prevent impermanence from suddenly coming, every moment we must try to recite Buddha's name. That way, at the last moment, you won't get confused.

On the path of practice, to prevent laziness, the Buddha taught: "The Bhikkhu often has eight ways of being lazy. For example, whenever you go begging for alms and are hungry, you immediately think: "Today, I'm hungry and begging for alms. I'm not healthy enough to rest for one night." Whenever I'm full, I think: "I'm full today, I'm feeling heavy and tired, I'll stop cultivating for now, I'll continue tomorrow." Like that until: about to work a lot - just finished heavy work - about to feel sick - when the pain is strong - about to go far - when going far away to return; In those cases, they always make one excuse or another, then give up practicing to sleep and rest. On the contrary, diligent Bhikkhus, in those eight cases, always think about impermanence and practice diligently."

The laziness mentality of people leaving the home life is like that, the laziness mentality of lay people is probably more. Master Hoang Nhut once advised a friend to recite the Buddha's name. This man wrote a letter to me, complaining that he was busy with a lot of work, and asked me to temporarily arrange things in order. The great master immediately wrote two sentences into that letter, then sent it back intact. Those two sentences are as follows:

I decided to stop now, stop immediately.

Wait for the appointment to finish, it won't be done in time!

Indeed, even when we close our eyes, life is no longer a job.

Once upon a time, a monk advised his friend Truong To to commemorate the Buddha. Your friend said: "I have three unfinished jobs: One is his grandfather's coffin still left in the grave, two is his unmarried son, and three is his unmarried daughter. Once the three things are done, I will obey." A few months later, my friend fell ill and died. The monk came to chant sutras for requiem, and recited a poem saying:

My friend's name is Truong To Luu

Advise him to recite Buddha's name and promise three things.

Three things are not complete, impermanence catches

It's a pity that the King of Hell doesn't respect each other!

In the exam, the monk said: He promised that when he finished the three tasks, he would recite Buddha's name, but unfortunately the impermanence suddenly came, did it wait for him? See, who can guarantee that we are not the second Mr. Truong To Luu? Therefore, those who are determined to practice should immediately recite Buddha's name at any given moment. Do not step on the wrong path of the ancients and harbor eternal hatred.

---o0o---

Section B. How to Recite Long Lasting?

tom_tat: Pure Land practitioners, if they want to recite Buddha's name for a long time, must set a time limit depending on their spirit, health, and circumstances, and then gradually increase their practice. Don't rush to practice too much at first. Like someone who walks too quickly, they easily get...
noi_dung:
Section 56 - Must Progress Gradually

Pure Land practitioners, if they want to recite Buddha's name for a long time, must set a time limit depending on their spirit, health, and circumstances, and then gradually increase their practice. Don't rush to practice too much at first. Like someone walking too quickly, they easily trip and fall. Those who do not measure their strength, but rush to practice too much, may later become tired and discouraged and give up.

Generally, people who practice Buddha Recitation should be divided into timed and non-timed. Timing means that every day there must be a certain time, and how many sentences should be recorded. Without a set time, outside of the sessions, you recite silently when walking, standing, lying, and sitting, but the chanting does not record a number. The essential point of Buddha Recitation is that whether the recitation is slow or fast, it must be clear and distinct, the mind can catch up with the reciting sound, the mind and the sound are in harmony with each other. Just like that, reciting for a long time becomes proficient, the reciting power gradually increases, it can increase from one thousand, two three thousand, one ten thousand, four five thousand, to ten thousand sentences every day and night.

Someone said: "I have experimented many times, no matter what method I use, I cannot recite ten thousand sentences every day and night. That's why the old saying goes: Every day and night, take ten thousand sentences as the key, roughly you should understand one number to encourage progress."

The above statement only refers to "experiment". But we haven't discussed how to "practice". According to Dharma Master Dogen, if practiced thoroughly, every day and night the practitioner can recite up to ten thousand Buddha's names, but must comply with the following conditions:

1. Must sit and recite. Although you can recite Buddha's name while walking, standing, lying, and sitting, you can recite Buddha's name quickly, but if you want to recite it quickly and still hear it clearly, sitting is appropriate.

2. You should use light strings and take ten sentences as one unit. Because if you recite quickly and recite each sentence with a rosary, your hands may not be able to recite it in time. Even if you do, you will easily experience hand tendon pain and shoulder fatigue.

3. Just recite the four words Amitabha Buddha, not the six words. By reciting six words there are ten thousand sentences. If you shorten the recitation of four words, it can reach fifteen thousand sentences.

4. You have to recite in the Vajrayana style, which means you will only move your lips. If you recite silently or out loud, I'm afraid you won't be able to recite quickly, and when you encourage the sound to come out of your mouth, it will take some time. Reciting out loud a thousand sentences, in exchange for reciting the Vajra Sutra method, it can be up to two or three thousand sentences.

If he follows the four conditions above and practices thoroughly, his ability to recite becomes faster and faster over time, but still does not lose clarity. Practice like this until reciting a thousand sentences takes only five minutes as your goal. So in one hour, reciting a thousand verses adds up to fifty minutes, leaving ten minutes to change your posture to avoid fatigue or stand up to pay homage to the Buddha, or put down the rosary, clasp your hands and circumambulate the Buddha, breathing lightly to gain strength. With this method of reciting and resting, reciting ten thousand verses takes ten hours. In a twenty-four hour day and night, excluding six hours of sleep, three hours of eating and urinating, ten hours of reciting ten thousand sentences, adding up the nineteen hours, there is still five hours left over. During those five hours, either doing chores, sitting quietly or reading sutras is still relaxing.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Section 57 - Should Pray for Purity, Don't Be Greedy Too Much
tom_tat: There are people who recite Buddha's name and don't like to recite the rosary. They only estimate how many hours each session is. Reciting like that has the advantage of easily nourishing the mind, each sentence of the Buddha's name is clearly penetrating. But if you are not a person with a strong mind,...
noi_dung:
Section 57 - Should Pray for Purity, Don't Be Greedy Too Much

There are people who recite Buddha's name and don't like to recite the rosary. They only estimate how many hours each session is. Reciting like that has the advantage of easily nourishing the mind, each sentence of the Buddha's name is clearly penetrating. But if you are not a person with a strong mind and determination, you will be lost in your shortcomings; The power of mindfulness is stagnant and difficult to achieve. You quickly get bored and tired. You often look at the clock to see if it's almost time or not. If you recite the rosary according to the prescribed number, then the strength of diligent recitation quickly matures, like a person whose legs are weak but relies on a stick so he can easily climb a high mountain. But if you don't skillfully keep to the basic point of reciting the Buddha: "The chant is clear and clear, mind and voice are in harmony," Everything is flawed because we want too much and become false thoughts! You should know that when the practitioner starts thinking, each Buddha sentence goes deep into the store of consciousness. When the accumulated capacity has increased, the Buddha's recitation from the store of consciousness will spontaneously appear while awake or sleeping. This is called the realm of "no self-thought." If you normally recite clearly, it will be clearly detected. If you recite falsely, it is not clear, meaning the Buddha's name appears unclearly. The failure point of those who recite Buddha's name is right there, so they must be cautious from the beginning. Proverbs often say: "As much as there is no truth, there is little truth." If because of your desire to quickly and a lot to seek fame, you recite tens of thousands of sentences every day and then your thoughts are not clear and your mind cannot catch up with the sound. It would be better to recite less but more firmly.

The author knows a Buddhist woman who practices Pure Land. This woman believes in the Three Jewels, but still likes to wander around. Every evening, when her children and grandchildren invited her to the table to eat together, she said: "The teacher taught me to make vows to recite Buddha ten times every day. If I don't keep my promise, I will be guilty of the Three Jewels. Now wait a bit until I 'make enough', then we'll have dinner." Having said that, she quickly put on her robe and recited Buddha's name as quickly as fighting fire. It only took fifteen minutes to finish the job. How can one rebirth by reciting Buddha's name like that? Not only this woman, but also many other Buddhists recite the Buddha's name in the "full number" way. that. Therefore, knowing that reciting the Buddha is precious in a place where the mind is truly developed, the recitation is definitely clear, is called "a person who truly recites the Buddha" Just hoping for results.

At the end of the Qing Dynasty in China, in Hangzhou, a Buddhist lady came to Hieu Tu Temple and asked Venerable Dogen: "I've been reciting Buddha for a long time, but I haven't seen any progress. I don't know why?" The Venerable said: "Reciting the Buddha's name is not difficult, but it is difficult to keep it for a long time. Perhaps she couldn't chant evenly and sustainably, that's why she was like that." She said: "That's true. Because I am bound by family ties, reciting Buddha's prayers is often interrupted and cannot last. From now on, I will put aside all fate and vow to keep exactly as you taught." A little while later, she came again and asked: "Since listening to the instructions until now, I have put aside all extraneous activities and chanted Buddha's name every day. Why haven't I seen any effect yet?" The Venerable continued to teach: "Reciting the Buddha's name is not difficult, it is difficult to stay for a long time. Reciting for a long time is not difficult, but it is difficult to stay focused. On the outside, although she had exhausted everything, in her heart she was still worried about the house, fields, and gardens, and thinking about her children and relatives. The worry has not ended, the root of love is still there, how can one single-mindedly see the Buddha? When she heard this, she immediately complained: "Indeed it is like that! Even though the external relationship has been abandoned, the thoughts still linger. From now on, please do not worry about a hundred things, to single-mindedly recite Buddha." After returning home from the teachings, if her children, grandchildren or outsiders asked questions, she would always say: "I want peace of mind. I don't care about a hundred things." Because of this reason, everyone calls her old lady Ba Bat Quan. A few years later, she went to Hieu Tu hermitage to bow to Venerable Dao Nguyen and said: "Thanks to your teachings, I can now recite with one mind and have seen the Buddha. Please come and pay my respects to the monk, because I am about to be reborn."

Ms. Bat Bat Quan above, understood two principles: Long-lasting and single-minded, the result is liberation. Therefore, those who recite Buddha's name and want to reach the level of purity must view everything from home, fields and gardens to close relationships as temporary predestined conditions that unite and then dissolve. If you have love for your relatives, you must first achieve rebirth liberation for yourself, and then save your loved ones. This is true love. So if you want to recite the Buddha's name, you should think that not only can you not control a hundred things, but you can also have a thousand things and ten thousand things that you can't control.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Section 58 - Don't Lose the Chapter Introduction
tom_tat: When practitioners recite Buddha making vows to pray to be born in the West, a lotus flower immediately grows in the seven-jeweled pond in the realm of Ultimate Bliss. If you continue chanting without interruption, the lotus flower will gradually grow bigger and bigger. On the contrary, natural flowers also...
noi_dung:
Section 58 - Don't Lose the Introductory Part

When practitioners recite Buddha making vows to pray to be born in the West, a lotus flower immediately grows in the seven-jeweled pond in the realm of Ultimate Bliss. If you continue chanting without interruption, the lotus flower will gradually grow bigger and bigger. On the contrary, flowers naturally wither. When you develop diligence again, another lotus flower will appear. That lotus flower is created by the practitioner's power of meditation, depending on the high or low level of merit, there are better or worse, divided into nine grades, from Lower Grade Lower Sanh up to Upper Grade Upper Sanh. Although it is said that there are nine levels in general, because the practice of practitioners is very different, it actually includes immeasurable levels. For example, in society there are roughly three classes: noble, middle class and poor; But in fact, within each class there are many different levels of superiority and inferiority. The lotus product in Ultimate Bliss is the same.

Pure Land practice depends on one's background and circumstances, so each person's actions are different. There are people who recite hundreds, thousands, up to tens of thousands every day. But no matter how busy you are, at least ten times a day, the practitioner must have at least ten thoughts, otherwise he will lose the "entry level", meaning he will not be able to participate in the nine lotus levels in the Western world. "Imported products" is the proper noun of Pure Land practitioners. It suggests and reminds practitioners not to forget Buddha's recitation. The Ten Recitations are also called the Ten Dharma Recitations. That is the method master Tu Van repented, based on the chapter Lower Quality Lower Birth of the Infinite Life Sutra, specifically for those who are too busy with domestic or domestic affairs to recite the Buddha's name and be reborn in the Pure Land. This method includes ten thoughts, each thought is a breath, the secret intention is to "borrow the breath to capture the mind." People who are a bit long can recite a dozen sentences per breath, people who are a bit short can only recite seven or eight sentences. For each breath the Buddha calls a thought, ten breaths are ten thoughts. After reciting ten breaths, continue reciting the verse describing merit:

I wish to be born in the Western Pure Land.

Mother and father are nine good lotus grades.

Flowers bloom to see Buddha enlightening to non-birth.

Pervades all species of consciousness.

After praying, pay homage to the Buddha three times and then leave. This method originates from Buddha's boundless compassion. No matter how extreme a person is in his work, he can still practice it to step on the path of liberation.

Regarding reciting Buddha for ten breaths, there is a point to note: let it be natural and do not lengthen or shorten it. Otherwise, you will definitely suffer from "injured energy." When Master Trung Luan came to Bac Binh to preach, one day an old man came and said: "Because I recite Buddha's name, now I have hearing loss and sometimes I can't hear anything at all." The magician asked the reason, the old man replied: "There was a Venerable who secretly taught me a method of reciting the Buddha's name. He said: "The practice of reciting ten breaths, currently no one knows it, the monks, because there is a formula in it that has now been lost." I sincerely prayed for the Dharma. He taught me to recite a rosary with each breath, consisting of one hundred and eight sentences. I did as he was told, tried to practice, and my ears started ringing and I have been deaf ever since. So I don't know if this method of reciting is in accordance with Buddha's teachings? After listening, Mr. Trung Luan rejected it, blaming the other monk for turning the Buddha's dharma into a pagan dharma, causing harmful results to people. Then he slowly explained the principles of the Ten Recitations to the old man.

This is a story that people chanting Buddha must pay attention to, to gain experience.

---o0o---

Section C. Pure Land, Special liberation discipline

tieu_de: Section 59 - Buddha Recitation, Easy Practice Method
tom_tat: The Pure Land discipline, especially with the method of reciting the name, is an easy path to practice, everyone can know this. But "easy to practice" has many meanings, this is because everyone is knowledgeable
noi_dung:
Section 59 - Buddha Recitation, Easy Practice Method

The Pure Land discipline, especially with the method of reciting the name, is an easy path to practice, everyone can know this. But "easy to practice" has many meanings, this is something everyone already understands.

By cultivating other methods, if one enters from the Teaching, the scriptures are vast and the meaning is extremely profound. Students of Buddhism must first grasp the basic meaning, and then from there, gradually understand the different meanings. After that, we must understand the principles, extract the essence, and choose to open a path of practice to follow for the rest of our lives. This event would not have been completed without wasting several decades of hard work and effort. If one enters from the Law, one must leave the home life, and the precepts are many, the practitioner needs to be familiar with the names, types, natures, and appearances of the various types of precepts. You must have wisdom to understand the meaning of the same language, to apply the points of declaration, maintenance, and violation depending on the time and place. Therefore, studying the sutras is not difficult, studying the law and knowing how to use it skillfully so as not to depart from the law nor be bound by the law is difficult. After understanding the law, you must have the spirit of patience and the will to endure hardship to reach success. If you enter from meditation, if you have not sown sufficient wisdom, your energy is not suitable, and you want to use your weak foundation to seek noble Dharma, then all the sharing of light and transmission will be hopeless. That's why Mr. Ta Linh Van, a famous Buddhist scholar in the past, said: "Practicing meditation to become a Buddha must be a person of wisdom and karma." This statement is still not wrong or excessive.

As for the method of reciting the name of the Pure Land discipline, once you have developed faith and vows, no matter your ability, you can recite Buddha's name and practice. Other methods only rely on self-reliance, but the Pure Land method has used up all of its own strength and also gained additional strength. Amitabha Buddha's power of forgiveness, that is, the guiding force of prayer, is extremely strong, even those who are not yet pure of karma, or even those who have created too much evil karma, can return to Buddha's thoughts and be welcomed back to the West. Ancient people once compared: "Practicing other subjects is as difficult and difficult as an ant crawling up a mountain. Reciting Buddha's rebirth quickly and easily is like sailing on a boat with favorable winds." This statement is very accurate. Furthermore, after being born into Ultimate Bliss, living in a beautiful and peaceful landscape, often close to Buddha Bodhisattva, no matter what method you practice, you will quickly achieve success, like rolling a round log down from a high mountain, still progressing without pause.

Summarizing the above, the ease of practice of Pure Land includes three points: One is easy to practice, two is easy to rebirth, three is easy to become Buddha. Because of that ease, the results of cultivating and attaining the Pure Land practice are like pearls touching gold, making a gentle sound, lotuses smiling and chrysanthemums smiling with fresh, fragrant products. In that journey from ordinary people to Buddhahood, there is also class and no class. Because when you are reborn, you have escaped samsara of life and death, and reciting Buddha means becoming Buddha. Just as silkworms, pupae, and butterflies are still indivisible, saying that butterflies are originally silkworms, or silkworms are butterflies, is not far off.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Lesson 60 - From Distracting Mind, One Will Come to Concentrate the Mind
tom_tat: Reciting Buddha with your mouth, thinking Buddha with your mind, or staying in Buddha recitation, is called Concentration of Buddha Recitation. The mouth recites the Buddha's name, the mind does not remember the Buddha but thinks vaguely about other things, that is the Praying Mind of Buddha's Recitation. Dispersing the mind while reciting, its effectiveness is compared to concentration...
noi_dung:
Lesson 60 - From Distracting Mind, One Will Come to Concentrate the Mind

Reciting Buddha with your mouth, thinking Buddha with your mind, or staying in Buddha recitation, is called Concentration of Buddha Recitation. The mouth recites the Buddha's name, the mind does not remember the Buddha but thinks vaguely about other things, that is the Praying Mind of Buddha's Recitation. Dispersing the mind and reciting it is much weaker in effectiveness than concentrating the mind. For that reason, from ancient times until now, good and knowledgeable people have advised people to try to concentrate their minds and meditate, not to let their minds wander. Therefore, praising Buddha's thoughts is not enough to be an example.

However, every external impact is related to the subconscious mind, which is the eighth consciousness within. If chanting the Buddha's thoughts is completely ineffective, then where did those six red names come from? Since six words have appeared, there must be two forces: One is due to seeds, discovered from the subconscious. Second, the impact from the outside gathers back inside. Therefore, it cannot be said that chanting Buddha's thoughts is completely ineffective, but compared to concentration, it is much weaker. The method of chanting the mind has not been promoted since ancient times, but its implications and uses cannot be denied. That's why ancient people saved a verse that says:

Amitabha six words of the central king,

Don't be shy if you're wondering!

Thousands of miles of clouds obscure the sunlight.

People all over the land glowed with sunlight.

This verse infers something relevant. Because the seed of Buddha recitation in the eighth consciousness, when mature, will inevitably give rise to the sixth consciousness, causing pure mindfulness to arise. Then from the sixth consciousness, the previous five consciousnesses are promoted to become current. But when the seed of the Buddha's thought passes through the sixth consciousness, because of the deep contamination of sentient beings, it is invaded by other thoughts. Although it escapes the siege, the remaining influence is not much. For example, although the sun is bright, but because it is covered by many layers of clouds, when it reaches the human world, only the glow remains. But the reason why that excess light exists is also due to the influence of the sun. Knowing this, Pure Land practitioners should not be too afraid to worry about confusing thoughts, just continuously recite one sentence after another, remaining mindful as long as possible. Reciting like that for a long time, the horse's mind will naturally return to hell, and the monkey's heart will gradually enter the cave. Recite for a while longer, then mindfulness will appear clearly. There is no need to remove it, but it will be achieved naturally. If you understand this, just cherish the thoughts a lot, don't be afraid to distract your mind. Just like water that is cloudy, if you keep pouring it, it will eventually become clear. Even though people have a lot of random thoughts, if they recite Buddha's thoughts for a long time, they will definitely become mindful. You should know that when walking, standing, lying, sitting, and doing all actions, one recites the Buddha's name. If they completely use concentration and concentration to recite, then they will definitely stumble on the road, or they will not be able to succeed when writing scriptures or doing work. Therefore, the ancients also had times when they had to distract their minds and chant, but still did not leave the chant of Buddha, because even if they distracted their minds, they still did not lose their influence.

Come here, let me tell a story. At one time, someone came and asked a monk: "To be honest with you, I have been reciting Buddha for more than ten years now but there are still many false thoughts and I don't know how to get rid of them. I went to many places to ask about methods from those who had practiced before me. This person gave this experience, that person taught another way, and there was a monk who advised me to hold my breath and recite twenty-one sentences and then swallow one. I have applied all kinds of methods, but I can only concentrate my mind at first, then perhaps because I am used to it, my wandering thoughts return to the way they were before. I wonder if you have any effective method to teach me?"

The monk replied: "That point of failure was because he was not persistent, but kept changing his path. We should know that we ordinary people have created so much negative karma from countless lifetimes that we cannot be pure all at once! The key is to use your mind for a long time. Let me give you two examples: For example, if a vase of dirty water was full, he would pour clean, fragrant water into it. Because the dirty water is full, the clean water must be flushed out, but at least a few drops will remain in the jar. If you keep pouring it in, one day the pot of foul water will turn into clean, fragrant water. For example, if you have a stomach ache, no matter what medicine you take, you will vomit. Just be patient and take the stomach medicine right away, don't change anything else. Although every time he took it, he would vomit, but the medicine still remained, and gradually his illness would go away. The same is true for the afflictions and delusions of sentient beings. Using Buddha's recitation medicine to treat it naturally is appropriate. If we keep changing, how can we succeed? It's like someone uses alum to boil water, but before it clears, he quickly stirs and pours in salt. Before pouring the salt, he stirs again and pours in lime powder. If it keeps changing like that, how can the water stay clear? Therefore, the problem of ending false thoughts does not come from changing many methods, but from choosing an appropriate method and then practicing it for a long time to achieve success. After listening, he nodded to think it was reasonable.

As said, if you want to concentrate your mind, the basic point is to put effort into it for a long time. However, if you are afraid that the power of your thoughts will be scattered and need a means to easily calm your mind, you should apply the method of Ten Recitation Numbers presented previously. This magic uses all one's mental energy to memorize one to ten sentences, so it is easy to enter pure concentration. If your mind is still confused and cannot use the Ten Niem Ky Number magic, then in each chant you just need to focus on firmly recording the letter "A". When the letter A is still there, all the other letters are still there. If you are confused and let it disappear, all five other words will also be lost. The letter A is also the basic letter, and the mother of all letters. Concentrate while reciting and firmly note the letter A. From time to time, the mind and the scene will naturally dissolve and merge into one mass, the vastness is like nothingness, Buddha and I are both lost. At that time, of course, the letter A was no longer there. But before it was lost because the mind was agitated and disturbed, now it no longer belongs to the fused state of constant concentration. This is the phenomenon of the mind being empty, the starting point to enter Buddha Recitation Samadhi.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Section 61 - Muoi Phuong Pure Land and Tushita Pure Land
tom_tat: In the ten directions, there are countless Buddha realms with beautiful, pure and solemn colors, such as the world of Pure Water in the Medicine Buddha Sutra, the world of Incense and Wonderful Joy in the Vimalakirti Sutra. But why don't we recite the name...
noi_dung:
Section 61 - Muoi Phuong Pure Land and Tushita Pure Land

In the ten directions, there are countless Buddha realms with beautiful, pure and solemn colors, such as the world of Pure Water in the Medicine Buddha Sutra, the world of Incense and Wonderful Joy in the Vimalakirti Sutra. But why don't we chant the names of all Buddhas to pray to be born in the Pure Lands in the ten directions, but only make vows to be born in Ultimate Bliss? - There are three reasons:

1. Due to the recommendation and advice of the Original Teacher Shakyamuni Buddha, he advised him to pray for rebirth in the realm of Ultimate Bliss. According to ancient teachings, in addition to the fact that the Ultimate Bliss realm has many miraculous conditions suitable for transforming the roots in the Impure realms, the Original Teacher does not want to explain much about other Pure Lands, for fear that sentient beings will start thinking about comparisons and confusion, and their minds will not be unified. Due to the miraculous conditions for transformation, not only in the Saha world, sentient beings in countless worlds in the ten directions all pray for Ultimate Bliss.

2. Due to Amitabha, the World-Honored One made 48 vast vows that adorned the Pure Land, vowing to lead from the Bodhisattva level to the many sinners.

3. Because sentient beings in this realm have great karma with Amitabha Buddha and Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara in the realm of Ultimate Bliss. The proof is that when Buddhists meet each other, they greet each other with the words Amitabha Buddha and when they are in an accident, they often chant the name of Avalokitesvara.

Because of the above reasons, the Ultimate Bliss realm has advantages over other Pure Lands in the ten directions.

- About Tushita Pure Land, layman Phuong Luan, a scholar of Buddhist studies, presented his opinion as follows:

In this world, in the upper direction there is the inner courtyard of the Tusita heaven, owned by Maitreya Bodhisattva. That place is also beautiful and dignified, Lord Maitreya always preaches the Dharma, good people gather to practice, so it is called Tusita Pure Land. In the Upper and Lower Maitreya Sutras, Thich Ton also introduced that country very clearly and advised one to seek rebirth. The reason for that introduction is because Thich Ton's original intention was for practitioners to first follow Maitreya Bodhisattva to study, and in the future follow him to be born and attain fruition in the three Dragon Flower Associations. This was encouraged by the Original Teacher, and many Buddhist practitioners also prayed to Tushita Pure Land. Furthermore, Maitreya Bodhisattva once spoke about Yogācāra Master Earth, he is the founder of the Mind-Only sect. Therefore, most people who practice the Duy Thuc sect have a wish to be born in Tushita, so that their practice can advance to a profound level. For this, those who wish to be born in Ultimate Bliss can only praise Thich Ton for his immeasurable compassion and skill in opening many means to save sentient beings. Also praising those who seek Tu Suitai for their eagerness to study without getting tired, their wish to return to the impure realm to attain salvation is very clear. But Tu Suat's inner court is not yet the ultimate scene, and is not a sure place of success for those of middle and lower base. Because there are three events in it:

1. Tu Suat Hospital's medical report is not as solemn, spacious, and magical as Ultimate Bliss. In terms of right return, it is also worse, because in the West there is currently Amitabha Buddha preaching the Dharma, and countless Bodhisattva Bodhisattvas are helping to encourage and guide him. Furthermore, in Ultimate Bliss, people have unlimited lifespans, which is the best and most secure refuge.

2. Lord Maitreya did not have the original vow to guide him like Amitabha Buddha and was born into Tushita purely through his own power. He was afraid that when he fell ill, he would fall into a coma and not be able to grasp the results.

3. It is very difficult to rebirth within the hospital. Just like in the past, Master Huyen Giac had solemn conduct, participated in meditation and enlightened enlightenment, and penetrated the Tripitaka to the depths. When he was about to die, he gathered his disciples together, finished reciting the poem, and suddenly raised his face to the void and said: "This is strange, I have made vows to be born in Tu Suat inner court, why am I now the heavenly lord in Da Ma heaven?" His disciples asked, and he said: "It's not something you understand." Moments later he said: "There are so many guests in the sky!" After speaking, he passed away.

Nine hundred years after the Buddha's death, in the land of Thien Truc, there were three Bodhisattva brothers, namely Asanga, Vasubandhu and Lion Giac, who practiced the Nhat Quang Dinh sect and made vows to be born in the Tushita monastery. The three people made an agreement, whoever came up first had to come down and tell the news. After the first part of Lion's Enlightenment, three years passed without any news. Next, Vasubandhu passed away and was never heard from again. Two years later, one evening, Asanga was sitting and lecturing the sutras when he suddenly saw a bright light in the middle of nowhere, and a heavenly prince in a solemn robe appeared, claiming to be Vasubandhu, saying he had been born in the Tushita inner courtyard. Mr. Asanga asked: "Why didn't it be revealed until now?" The Than replied: "As soon as I was born, Maitreya blessed me with a Dharma teaching. After listening to the Dharma, I circumambulated three times and then came down here immediately. Because the time spent at Tu Suat was one day and night, and four hundred years down here, it made me tired of waiting." Vo Truoc asked again: "And where is Lion Horn?" - Answer: "While I was circumambulating, I saw Lion Horn entering the outer courtyard, engrossed in heavenly music."

Like Mr. Huyen Giac is a high monk, Mr. Lion Giac is a Bodhisattva, but one only ascended to the third heaven, while the other reached the fourth heaven, but got lost in the outer courtyard, fascinated by the wonderful scene of the five desires. If such highly intelligent beings still do not achieve the result of being born in the Pure Land of Tushita, then those who have basic abilities will not easily gain hope. Remember when Bach Lac Thien used to ask for an exam:

Some people go to sea to visit Than Chau

Say you see a colorful island palace

It's so beautiful, the fairy said:

Will wait for Bach Lac to go upstairs.

Loved no subjects, did not study immortality

This story is also a myth

Bong Lai is not where we live

Returns to Tu Suat Thien palace.

Bach Lac Thien first studied immortality and sought to return to Penglai, but later abandoned the ancient studies of Buddha to seek Tu Suat. When he was old, he recited Buddha's name to pray for rebirth in Ultimate Bliss. This can be called the more you contemplate and choose, the more sophisticated you get.
