Section A. Briefly About Dependent Investigations

tom_tat: The elders in the monastic village often said: "When making vows to do great merit, or practice, we often encounter many obstacles and challenges." People leaving the home life have four stages where obstacles are often detected...
noi_dung:
Section 62 - Some Causes of Obstacles

The elders in the monastic village often said: "When making vows to do great merit, or practice, we often encounter many obstacles and challenges." People leaving the home life have four stages that obstacles are often detected: when shaving one's hair to enter a temple, when receiving precepts, when studying sutras, especially the Mahayana sutras, and when giving up everything to meditate. There are many people who have already planted good conditions, or because of their diligent efforts, they easily overcome the previous three stages and move on to the fourth level. But when your practice progresses to a fairly high level, it is inevitable that obstacles will be discovered. Like the Venerable Hu Van, a modern monk, while diligently practicing meditation, karma suddenly discovered and made him blind, deaf and mute for three weeks. Browsing through old stories, the writer remembered a man named To, built his own hut in a quiet place to meditate, and brought someone along to help him. Initially, he practiced sitting for one or two hours and then gradually increased to be able to stay in concentration for three days and nights. One day, layperson Su meditated for twenty-one days without eating or drinking. The attendant saw that he had been sitting for too long. When he came closer to take a look, his breathing was great and he was no longer breathing like before. He did not know that it was a profound state of meditation, mistakenly thought the layman was dead, and immediately buried him alive.

There was a Pure Land monk who recited Buddha's name every day and night for ten thousand verses. Due to the merit of reciting Buddha, the ground the monk walked on turned into pure gold. One day, a refugee came to ask for shelter. The monk looked at that person and then said privately to the attendant: "This guy has the qualities of a thief. You should feed him enough and then tell him to get out of here." The little priest, out of pity, saw the other person beg and plead, but his attachment did not bloom. Sure enough, a few days later, that person sneaked into the monk's room in the middle of the night, broke his limbs, killed him, stole some things from the hut and then left.

In the two cases mentioned above, ancient German commentaries said that karma concentration was inevitable. Practitioners have three obstacles: Obstacles of affliction, karma and retribution, but the power of karma is heavier and more dangerous than the other two. But why is it that when you don't practice, you have nothing, but when you practice at a higher level, you often encounter many obstacles? - That's also because we are ordinary people of the end of dharma, of course most of the obstacles are heavy. If we had light karma, we would have been born in the time of the Dharma image or the Dharma. But it is not due to practice that obstacles arise, but it is the power to transform karma, to change heavy retributions into light retributions, to change future retributions into present retributions. Suppose we have ten parts of karma obstacles, but due to merit of cultivating, we can eliminate seven parts, and still discover three parts. And that retribution should have come later, but thanks to the power of meditation, I only suffered a light retribution in this life to quickly achieve liberation.

Like Gioi Hien, a monk in his previous life was a king who brought troops to destroy many places and created too much karma. In this life, after receiving excess blessings and dying, he would have fallen into hell. But thanks to the monk's dedication to practicing and propagating Buddha's teachings, every day he suffered from an illness that felt like there were many invisible swords stabbing and slashing in his body. Thus, it took two years for the illness to end. Because of that fate, the monk was able to eliminate the karma of hell and be born in the Tusita Heaven. Like the predecessor Ngo Mao, he also created karma, so he should have been a pig for seven lifetimes for people to kill. But thanks to the old man reciting the Buddha's name, when his life was fulfilled, he was stabbed seven times by the enemy to repay his karma once, and was then reborn to Ultimate Bliss. In short, proverbs call it the state of accumulating karma.

However, not every practitioner is punished. Some people practice more and more, the better they get, the more peaceful they are, and there are no obstacles. That is because in previous lives he did not create too heavy karma, or he had practiced mindfulness and had many good roots. But according to most people, if you don't encounter big obstacles, you will also encounter small obstacles. In addition to external obstacles, there are three causes of karma:

1. According to the Dhammapada sect, our consciousness contains mixed karma strains, good and evil. When reciting the Buddha's name or engaging in meditation, we collect the seeds of merit that are immutable and must be detected by all other karma seeds. For example, if a forest is full of animals, if people come to reclaim it, all the trees are cut down and all the animals run out. The same is true of the appearance and afflictions and afflictions discovered by karma. This is called the reaction power of the karma seed.

2. There are practitioners who are not familiar with the teachings, do not understand that the internal and external appearances are illusory, and have not yet discovered what is true and false, so their judgments are wrong. Therefore, with regard to the internal and external conditions, thoughts of attachment, joy, worry, and fear arise, which create obstacles for ourselves.

3. Again, like a person following a plan to find a gold mine, the road must go through high mountains, abysses, wilderness, deep forests, the journey must be very elaborate and arduous. If that person is not steadfast, does not know how to be patient and flexible according to his strength and circumstances, he will definitely retreat. Or maybe I give up and stop at a temporary scene, or die on the way. The path of practice is the same. Although practitioners practice according to the sutras, if they do not know how to be patient and flexible depending on their strength and circumstances, their determination will not last long and they will certainly fail. That tribulation was also caused by ourselves.

Above is a summary of some of the causes of obstacles.

---o0o---

tom_tat: The karmic conditions that cause obstacles for practitioners have many discrepancies. Now I just want to summarize the general outline through six
noi_dung:
Section 63 - Magical Conditions

The karmic conditions that cause obstacles for practitioners have many discrepancies. Now I just want to summarize the outline through six points:

1. Internal Examination: - Some people, while practicing, suddenly have thoughts of greed, anger, lust, jealousy, contempt, doubt, or ignorance that can easily cause drowsiness and drowsiness. These thoughts are sometimes very intense, and when faced with small things, they can easily cause anger and resentment. Many times in dreams, we see signs of good and evil changing. The detailed details here cannot be fully described. Encountering this scene, the practitioner must be aware that it is due to the ability of practice that karma signs are discovered. At that moment, one should enlighten the karma signs that are all illusory, heighten mindfulness, and naturally those signs will one by one disappear. If you don't perceive it clearly, it will inevitably cause you to rot and fall. Tien Duc said: "I'm not afraid that karma will start early, I'm just afraid that enlightenment will be slow," is this point. Some people, while working hard, suddenly experience confusion and unbearable fatigue. At that time, you should stand up and pay homage to the Buddha, walk in meditation, or temporarily take a break and go outside to read a few pages of a book, fix five or three flower stems, wait for calm and then return to reciting the Buddha's name. If you are not conscious and keep forcing yourself to have one mind as soon as possible, the more you try, the more chaotic it becomes. This is flexibility in the use of attack, for example, if the enemy is so strong that it seems like the water is overflowing, the commander must depend on the opportunity, so he should entrench himself and not attack. There are practitioners who, when reciting the Buddha's name, suddenly feel solitude like a monotonous piano piece that easily gets bored, so they do not hesitate to add reciting mantras, visualizations, or chanting sutras.

By the way, I would like to tell you something here to give fellow practitioners more awareness. There was a female Buddhist who came to the pen pretending to be sad and crying, telling the truth: Every time she recited the Buddha chanting sutras for a few dozen minutes, she would fall asleep without realizing it, sometimes urinating right in front of the Buddha's table. Therefore, she was afraid of sin and did not dare to chant. The fake pen advised her to specialize in repentance for a while. Sure enough, not long after, she completely abandoned that karma and dreamed of many snail shells. When she cracked each shell, she found a lotus seed. This girl has heavy karma delusion, the snail shell is the manifestation of karma delusion, breaking the snail shell and seeing lotus seeds is breaking delusion and achieving the good cause of enlightenment and rebirth to the Buddha realm.

Another monk narrated that: Every few nights he dreamed that he saw thirty or forty people holding knives and sticks coming to fight and slash. The mantra changed from reciting Great Compassion to Standard Dharma mantra-words was not successful, because each time chanting the Dharma was less frequent and gave me headaches all day, even taking medicine did not cure it. Knowing that his karma is heavy, he makes vows to bow to Tam Thien Buddha for repentance. But when he went to the temple to pay homage to the Buddha, he saw a tall and ferocious man who pushed him down and did not let him bow. So he came sadly and cried: If you commit a crime, repentance practices, but repentance cannot practice. I don't know what to do? After listening, the author thought and thought that this person had heavy karma, that the Great Compassion and Chuan De mantras had quite strong karma-breaking power, and his wish to bow to the Three Thousand Buddhas was a vast vow. This is the error of only knowing how to pray for oneself and not praying for the wronged ones, and not being flexible enough to use the karma-destroying technique. For example, if a weak person has severe leprosy, they should use mild medicines like Phong Kinh Kinh Gioi to eliminate them one after another, but on the contrary, in order to heal quickly, they use strong medicines such as Ma Tien Ba Dau to cure the leprosy, and the patient will be tortured unbearably. Therefore, the writer advised him to try bowing to the Little Repentance every night according to the Lotus Sutra, then kneel down and recite rebirth twenty-one times, recite Buddha's name for five hundred sentences to pray for sins to be eliminated, and pray for unjust past relationships to be quickly overcome. Just practice like that for a while, if you feel stable, you can gradually increase it. The novice did as he was told, and sure enough, that state ended.

Above are the hidden karma signs inside. If you don't know how to gracefully destroy enlightenment, it will definitely become an obstacle.

2. External Examination: - These are external obstacles that cause difficulties and depravity for the practitioner. Witnessing that scene is heat, noise, uncleanness, or a place that is too cold or too many insects and mosquitoes. When encountering this scene, you should also be flexible, don't be attached to formality, just pray for peace of mind. For example, in a very hot situation, do not hesitate to wear a thin robe to pay homage to the Buddha, then go sit in a cool place to recite, and when finished, return to the Buddha making vows dedicating merit. Or if you encounter a place with many mosquitoes, you can sit under a thin curtain and recite Buddha's name. As in northern China, because the weather is too cold, monks, when going to the main hall to chant sutras, must also wear shoes, socks and hats carefully. There are Buddhists who, because their families are poor, work hard, go home early and come home late, or are in debt, hungry and cold, have weak wives and sick children, and have no dignified place to worship. In that situation, practice is actually very difficult, one must have patience and try like the old beggar reciting the Buddha's name to be successful. Or there are people who, because of many karma obstacles, when they don't practice, they stop practicing. When they are about to enter the Buddha's table, they get headaches, dizziness, and various illnesses, or they have visitors and many unusual things happen. Encountering such scenes, we must try and be flexible in finding ways to practice. The effort to be flexible depends on the different situations that the application cannot fully describe. Remember that when faced with a difficult situation, you must pay attention to the mind and not be attached to the appearance so that you can be tolerant. The evil Saha world still has many sufferings. If you do not have the strength to endure, all your practice will be difficult to achieve.

3. Paradox: - On the path, practitioners are often hindered by adversity. Some people are prevented or sabotaged by their parents, siblings, spouses, or children from practicing. There is a body with a disease that never heals. There are people who are unjustly pursued and always seek to harm them. Some people are falsely accused and are forced to go to jail and undergo interrogation or exile. Some people are caught up in competition, jealousy, or bad reputations, making it difficult to be patient. The latter happens most often. Such situations are all due to the power of karma. The old saying once said: "If you are not foolish, if you seek perfection, you will be destroyed." The above sentence has the meaning: There are compliments and unexpected honors that are not worthy of praise but are praised; and there are events that are actually not worthy of contempt, but turn into scenes of complete contempt and contempt. To prove this point, the author would like to tell a few small things:

Previously, during the French colonial period, there was a monk who was awarded the degree of Tang Cang by the Hue court, and the pagoda's title was Sac Tu. Therefore, wherever he went, the monk had a horse-drawn carriage and a staff to accompany him, and even when he got on and off the boat, there were people carrying him around. A gang member saw this and cursed dissatisfiedly, then declared that on the full moon day of the seventh lunar month, he would go to the temple and scold the monk in front of his followers. On that day, after drinking alcohol, the bandit went to the temple naked, and a Buddhist took his son and asked the monk to pray to release it in a lotus pond. Seeing that scene, he was suddenly moved, returned and called his companions to go to the temple to take refuge, and from then on, wherever he went, he praised the monk for being a gentle and virtuous person. Even when serving the hammock, he also said that it was because of his teacher's blessings.

Another story happened not long ago, two Buddhists from far away came to visit a fellow monk they had known personally. When we arrived at the temple, the monk had just left about fifteen minutes away. The two asked, the attendant said the teacher had just left; When I asked the others, they didn't know and said they just saw me here. Just for a moment, those two Buddhists became suspicious that the monk did not want to receive them, said goodbye and did not go to the temple, and then everywhere they went, they criticized the monk for not doing virtuous things.

Actually, the way of the above monk is not praiseworthy but is praised. And the monk's heartless action mentioned below is nothing worthy of criticism, but was misunderstood and destroyed. The world considers it a matter of luck, but the Buddha's cause and effect theory believes that it is the time when karma, blessings, and blessings appear. An ancient poem has a saying:

It seems like eating and drinking is normal.

It's also a pretty pitiful predestination.

If a small thing is like that, then all other adversities are due to karma, or caused by karma. When encountering these scenes, the practitioner should only be patient and repentance, not be sad or resentful and lose his mind.

4. Thuan Khao: - There are people who do not encounter adversity but instead encounter favorable circumstances. Whatever they wish for, they get whatever they want, but success is all about bondage, not liberation. There are people who, when they have the intention to cultivate in peace, suddenly see a scene of fame, fortune, and beauty, or many people they love and want to follow and serve by their side. For example, when a person leaves the home life when he develops his mind to practice, suddenly someone comes to invite him to become the head of a large temple; Or like a lay person, there is a letter inviting him to become a president, a minister, or a business that will quickly make money. These are scenes that, according to life's fate, attract practitioners, and then lead to other troubles that cause loss of religious mindfulness. Few people die from fire, but many die from water, so on the path of practice, favorable circumstances are actually more terrifying than adverse circumstances. Adversity sometimes makes the practitioner awaken and easily escape from greedy thoughts, or get frustrated and worried about practicing. As for favorable circumstances, people secretly turn away from their religion without even realizing it. When they wake up, they find that they have rolled far downhill. The ancients said: "Things go well, Dad. Bewitching people until old age." This statement should be called a wake-up call. Therefore, the conditions for testing and testing are very subtle, practitioners need to pay attention.

5. Minh Khao: - This is a clear challenge ahead without awakening. For example, a person with little talent and virtue, but is praised by flatterers for having many virtues, talents, and great blessings, then becomes arrogant, looks down on everyone, does bad things, and ends up being defeated miserably. Or a person has the ability to progress high on the path, but is hindered by others, such as saying that being a vegetarian will make you sick, reciting Buddha reciting mantras too much will cause you to lose karma, encounter many bad things, then give birth to fear and fear, losing your mind. Or there are situations where you know that if you proceed, you will easily lead to failure, but because of ambition or pride, you still pursue it. Or for external conditions, although we know they are false, we cannot let them go, and then bring sadness to our hearts.

It's like there was a monk who spent a lot of money hiring stone cutters, carpenters, and masons to build a big temple on the mountain. When the monastery was just completed, the monk was exhausted and seriously ill. When he was about to die, he sent his disciples around the pagoda to touch the sad stone and cry in mourning!

Once upon a time, there was a monk whose position in the religion was quite high. His personality was sincere and generous, and he loved giving, but he had a weakness: he was often arrogant. Some dignitaries saw that place, brought a general to pretend to visit, and then took the opportunity to look at the monk and praise him for his many blessings. He certainly won the support of countless people, and his fame and success increased. He added that if he liked being active, he would become a leader, and like in real life, he could become president. After hearing this, although he was humble for a few moments, he appeared extremely happy. On that occasion, the politicians lamented the times, felt sorry for the suffering people, and the country's deteriorating fortunes, and gradually persuaded the monk to participate in a political campaign. And because of that, the monk had an accident for quite a long time.

That's why easy-going and gullible people are often deceived. When ambition has not been eliminated, it is easy to be enticed by others using money, beauty or status. If you still have a hot-tempered personality, you will easily be provoked by people and take on troublesome things. These are the pitfalls of life but also of religion. We would like to point them out to advise each other. If we are not careful about these points, we will fall into the cycle of karma. Regarding such challenging conditions, the practitioner must discern clearly, and be determined to follow the path of morality to be able to overcome them.

6. Dark Examination: - This refers to a silent challenge that is not obvious. If the practitioner does not pay careful attention, it will be difficult to notice. There are people who are initially diligent in reciting the Buddha's name, but then because their family fortune gradually declines, they fail at whatever they do, and become worried, depressed, and delay their practice. Some people have their work quietly progressing smoothly, then they indulge in pursuing profits and forget the path of practice. There are people who chant diligently at first, but because of lack of self-reflection, their inner afflictions increase a little each day, gradually giving rise to laziness. Sometimes they cannot recite the Buddha's name for several months or even a few years. There are some people whose lives are still in complete harmony, but because of changes in external times, their lives and homes change from day to day, their minds are always confused and look outward, unconsciously forgetting to meditate.

The above are all effects of good and evil karma, but it has the power to secretly attract practitioners and make them neglect their practice, so it is called "chao". When first practicing, everyone had a point of kindness, but one by one, due to internal and external karma conditions, one hundred people lost ninety-nine. The old saying: "Practice Buddha for the first year in the past, Buddha for the second year in the West, and Buddha for the third year at the beginning." This sentence has the meaning: The first year of Buddha's practice is as before, the second year Buddha has gone west, in the third year anyone who wants to ask about Buddha or recite Buddha's name must pay money to talk about it, or recite too few sentences. This parable also points to the points above that practitioners need to pay attention to.

---o0o---

Section B. Methods of Dissolving Obstacles

tom_tat: When he first entered the temple, the author heard a legend that contained hidden meanings, but did not know if it was true to the original language, and where it came from? That sentence is: "Buddha is one foot tall, ma is one foot tall, Buddha is one foot tall, ma is so tall...
noi_dung:
Section 64 - Co Duc's Advice

When he first entered the temple, the author heard a legend that contained hidden meanings, but did not know if it was true to the original language, and where it came from? That sentence is: "Buddha is one foot tall, demon is one foot tall, Buddha is one foot tall, demon is higher than the head of the staff, Buddha is sublime than the head of the staff, demons surrender to Buddha." The meaning of this sentence is: "Buddha is one meter tall, mama is one meter tall. The Buddha is one foot tall, the devil is above the head of the staff; If the Buddha is any higher than the head of the staff, the ghost will surrender to the Buddha." Reflecting on the above sentence, the practitioner must make his Buddha higher than the ghost, otherwise he will be overthrown by the demonic obstacle. Therefore, in the monastic village, those who are corrupted should not blame circumstances or blame anyone, but only blame their Buddha for losing to the ghost. If you try to keep your wish, the evil obstacles will be eliminated. Because he knew there were many obstacles on the path of practice, in the past, the Great Master Bodhisattva Bodhisattva taught four virtues as a guideline for his disciples. Those four virtues are: Reporting unjust conduct, depending on fate, worthy of Dharma and seeking happiness without reason.

1. Why is it called Oan Hanh Newspaper? - We have always committed samsara in the six realms, each life causes karma, either kindness or resentment, from small things to big things, which can be said to be limitless and boundless. Therefore, when we practice the Dharma, although the merit of our practice is partly eliminated, the karma has not yet dissipated, so we must pay it back one by one. Like an ordinary person who is sick or disabled, because of his previous life he created karma to kill living beings. People who receive many compliments and criticisms in their past lives rely on their intelligence and power to look down on others, or they have created destructive karma. People suffer from poverty and lack because in their previous lives they did not have compassion and practiced giving. People are shackled, tortured and imprisoned, because their previous lives used to bind, beat, and imprison living beings. The lonely person lacks a support person because in his previous life he was not happy to make love with people. Such karma is limitless and limitless. Nowadays, when you practice wrongly, you must calmly and patiently pay for it, and should not complain or be sad. In the samsara life, all sentient beings eat and drink with the couple's family, so among the karmas, the karma of friction and the karma of craving are the heaviest. The ancient monk lamented: "The pool of karma is vast, nothing more difficult to break than desire. The world is barbaric, the only thing that can be committed is killing!"

- The author once heard a North Vietnamese Buddhist recount the story, but because it had been so long, he only remembered the general outline and forgot the names and addresses of the people involved. Those Buddhists said: "There was a monk who was a former teacher. Because he was awakened to the ephemeral world, he went to meditate in the mountains. After a while, the monk was told by the gods: He had a debt of nineteen years with a girl whose last name was that. Although he had now practiced and should not get married, he had to go down to the mountain to teach her enlightenment, pay off the debt on time, and then return to the mountain to practice in order to be successful. The monk went down the mountain and sure enough, he met a girl whose name and surname were exactly as the gods had told him, and he fell in love with her. The monk advised her to teach her the Dharma, returned the robe on time and then went up the mountain. When she said goodbye, she was still so attached and crying. This is the repayment of the debt of karma craving.

In the story of Quan Tien, on the occasion of mid-autumn festival, the writer Van Tieu went to the mountains to play. On the night of the full moon, he witnessed fairies lifting seeds from the clouds and landing them on a stone table, setting out a feast of delicious fruit and precious wine, while playing and singing:

Autumn night one minute one minute

The moon cleverly illuminates this mountain scene!

Tilt your gourd and ask your confidant

Hang Nga is out of sight, where can I find her?

At the fairy's side, there was a girl named Thai Loan. She had a gentle beauty and sang the best songs. Even though Van Tieu was secretly listening, she was also shocked and moved. A moment later, an old fairy finished drinking and sang:

Fate meets each other at the fairy altar

Winning Van Tieu at Thai Loan price!

Hearing those two sentences, Van Tieu had to show his face to attend the fairy altar. The immortals told the fairy Thai Loan that she had been in a relationship with Van Tieu for thirteen years, and told her son to take out the book and erase her previous records. And after thirteen years of living with Van Tieu, the love affair was over, Thai Loan used the magic to hide and fly back to the mountains to practice again. Therefore, the immortals are still in the cycle of cause and effect.

Regarding karma, like the Venerable Lion in India and the Second Patriarch Than Quang in China, although they both attained enlightenment, on the day of death they still had to peacefully be beheaded to pay for their debts. Like Maudgalyayana, although he attained Arhat, the highest supernatural power among the Sravakas, but because he wanted to pay back his karma, he let the villains beat him to death with stones and sticks, and his body was buried in the cesspool. The Buddha felt sorry for him and sent his disciples to take his body up to wash it clean, rub it in fragrant oil, and then take it to the temple to collect the relics. And like the crown prince of An Tu left the home life to practice and attain enlightenment, using Su Mang Tri to see that he still had the karma left to kill living beings, so he transferred his life three times to Luoyang in China to pay his life debt three times. In his last life, he was the monk An The Cao.

Therefore, on the path of practice, we do not know who is perfect. We should not be complacent and look down on others. Because the karma of sentient beings is so great, sometimes one layer of compensation comes after another. Many people seem to have free time and are not unjustly wronged, but that is not necessarily because they do not have it, it is just because the time has not come for them to repay that fate. To end injustice, we must patiently repentance and try to practice to eliminate it. Poet Nguyen Du may have deeply believed in the theory of karma and the reformation of cause and effect by the Buddha, which is why he has the sentence:

Has brought karma into the body

Don't blame the sky near or far

There is heaven and there is also me...

This statement has been recognized by many wise people.

2. What is Dependent Fate? - This is talking about the peaceful destiny of the person who cultivates any scene and lives according to that scene. Like the rich scene depends on the rich, the poor scene depends on the poor, the barbaric scene depends on the barbarian, the tribulation scene depends on the tribulation, to the scene of success and decline, blessings, blessings, gain and loss... are all the same. To have peace according to fate is to be rich without being arrogant, to be poor and miserable without being sad and having a change of heart. Why? Because all blessings, blessings, and blessings are illusory, depending on karma that appears for a while and then disappears, is there anything worth getting attached to and feeling sad about?

Once upon a time, Confucius and his disciples were besieged by enemies in the Tran Kingdom of Thailand. They were without food for seven days, but he still played the piano and smiled. Tu Cong asked: "Why is it that when faced with life and death situations that have no fixed date, you can still laugh and smile?" He replied: "What happened that I tried my best to do was like this? It's the fate of God. What's the use of being sad and crying?" Confucius can be called a wise man, always calm and clear-headed, not flustered by any situation. Cultivators should be like that, they must consider fields, gardens, houses, relatives, and property as temporary predestined conditions, and not become attached or preoccupied with them, only then can they advance on the path of liberation.

3. Why is it called Worthy Dharma Hanh? - "France" This is the True Dharma, for Pure Land practitioners it is Buddha Samadhi. When practicing meditation, when walking, standing, lying, and sitting, the mind must be in harmony with the True Dharma, like water and water, like emptiness and emptiness. Practitioners who practice Pure Land are the same, their minds are always focused on reciting Buddha. Ancient virtue said: "If you temporarily do not stay in the right concentration, you are like a dead person." Because you cannot stay in the right place of concentration, it means being robbed by the worldly realm. Being robbed and enticed by the worldly world, the dharma body's life and wisdom no longer exist. Therefore, if a Pure Land practitioner constantly abides in the recitation of Buddha, his mind will gradually become calm and clear, sympathize with Buddha, and will certainly be reborn.

4. What is Selfless Pursuit of Happiness? - The Tao is for pure conduct of mind without wishing for anything. Because all dharmas are like illusions, arising and then passing away, passing away and being born again, what truth is there to hope for? Besides, worldly dharma is relative, in disasters there are blessings, in blessings there are disasters, so the wise person remains calm, in times of prosperity and disaster, blessings are not moved. For example: When a monk retreats to a deserted hermitage, life is gloomy, few people visit him, and although life's fate declines, his religion is strong. A little while later, if a devout person learns about making offerings and gradually builds a large pagoda and the monks gather in large numbers, then the blessings may be successful but the liberation part will decline, because he is preoccupied with dealing with outside affairs. The same is true for blessings that depend on each other. Therefore, a practitioner's mental conduct is not to seek evil deeds, or to become a sentient being, nor to seek good deeds, or to become a Buddha. Someone asked: "If chanting Buddha's name does not pray for rebirth, and does not pray for the blessings of perfect wisdom to become a Buddha, how can we progress?" Answer: "Because Buddha is empty, the more you seek, the farther you get, the more you lose." Therefore the Lotus Sutra says: "Suppose there are countless Sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas and Bodhisattvas who, after countless eons of thinking and searching, still cannot understand the Buddha's true wisdom." Regarding rebirth, the practitioner's way of praying is to pray without praying, to pray without praying. That application is like the surface of a clear mirror. When the image comes, it shines, when the image goes, it is quiet and empty all the time. If you keep seeing, knowing and seeking, you will be lost in delusion. If you don't see and know what to seek, you are like ignorant wood and stone! Broadly speaking, the practice of Non-Consciousness includes all three subjects: No, Formless, Vowsless.

If one practices according to the four virtues taught by Patriarch Bodhidharma, one can be calm in the face of all obstacles.

---o0o---

tieu_de: Section 65 How to Maintain a Steadfast Mind and Not Rot
tom_tat: In the treatise on Reciting the Buddha's Precious King Samadhi, there is an explanation of the Ten Non-Sought-For Virtues, meaning the ten un-sought-for actions, to destroy the ten great obstacles. These ten obstacles include all obstacles. So if you master…
noi_dung:
Section 65 How to Maintain a Steadfast Mind and Not Rot

In the treatise on Reciting the Buddha's Precious King Samadhi, there is an explanation of the Ten Non-Sought-For Virtues, meaning the ten un-sought-for actions, to destroy the ten great obstacles. These ten obstacles include all obstacles. Therefore, if you master these ten non-seeking practices, all obstacles will be eliminated. Those ten virtues are:

1. The body does not seek illness. If the body does not suffer from illness, greed and lust can easily arise. Being greedy for birth destroys the precepts and rots the path.

2. Life without prayer or hardship. Without hardship in life, arrogance easily arises. When pride and luxury arise, contempt will overwhelm everyone.

3. Cultivate your mind without seeking and without obstacles, if your mind is without obstacles, your learning will be outstanding. If you study beyond your limits, it's a mistake not to think you've achieved it or understood it.

4. Establishing virtue without seeking will not be hindered by demons. If one's conduct is without evil obstacles, one's vows will not be strong. If the vow is not steadfast, there will be a mistake of not realizing it, thinking that it has been realized.

5. Planning without asking is easy to achieve. When things are easy to achieve, thoughts of contempt arise. If you think contemptuously of birth, you will inevitably make the mistake of thinking that you have enough virtue and talent.

6. Communicate well without asking for personal benefits. If we gain benefits, we will lose morality. Morality is lost, only one's faults can be seen.

7. For those who cannot ask for approval. People who are obedient are easily arrogant. And when the heart is arrogant, it only sees its right side.

8. Please do not ask for anything in return. If you want to repay something, there is room for calculation in your heart. If you have plans, you will definitely be greedy for profit and fame.

9. If you see benefits, don't ask for your share. If you pray for a share, your ignorance will stir. When ignorance arises, it will inevitably destroy your reputation.

10. Being wronged doesn't ask for excuses. If you seek justification, your ego will not end. The mind of humanity, ego, and philandering has not ended, so many resentments will arise from it.

Thinking through the above points, we see that life is full of obstacles, which can be summarized in 10 things:

1. Body is sick

2. Having trouble

3. Studying is hindered

4. When establishing evil deeds, obstacles are destroyed

5. The plot failed

6. Friends react indifferently

7. Many people oppose

8. Please take offense

9. People who plot to gain fame and fortune

10. Suffer injustice

In these ten things, the Bao Vuong Samadhi commentary used ten actions of not seeking to destroy them. So in blessings there is disaster, in disaster there are blessings, in blessings there is hindrance, in hindrance there is clearance. Because of understanding this reason, ancient practitioners used "obstacles as conditions for advancement." Tien Duc said: "Without human views, the path is difficult to achieve!" This sentence means: "If you are not influenced by others, your path and fruition will be difficult to achieve." Because contempt, scolding, slander, and all other obstacles are "the level to measure a practitioner's moral power." If one encounters those obstacles and still manages to persevere peacefully, it must prove that one has advanced to a fairly high level of cultivation. Otherwise, how can we measure our progress? In fact, it is not that practitioners hope for obstacles, but because the path is full of difficulties and uncertainties, they need to always be vigilant and place themselves in front of all obstacles, so that when faced with a difficult situation, they can still be calm and not disturbed. Master Dieu Hiep said: "The above ten virtues can only be applied by a wise and courageous person. If you know how to consider enlightenment and maintain these ten things, then even though you enter the realm of demons, you will not be corrupted by demons. Even in the midst of beauty and silence, fame and fortune, love and hate, ups and downs, success and failure, gain and loss... Still at peace."

So if you don't know, all the good and favorable things can become obstacles to the path. If we see that all illness, suffering and demonic obstacles are false and have no basis, they will certainly not be able to do anything. For the above ten things, the way of using wisdom is:

1. Use illness and suffering as good medicine.

2. Using tribulation as liberation.

3. Use obstacles as targets.

4. Take demons as your Dharma friends.

5. Take difficult things to make you happy.

6. Take bad friends for help.

7. Use the enemy as a flower garden.

8. Forgetting to do favors is like forgetting to put away a torn sandal.

9. Use frugality to become rich.

10. Use injustice as a predestined path.

See here to clearly understand whether good or bad, success or failure still depends on the mind. Therefore, beginners are very afraid of obstacles, but those who have practiced for a long time sometimes want to try to cope with obstacles. Let me tell you a few stories for reference:

In ancient times, Than Quang, after attaining Dharma with Bodhisattva Dharma, immediately retired to work as a hired laborer, such as chopping firewood, pounding rice, or guarding doors for people. Someone came and asked: "You are the successor to the Patriarch, why do you lower yourself to do such trivial things?" He replied: "I want to subdue my mind, it's not where you know!"

Another fairy, Luu Truong Sanh, after becoming single, flew in a trance to Ms. Dieu Tri Kim Mau. Seeing the fairies' extremely beautiful and difficult to describe, he was immediately moved. Kim Mau scolded: "Even though you have attained enlightenment, your love for beauty has not disappeared. How can you be worthy of being ranked among the immortals?" Truong Sanh was ashamed, returned to the human world, used the magic of turning stones into gold, went to a brothel and hired five or seven of the most beautiful prostitutes to live together. For two years he lay near naked prostitutes to practice eliminating thoughts of lust. When he judged that his mind was unmoved, he asked the girls to make cakes, then put the cakes on the belly of the Duan Dien fire, cooked them, served them to them, spoke enlightenment to them, and then rode the clouds and flew away.

To compare the practices, let me tell you a few more stories:

- A certain nun wanted to get rid of her mistakes and vowed to enter into a retreat and be silent for three months. That afternoon, she was sitting by the window reciting the Buddha's rosary. A monk saw her and immediately talked to her friend, telling her she had a lot of karma and bad qualities. She felt angry and blushed, but remained silent and continued chanting Buddha. Moments later, the priest said: "I spied this girl marrying a man next door." She was so angry that she couldn't help but say loudly: "You said you have to confirm who I'm marrying, but I won't let this matter go?" The elder smiled and replied: "That's because I intentionally tested you. She had vowed to remain silent, so why were she still talking? Besides, quieting your mouth is essential to calming your mind, but if you can't calm your mind, then what's the use of quieting your mouth?" After hearing this, the nun suddenly came to her senses and remained silent in shame.

- One day, the writer went to Hue Nghiem Buddhist Academy and met the chairman of Thuyen Lam Pagoda. While talking, he told the story: "In the past, outside China, there was a monk who practiced meditation quite elaborately, and could sit for up to six or seven hours at a time. Perhaps wanting to get rid of predestined relationships, the monk often avoids women. Even if she visits the temple and then returns, he carries water to clean her seat. Some time later, the monk came to stay at Thap Thap Pagoda in Binh Dinh. One morning, while meditating in the temple, the monk suddenly screamed and ran out. Venerable Thap Thap asked the reason, the monk replied: "I was doing meditation and suddenly saw a beautiful woman come and hug my neck." After speaking, the monk was tired and lying down in the afternoon. He called Venerable Thap Thap in and said: "You have to urgently find a wife for me, otherwise starting this afternoon I will go on a hunger strike until I die?" Mr. Thap Thap called a trusted Buddhist woman to discuss. She said: "Let me go call my maid and tell her to pretend to be okay so I can entice you to eat and drink well and you'll be fine." The next morning, the monk brought the maid in and said: "I have finished discussing, there is this girl willing to be your wife." The monk heard that he opened his eyes, took a look, held the maid's hand and stroked it for a while, then passed out."

In the two passages above, we see that the nun wanted to destroy afflictions, but only in form. And Mr. Than Quang knows that all afflictions are empty, and that the root is in the mind that clings to self, so he pretends to be a lowly person and is scolded by others, to see if the mind of human, self, and non-self is still moving in order to end it. And Luu Truong Sanh wanted to destroy the thought of love for form, so he dared to boldly go right to the place of female form and contemplate destroying it. That monk, because he did not understand that form is empty, was too afraid of female form, and in his heart was still afraid of form, and ended up being harmed by the demon of form. Recall that in 1960, Buddhists brought the newspaper Tieng Chuong, showed a picture of a Japanese monk shaking hands with a naked woman, only wearing small pants, and criticized the modern practice as contrary to morality. Fake Pen explained: "Don't misunderstand, that is the way of examining the mind of Japanese meditation masters, to see if they are still attracted to female form? If they are not yet motionless, they will return to practice again. This monk has meditated to a pretty high level, so he dared to do that."

To conclude, a wise person not only does not mind obstacles, but also borrows obstacles to advance his practice. They are no longer attached to form, because form is only the means and the inner mind is the end.

---o0o---

Section C. Examples of Patience

tieu_de: Section 66 - The Patience of the Layman Tien Van Dat
tom_tat: Tien Van Dat, nicknamed Duc Son, was born in Thuong Thuc, Mai Ly town, from the Qing Dynasty in China. When he was young, Van Dat followed the karma family and specialized in selling alcohol. After that, he changed his profession, practiced mindfulness, practiced pure karma, and tried his best to correct his mistakes...
noi_dung:
Section 66 - The Patience of the Layman Tien Van Dat

Tien Van Dat, nicknamed Duc Son, was born in Thuong Thuc, Mai Ly town, from the Qing Dynasty in China. When he was young, Van Dat followed the karma family and specialized in selling alcohol. After that, he changed his profession, practiced mindfulness, practiced pure karma, and tried his best to correct his previous mistakes. Van Dat only had one son. Unfortunately, he fell ill with tuberculosis, chanted Buddha's name, and passed away. The neighbors laughed and said that because I was so worried about practicing, I died. He heard that and smiled, still peacefully worshiping Buddha as before.

One night, the house caught fire. Van Dat clasped his hands and looked up into the sky, praying: "My karma is heavy, I deserve to have my property destroyed, please don't hurt the nearby houses." After the fire went out, only his house was reduced to ash, the nearby houses were all fine. After trying to arrange a temporary place to live, Van Dat advised his mother, Ngo Thi Thi Trai, to recite Buddha, and his mother did as he was told. Next, he also became a vegetarian himself, but because old habits still existed, he often drank alcohol. But thanks to the advice of his relative, layman Ta Phung Ngo, he tried to gradually get rid of it.

In the spring of Dao Quang's twenty-second year, his wife died of illness, and Van Dat still lived alone. Many people advised him to follow the myth, but he refused and said: "If you have a child and die early, what's the point of getting married again? Besides, my will is in the place of origin, not in the line of succession!" In the summer of that year, he suffered from hemorrhagic fever, his desire to escape from the world became even stronger, and he still tried to recite the Buddha's name. By the beginning of July, his illness became worse, and he immediately vomited after eating. Phung Ngo came to visit and comforted him and said: There was an ancient monk who fasted to see the Buddha. Van Dat heard this and happily said: "If there is such a convenient thing, I will try my best to do it." The next day, he took a bath, went to the Buddha's table, chanted incense, made vows to stay young for seven days, and spent money to buy life-giving objects to pray for the Pure Land. After that, he recited Buddha's name non-stop day and night, and when he was thirsty, he only ate melon. Someone asked: "If you don't sleep all night like that, are you tired?" Van Dat replied: "Thanks to not sleeping, I can recite Buddha a lot. When I'm not sick, I'm not at ease. Now, when I'm sick, I'm free to work hard, I'm not tired at all!"

Seven days had just ended, because he was exhausted and his consciousness was confused. The family gave me some porridge to eat, so I felt sad and full, and the commotion became even worse. Van Dat was scared, clasped his hands on the pillow, and told him to knuckle making offerings to Buddha. Phung Ngo says: "If you realize that wish now, it's like burning your fingers. It's better to let go of all fate and single-mindedly seek Ultimate Bliss! He heard that and immediately closed his eyes and recited the Buddha's name. At first, he seemed to be still struggling, but then, thanks to using strong strength, his spirit gradually calmed down. Fortunately, thanks to dozens of fellow believers who heard the news and came to help recite, day and night in his house, the sound of reciting Buddha's name continued endlessly.

On the afternoon of the 10th day, Van Dat said that he saw a person walking in front of his bed, telling him not to eat melons or fruits. When asked, he claimed to be a messenger from the upper world. The next day, he suddenly saw the three good saints of the West standing in front of him in the middle of nowhere. He wanted to go up and sit on the golden stage, when suddenly he heard a voice saying: "Your body is not clean yet!" Next, all the generals disappeared. Van Dat immediately told him to cook fragrant water for me to bathe. After bathing, Tam Thanh appeared as before. He called his family back and said: "I walked around Pure Land, saw countless lotus flowers, I sat on a flower base, the joy was indescribable!" Pointing to himself again, he said: "This is not my body."

Early in the morning of the twelfth day, Van Dat said goodbye to his mother and said: "Buddha and the saints have filled the house." Having finished speaking, he immediately clasped his hands and recited Buddha's name and passed away. At that time, he was thirty-seven years old.

- Like layperson Tien Van Dat: When encountering adversity, the initial mind does not rot; when suffering from illness, mindfulness remains steadfast. At the end of the relationship, the world is washed away, the pure scene is revealed, the mysterious point of the golden stage, the serene body plays in the jade realm, the high dignity is no longer in doubt. Oh! Patience is so strong!

---o0o---

The Patience of the Layman Pho Xuan Pho

Fu Xuyen, surnamed Xuan Pho, a person from the Republic of China period, was from Dong Quach commune, Thanh Giang district, Jiangxi province. When he was young, he lost his father early. His mother, Mrs. Nhiep, was a devoted wife and patiently raised him and encouraged him to study until he became a man.

Xuan Pho has held positions such as: instructor at Thanh Giang district, police chief at Chu Dam town, and principal of Nghia Nghia school in Chuong Tho. He is an intelligent and diligent person who always attends public affairs. Whenever there is a difficult matter, officials are often invited to ask for help in solving the problem.

The royal family has long worshiped Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, and recited Buddha's name for a long time.

In the seventeenth year of the Republic of China, the mother-in-law became ill. He made vows at the Pho Da dynasty to pay homage to the Great Master, thanks to which the illness healed itself without medicine. In September of the twentieth year of the Republic of China (1931), Xuan Pho arrived at Putuo to complete his vows. When he sincerely bowed to Pham Am, Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva appeared in the form of a white robe, holding a vase and a willow branch. He again asked Bodhisattva to reveal his past life, seeing that his previous life was a monk with a monastic practice, dressed in rudimentary clothes.

Due to that incident, Xuan Pho awakened, knew that samsara was not a myth, and his desire to emerge from the world became even more earnest. He asked Dharma Master Nguyet Tinh to introduce to him Mr. Quang and Dharma Master Duc Sum at Bao Quoc pagoda in Suzhou province, and then heard the essence of the Pure Land sect. After that, all the scriptures published in Hoang Hoa Xa were given as gifts. Thanks to that, his understanding of Buddha's teachings became more profound. At that time, Xuan Pho decided to go straight to the path, took refuge and received the Upasaka precepts from the Dharma Master Duc Sum, whose Dharma name was meditation Xuyen, from Hang Tay.

After entering the religion, lay people have deep faith in their vows and diligently recite the Buddha's name without delay. In the twenty-second year of the Republic of China, he was invited to lead a lecture at Niem Buddha Lam in Loc Giang, leading and encouraging many people to practice. Lay people are physically weak and often get sick, but because of their integrity, their family is still poor and is often in debt. Because of coldness, life's love is often weak, karma is discovered, and there are many scandals. He always wanted to leave the home life, but because of his luck, the opportunity was not convenient. Even though they are surrounded by family and constraints, because of their sincere wish to be weary of the world of depravity and seek rebirth, the layperson still diligently celebrates, even when he is sick, he tries his best, never making a mistake.

In the spring of the twenty-seventh year of the Republic of China (1938), lay people dreamed that Avalokitesvara appeared and told them that the time would come in the second week of the seventh month. On the full moon day, after the Vu Lan Bon festival, the lay person fell ill, but still single-mindedly recited the Buddha's name, almost forgetting the illness and suffering, drinking and eating. On the twenty-sixth day, the illness got worse, the family members cried, and the lay people smiled and said: "I will be reborn on the day of Ksitigarbha's soul. Be happy, don't be sad." On that day, the lay person sat cross-legged in his chair, made the Amitabha mudra, looked intently at the Buddha statue, and then peacefully passed away. At that time, his face suddenly became brighter and brighter than when he was born, his body gradually became cold, only the top of his head was still hot.

After the lay person's rebirth, the chairman of Thong Tue Pagoda and the Dharma Master Dai Nhan came together to take care of the examination, and the lay person's physical body still sat upright as in normal times. Before that day, the wind and rain were very strong, but at midnight, when the fire was lit for the cremation ceremony, the sky suddenly brightened, and a strange scent drifted in, neither the smell of agarwood nor the scent of orchids. From the roof of the prison, a beam of white light shot up into the void, then flew straight to the West. At that time, in the first autumn, the climate was hot and hot, the lay person had been dead for three days but his body did not smell bad, but it emitted a fragrant scent and a bright light, so everyone praised it for its strangeness. At that time the layperson was forty-eight years old.

- At the end of the Dharma, many people recite Buddha's name, but few succeed, because they do not wish to believe deeply. Discussing the status of a man, Master Mencius said: "Wealth does not make you arrogant, poverty does not make you change your mind, power does not make you submissive." The world's dharma is still like that, let alone those who follow Buddha's Pure Land practice to seek transcendence and sainthood? Like layperson Pho Xuan Pho: Poor family, sick body, family burden, but still patiently passing by, focusing on Buddha's thoughts, thousands of praises and criticisms are not taken care of, hundreds of things are sharpened and broken without fraying. Thanks to that, when he was about to die, he knew the day and time in advance, and strange signs appeared. This is enough to see that Pure Land is the ultimate tragic wish of the Tathagata. If they are determined, no one can board the boat of liberation. After looking at the example of a lay person, I suddenly felt moved and asked myself: The original spiritual nature is still the same, why is the transcendence different? Cao Son's melody echoes there, who listens to Luu Thuy? You should write it down to advise others but also to remind yourself.

-ooOoo-

Chapter X: The Tenth Essential - Reciting the Buddha's Name Must Be Prepared for the Time of Death

Khai De:

On the side of the road a sad hearse passed by

That afternoon, the deserted tomb was misty and the moon was dark

The impermanence of this mortal life is so pitiful!

He left and then it was my turn.

Thousands of years ago in the mist

Talent disappears to infinity!

samsara does not seek the path of transcendence

Even if he is wise, why is he heroic?

Sunset with pink clouds in the distance

The flowers slowly dry with old age

Amitabha specializes in death prevention

Dreaming of the Lotus Heaven.
