Section A. Necessary Preparations for Final Death

tom_tat: Co Thi said: "I saw someone else die. Heart filled with sorrow! It's not about pitying the lost. Because it will be my turn!" In life, there is no greater sadness than death. But death is something no one can avoid. So…
noi_dung:
Section 67 - Preparation for Offshore Affairs

Co Thi said: "I saw someone else die. Heart filled with sorrow! It's not about pitying the lost. Because it will be my turn!" In life, there is no greater sadness than death. But death is something no one can avoid. Therefore, those who want to benefit themselves and others cannot help but prepare in advance. In fact, the word death is originally a pseudonym, because it is nothing more than the end of a period of retribution, due to karma passing between each life, when you give up this life, you will take on another life. Those who do not know Buddha's teachings still have to let karma turn around. Those who have heard the Pure Land Dharma of the Tathagata must believe and pray to recite the Buddha's name to prepare their thoughts, so that when they die, they can have a peaceful rebirth. Only then can we hope to soon escape the illusory suffering of samsara of life and death, and attain the true bliss of permanent Nirvana. People who have practiced Pure Land, not only care for themselves, but also for their parents, relatives and acquaintances, should develop filial piety and compassion, advise them to chant the Buddha's name, and support their chanting when they are seriously ill and at the point of death. That is the act of benefiting others, it is also the act of bringing blessings and good fortune to oneself in the next life.

• But preparing for death has many details, so let's first talk about external conditions. Pure Land practitioners, while still healthy, must plan ahead to find friends, especially those close to them, to support each other when they are seriously ill and at the point of death. Because most of us have heavy karma, even though we have tried our best, at those times we are afraid that when obstacles are discovered, our body is weak, our mind is unconscious, and it is difficult to maintain mindfulness. If you don't ask someone to help you, you will easily be subject to the flow of karma. Wouldn't a lifetime of cultivating be in vain? This is the first essential point.

• The second point is that when people recite Buddha's name when they feel weak, they should make arrangements for their future in advance, so that when they die, they won't have to worry. If you are leaving the home life, you must leave the temple affairs in the hands of your disciples and appoint someone to replace you to run Buddha's affairs. Like a layman, he gives his property, fields, and gardens, and divides them among his children and grandchildren, pre-arranging all fates. You must warn your relatives in advance, when you are seriously ill or dying, not to cry or show sadness. If you have love, you should calm down, because if you recite Buddha's name and pray, or support rebirth, that is true love.

---o0o---

tom_tat: Regarding external conditions as mentioned above, people who recite Buddha's name also have to mentally prepare themselves. What is that preparation method like? - On the path of practice, practitioners must have a spirit of liberation, from the money of the fields and gardens to the body...
noi_dung:
Lesson 68 - Mental Preparation

Regarding external conditions as mentioned above, people who recite Buddha's name also have to mentally prepare themselves. What is that preparation method like? - On the path of practice, practitioners must have a spirit of liberation, viewing everything from money from fields and gardens to relationships and relatives as temporary karma, living according to illusory circumstances, and dying completely empty. If we do not understand this principle, we will definitely hinder liberation, and sometimes we will have to become animals like dogs or snakes to guard the house and keep the door. There are many people who, because they hold on to money or relatives, have difficulty dying and cannot rest assured when they are about to die.

When the writer was still a priest, while offering late-night tea, he heard a Dharma teacher recount a story that contained the meaning of awakening. The plot is roughly as follows:

Once upon a time there were two fellow practitioners, one liked to live in high mountains, the other built a hut in the forest next to a stream. Some time later, the monk living next to the stream passed away first, and the monk on the mountain often came down to visit. After chanting the prayer sutras, the monk immediately sat still and meditated to see where his friend was born? But searching and observing everywhere, from heaven to hell, he could not see his friend anywhere. Coming out of meditation, the monk asked his friend's attendant: "What does your teacher do every day?" Dao Dong replied: "Bach, a few days later, because the sugarcane bushes in front of the hut were so plump and healthy, my teacher often went out to fertilize and prune the leaves, kept looking at them, and seemed very excited!" The monk heard that he entered concentration again and saw that his friend had turned into a worm in a sugarcane stalk. The monk immediately cut down that sugarcane tree, split it, caught the worm, and preached the Dharma and prayed for its liberation.

The above story is only an oral tradition and has not been found in the scriptures. But based on reason, that event is still not a myth. In the Buddhist scriptures, there are also some similar things. Such as: -The story of a novice monk who was greedy for eating milk and peanuts, so when he died, he became a cockroach in a milk bottle. - The story of Upasaka, although he had the merit of observing the precepts of practice, but because he was too attached to his wife, when he died, his consciousness was reborn as a proboscis in his wife's nose. When the wife was crying and blowing the nose of the proboscis, she was embarrassed and wanted to trample it. Luckily, an Arhat intervened, clearly stated the reason, and preached deliverance to the proboscis. - The story of the wife of a merchant traveling by sea, because she missed her beautiful beauty, when she died, she turned into a tentacle from her nose and crawled around her face, as Kinh Hien Ngu said. Therefore, Pure Land practitioners must be mindful and reflect every day, eliminate greed and love, and be determined to aim for the Buddha realm, so that when they die, they will not be dragged away by the power of karma.

• Master Tu Chieu said: "Pure Land practitioners, when they are about to die, often have three doubts, four barriers, or obstacles to rebirth. They must prepare and think in advance to eliminate the three doubts:

1- If you suspect your karma is deep and you have little time to practice, you may not be able to rebirth.

2- I suspect that my original vow has not been fulfilled, my greed, anger and ignorance have not ended, I am afraid I will not be reborn.

3- If you suspect that you are reciting Buddha's name, if Buddha does not come to receive you, you will not be able to be reborn.

The four gates are:

1- Or people who are sick and suffering come back and blaspheme the Buddha for not being spiritual.

2- Or, because of greed for life, you kill an offering.

3- Or while taking medicine, use alcohol and foul-smelling blood.

4- Or, because of love and attachment, you are bound to your family."

The great master mentioned the theory of Three Thoughts and Four Views above, wise people can think and find a solution. Now the author would like to take the liberty of briefly describing the method of subtraction to give comments, and fellow practitioners with their own understanding, can deduce and understand more broadly.

1. Breaking serious karma with little practice: - Amitabha Buddha once made vows: "If any living being has the heart to return to Ultimate Bliss, recite His name for up to ten times. If he cannot be reborn, He swears he will not become a Buddha." Buddha never lied, so practitioners must believe in the Buddha. Ten recitations is a very small amount of time to practice and still get rebirth, let alone reciting more than that number. No matter how heavy a person's karma is, such as breaking the precepts and creating all kinds of evil karma, if his repentance is based on Amitabha Buddha, he will guide him. Doesn't the Infinite Life Sutra say that a person who commits serious crimes against the five or ten evils will be reborn when he is about to die? In the rebirth story, like Truong Thien Hoa, Hung Tuan, Duy Cung, all their lives they killed cows and buffaloes, broke the precepts, and did evil. When they were about to die, the appearance of hell appeared, they were afraid and recited the Buddha's name, and immediately saw the Buddha coming to process them. Even starlings and parrots reciting Buddha's name can be reborn, let alone I'm not that bad?

2. Breaking the doubt of the original vow that has not been returned, greed, anger and ignorance that has not ended: - The practitioner's vow is roughly two: religion and life. Regarding religion, there are people who vow to build a giving pagoda or pray to recite a certain number of sutras and mantras, but before they complete it, it is time to die. Must think: Just believing in the Buddha's mind, when reborn, will bring about boundless merits, but the original vow is just a small thing, whether completed or not is of little consequence, and there is no harm at all. In life, there are people whose family responsibilities have not yet been fulfilled, such as aging parents with no one to take care of them, young wives and children lacking support, or there are people who have debts that have not yet been repaid, their wishes are not fulfilled, so their hearts are not at peace. Must think: When we are about to die, whether we worry or not, there is nothing we can do. If only by concentrating on reciting the Buddha's name, when one has been reborn in the West and attained enlightenment, all of the undesired vows can be fulfilled, and all enemies and relatives can be saved.

Lai Kinh Na Tien said: "For example, if a grain of sand is light, if put in water, it immediately sinks. On the contrary, even if the rock is heavy, if carried by a boat, it can be carried from one place to another. The same is true for people who recite Buddha's name. Even if their karma is light, if they are not saved by Buddha, they will definitely suffer from samsara. No matter how heavy their sins, if they are guided by Buddha, they will be born into Ultimate Bliss." According to the passage here, we see that Buddha Recitation is a dharma that can cause karma rebirth, because of the power of others. The big rock represents the power of great karma, the boat carrying the power of the Buddha's vow. So practitioners should not think that they still have greed, anger, or ignorance, lest they be reborn. The above example can completely destroy the doubt about heavy karma in the first point.

3. Destroy the Buddha's doubts, lest the Buddha will not come to receive you: - People recite Buddha according to their merits. When they die, they see Buddha, or Bodhisattva, or the Holy Assembly coming to receive them. Sometimes you don't see anything, but thanks to your prayer and the Buddha's silent power, your consciousness flies to the West. This is because our deeds have highs and lows, deep and shallow. All we need at that time is to think Buddha with all our heart, don't think about anything else. If you have doubts, obstacles will arise. In short, when you are about to die, don't worry about whether your appearance is good or not, just recite Buddha wholeheartedly until the last moment.

• Break through the four barriers: - Suffering from illness and suffering, slandering Buddha - greedy for life, killing and worshiping, praying for healing, drinking alcohol, or using medicine containing blood - because of attachment, one's mind is bound to the family.

People who chant the Buddha's name and suffer from accidents and sufferings are due to the merit of their practice, so they can turn the heavy consequences into light ones, turn the consequences into present retributions, and pay it all off to be born in the West. If you return to doubt and blaspheme, you are a person with little faith and understanding, betraying the Buddha's grace, causing yourself a sin. In the Pure Land legend, there is a story about Mr. Ngo Mao and many other Buddhists who, thanks to accumulating karma, were soon reborn. So when encountering this scene, people chanting Buddha should be conscious to understand clearly.

Again, this body is temporary, depending on the sin karma, life will be happy and miserable for a long time. If you kill a living being to nourish a living being, or make an offering, your sin and suffering will become even more serious. You must thoroughly rely on the Buddha and firmly believe in cause and effect.

When you are sick, you should only pray to Buddha. You should not pray to evil masters, or listen to the words of people who do not understand the religion, return to eating salty foods, drinking alcohol, or taking medicine with foul-smelling blood. This body is filthy, the sooner we can return to Buddha's world, the sooner we will be able to return to the Buddha's world, like giving up a tattered shirt and wearing a beautiful, fragrant uniform. Why should we bother?

As for the harm caused by attachment at the time of death, it is as said in the above paragraph. Must think: In the family, parents, brothers, spouses, and children all have debts and resentments in previous lives, so they are temporarily reunited. When the predestined relationship ends, everyone goes their separate ways. If we have compassion, it is better for us to give up our worldly feelings and seek rebirth in the West, to save all those who have wronged us. When death is about to come, even if we are attached, we cannot take it with us, there is nothing we can do, because our very body must still crumble into dust. If you fall in love, you will not be reborn and will suffer endless samsara.

The above points about the Three Nghi Tu and Four Precepts, the practitioner must contemplate and remember carefully, to prepare in advance for mental peace at the time of death.

---o0o---

Section B. The Urgency at the End of Time

tieu_de: Lesson 69 - Inviting the Knowledgeable One to teach
tom_tat: Pure Land practitioners, even when their illness is not severe, should take medicine, but still diligently recite Buddha's name, not thinking: Take medicine and you will be cured. When the disease is severe, medication may not be needed. When Master Hoang Nhut was seriously ill, he had…
noi_dung:
Lesson 69 - Inviting the Knowledgeable One to teach

Pure Land practitioners, even when their illness is not severe, should take medicine, but still diligently recite Buddha's name, not thinking: Take medicine and you will be cured. When the disease is severe, medication may not be needed. When Master Hoang Nhut was seriously ill, someone asked him to help him take medicine. He immediately gave thanks and recited verses:

Amitabha Buddha.

Is the supreme king of medicine.

If you leave here, don't pray

That's a crazy person!

A sentence in the name of Buddha.

It is the magical medicine Da Da.

If you leave here, don't drink.

What a big mistake!

Then he only concentrated on thinking about Buddha. Sure enough, my illness gradually improved.

Remember that when the illness is severe, the practitioner must let go of everything around him, including his own body and mind, and focus only on reciting the Buddha's name, wholeheartedly wishing for rebirth in the West. By doing so, if your life span has expired, you will be able to get rebirth. If your lifespan has not ended, even though you pray for rebirth, you will quickly recover from your illness. Because your heart is dedicated, you can eliminate the evil karma of your previous life. On the contrary, if you don't let go of all conditions and recite the Buddha's thoughts, then if your life span has expired, you will definitely not be able to be reborn, because you only pray for healing and not for rebirth, so there is no way to return to Ultimate Bliss. If your life span has not ended, not only will your illness not be relieved quickly, but your illness will increase. Because of your desire to heal your illness, hopelessness will give rise to sadness, worry, and fear.

There are many people who practice Pure Land. When they are seriously ill, their relatives, because they do not understand the Dharma, do not bother to promote the practice of reciting the Buddha. They return without wasting money to bring in many Eastern, Western medicine or witch doctors to pray for treatment or make offerings to quickly heal their illness. Doing so will cause the patient to not receive recitation support and become distracted, so they cannot be reborn. That is using money to buy filial piety or reputation, to show outsiders that you are a kind, caring person. They don't understand that Buddha Saints know whether they have the heart or not, not the appearance! That action makes wise people only smile in pity!

When the patient is in a lot of pain, but the consciousness is still clear, family members should invite a wise man to preach the Dharma for enlightenment. If there is no knowledgeable person, a fellow practitioner should be invited to comfort and teach. This person should advise the sick person's relatives, and use compassion to try to conduct everything in accordance with the religion, so that the person about to die can receive the benefits of rebirth. In general, teaching positions should follow the following details:

1. Talk about the suffering of Saha and the joy of Ultimate Bliss, and remind the patient to admire it. We should also clearly state and praise the patient's good deeds and practice, making the patient happy without doubt, knowing that when he dies, he will rely on that good karma to be born in the West.

2. If the patient has any doubts, he or she should explain it according to the theory of Three Nghis and Four Views in the above paragraph. The essential point here is to advise you to get rid of greed for property and attachment to family.

3. If the dying person has a will, then that's fine. Otherwise, the priest must intervene and advise relatives not to ask about the will. It is also advised not to talk uselessly, causing the patient to be moved by thoughts of love and attachment to the world, which could hinder rebirth.

4. When relatives or friends of the sick person come to visit, they should prevent the patient from coming in front of the patient to look sad and ask questions. If you come to visit because of affection, you should just stand nearby with your hands clasped and recite Buddha's name out loud for a while, that is truly affection. If you lack understanding and only use it according to conventional feelings, that is pushing people into the sea of suffering. Although the feelings are sympathetic, the consequences are pitiful.

5. Patients should be advised to donate their clothes and supplies to others. Or according to the Tathagata Praise chapter in the Ksitigarbha Sutra, it is even better to offer that material to the image sutra. This also helps the sick person gain more blessings and eliminate sins, making rebirth easier.

The teaching staff must pay attention to the above general things. In addition, you can improvise, it is impossible to say everything here.

---o0o---

tom_tat: From the moment the patient is in severe pain until the moment he is about to die, his relatives must stay calm and not cry. Even though some people don't cry, they show signs of sadness and sadness, which is also something that should not be done. Because at that time, the patient had...
noi_dung:
Section 70 - How to Support Recitation

From the moment the patient is in severe pain until the moment he is about to die, his relatives must stay calm and not cry. Even though some people don't cry, they show signs of sadness and sadness, which is also something that should not be done. Because at that time, the patient had come to the dividing line between demons, humans, mortals, and saints, with an unusually dangerous emergency, like a thousand pounds hanging under a strand of hair. At that time, single-minded support of reciting the Buddha's name is essential. Even if a person has the will to rebirth, if his relatives mourn and cause him to arouse thoughts of love, he will inevitably fall into samsara, and his efforts in cultivating will be in vain!

When a patient is about to die, if they want to bathe, change clothes or change their bed, they can comply, but they must do so gently and carefully. If they refuse, or are speechless, you should not do it reluctantly. Because a dying person's body is often in pain, if forced to move, change position, take a bath, or change clothes, the patient's pain will increase. Many people practice making vows to pray for Ultimate Bliss, but when they die, they are disturbed by their mobile relatives and destroy their mindfulness, so they cannot be reborn. This happens very often. Or a person who has died may be reborn in a good realm, but without someone else's knowledge, touching their body or changing their limbs causes pain, so they become angry. Because of that one thought, one immediately falls into an evil path, becoming a dragon, snake, tiger, leopard, or other poisonous species. Like King Ajatasatru who cultivated many good blessings, when he was about to die, his servant fell asleep and dropped the fan on his face, so he was angry and died as a python. Shouldn't this example be a warning?

When a sick person is about to die, he or she can sit or lie down, do it freely, don't try too hard. If you feel weak, you can only lie down, but if you want to show off and try to sit up, it's dangerous. Or normally, you should lie on your side facing west, but because your body is in pain you have to lie on your back, or lie on your left side facing east, just let it be natural and don't try too hard. This is what patients must understand and behave themselves. Relatives must also understand this reason, they should not seek fame, force the sick person to lie on his side facing west, or help him up, put on his robe, and sit cross-legged. Who knows that just to seek a little fame, it causes the dead to fall into the three realms and endure immeasurable suffering!

• When the patient is about to finish, recitation support is very necessary. Because at that time, mentally and physically sick people are weak and confused, and have difficulty controlling themselves. Don't say that ordinary people who haven't practiced can't keep reciting the Buddha's words for a long time; But ordinary people often take Buddha's recitation as a key. Without the help of reciting, it would be difficult to be effective. The method of supporting chanting must comply with the following conditions:

1. Ask for Buddha Amitabha's statue to be placed in front of patients so they can see it. Place a vase of fresh flowers and light a light incense burner with faint fragrant smoke to induce mindfulness in the patient. Remember, the smoke is only light, don't let it get too much because it will make it suffocating and make it difficult to breathe.

2. The person assisting in reciting should take turns chanting depending on how much or how little. At least one or two people at a time, divided into three sessions. At most, each session can have six or eight people. Remember that at that time, patients with weak health really need fresh air. If people are allowed to go into the winter, or there are too many people supporting the chanting, it will definitely make the patient agitated and stuffy, which will do more harm than good. Again, the sessions must follow the clock and alternate in silence, so that the chanting of Buddha continues without interruption, without calling out. Each chanting session lasts about an hour.

3. According to Mr. An Quang, four words should be recited so that patients can easily accept them while their mind and body are too weak. But Master Hoang Nhut's opinion is that if you want to recite four words or six words, it is better to ask the patient, in order to comply with the patient's favorite daily habits, so that they can recite silently. If we go against our favorite customs, that is, we destroy the patient's mindfulness, and we are also guilty. Another way to support recitation is not to recite too loudly, because you will lose breath and have difficulty sustaining it; Do not recite too softly, for fear that mentally ill people will be dull and have difficulty receiving it. You should not recite too quickly, because the patient will not be able to hear clearly and not be able to keep up; You should not recite too slowly, because the chanting sound is fragmented, making it difficult for the sick person to continuously focus on the mind. In general, the recitation must be neither high nor low, neither slow nor fast, each word and each sentence must be clear and distinct, allowing the recitation to pass through the ears and penetrate deeply into the sick person's consciousness, only then will it be effective. Another thing that should be noted is that when the patient's mind is too dull, the thoughts outside may not be heard clearly. In that case, you must put your mouth close to their ear and recite, only then can the sick person's mind be clear.

4. Regarding the dharma weapon to use while assisting in reciting, it is usually recommended to strike the dharma. Because the sound of the gong is dull and not as clear as the clear sound of the gong, it can easily make the patient's mind clear. But that issue also depends, because according to his own experience, Master Hoang Nhut taught: "People who are mentally weak are very afraid of hearing the sounds of gongs and bells. Because the sounds of these things are deafening and stimulate the nerves, making mentally ill people feel uneasy. In my opinion, just reciting it is most satisfactory. Or if there is, you should only play the big bell. These dishes have a majestic sound, causing the sick person to revere them, and are much more real than playing the flute and the small musk. You should not play the dull-sounding gong, because it will make the patient mentally ill. However, everyone's preferences are different, so it is better to ask the patient in advance. If there's something that doesn't fit, you have to change it according to the opportunity, don't be stubborn."

Above are a few points to note about how to support chanting.

---o0o---

Section C. Urgent Things After Completion

tieu_de: Lesson 71 - When Breathing Comes Off Until Time Goes Forward
tom_tat: For newbies, it is important not to rush to move. Or if a dead person's body is dirty, he should not rush to clean it. He must wait eight hours, or at least three hours, before he can wash and change his clothes....
noi_dung:
Lesson 71 - When Breathing Comes Off Until Time Goes Forward

For newbies, it is important not to rush to move. Or if the dead person's body is dirty, he should not rush to clean it. He must wait eight hours, or at least three hours, before bathing and changing his clothes. Before and after death, relatives are not allowed to cry. Because crying is useless and harmful, because it causes the doomed person to become attached and unable to achieve liberation. Only trying to recite Buddha's name will be truly beneficial for the deceased. If you want to cry, you have to wait eight hours. Why? Because even though the patient was out of breath, A Lai Da had not yet left consciousness. If at that time they shake, bathe, change clothes, or cry, they will still feel pain or be sad, angry, and sad, and will fall. This is very important, very important, so pay attention and remember carefully.

The theory of probing the heat to test where birth comes from, although there is evidence, should not be accepted. If the patient is normal and has sincere faith in their prayers, when they die with clear mindfulness, they can experience rebirth. Many people are not careful, they keep probing, touching here and there, stirring up thoughts of their loved ones, which is also very harmful.

After the patient dies, the person assisting in chanting must continue chanting Buddha for three hours, so that rebirth is guaranteed. After reciting, immediately close the door and watch carefully, lest cats, dogs or people who are not knowledgeable rush in and touch you. Wait until eight o'clock to shower and change your clothes. If during eight hours there is someone nearby reciting Buddha's name, it is very good. In addition, absolutely do not do anything else. Again, during this time, the dead still have feelings.

After eight hours, if the deceased's limbs are stiff and unable to move, a cloth soaked in hot water should be used to cover the joints. If you do this for a while, you can straighten your arms and legs as usual.

At the funeral of the deceased, relatives should keep it simple, not too cumbersome and waste nothing. It is necessary to use vegetarian food, not to kill for offerings. If you absolutely need some salty food, you should buy dead fish meat, or people who have prepared it and sell it in the market. If we kill living beings to offer sacrifices, we will certainly be wronged and unable to attain liberation. Even though the deceased has been reborn, his lotus rank is also lowered because of that.

In the past, the author and the Sangha chanted sutras deliverance for his friend's stepmother, Venerable Bao Hue, in Tan Hoi commune, Long An province. At the funeral, the writer saw that all vegetarian food was being used, and when he praised and asked questions, the monk replied: "The offering of vegetarian food was actually encouraged by me, but it was mostly motivated by something that happened in the upper neighborhood. There was originally a quite rich family, the homeowner was satisfied, the son killed many cows, pigs, chickens and ducks to entertain relatives and acquaintances near and far, for several days. When he was born, the homeowner was a gentle and kind person who often ate vegetarian and recited prayers and had a wide social life. After that funeral, in the afternoon, his soul entered his grandson's, his face red, he jumped up on the board, patted the table, called the child's name immediately, and shouted: "In my entire life, I practiced blessings, did not commit any serious sins, and should have been born in a rich place. Now that you have killed so many creatures to make offerings, I have been unjustly denied liberation. Currently, I am under house arrest and have to take care of a herd of cows, pigs, chickens and ducks, and run through the mud and thorns. It's extremely miserable!" After telling the story, the monk smiled and said: "Thanks to the fact that everyone knew about it, and it happened just a few months ago, my family was already scared and confident, so as soon as I proposed, it was immediately accepted." The Ksitigarbha Sutra also clearly states the dangers of killing living beings and offering sacrifices at funerals, so Buddhists should pay attention to it.

When serving as a Buddha to send off the deceased, relatives should bring that merit and dedicating merit to all sentient beings in the Dharma world. Thus, the merit will be greater, and the blessings of the deceased will also be increased.

In the above preliminary points about the time of death, most writers took the opinions of famous people such as Mr. Quang and Master Hoang Nhut to combine them. Because the moment of death is the most important time in a person's life. If you have not fully prepared for rebirth, then it will be difficult to avoid panic and confusion, you will not be able to call in time, evil karma from many lifetimes will appear at the same time, how can you achieve liberation?

Therefore, when you are about to die, even if you ask someone to follow the method to help you chant, but during the day you have to try to practice this way to be at peace.

Please make sure to prepare early to purify your karma so that you can receive the lotus products at the Lien Tri sea assembly.

---o0o---

tom_tat: Layman Liu Canh Liet, from Jiangxi province in China, when he was young, he went to study in Nhut Ban. After recovering, he served as a member of the National Assembly and as a local company leader. The layman's brother is Canh Hy, originally...
noi_dung:
Section 72 - Winning Examples of Support

1. The story of layman Liu Canh Liet

Layman Liu Canh Liet, from Jiangxi province in China, when he was young, he went to study in Nhut Ban. After recovering, he served as a member of the National Assembly and as a local company leader. The layperson's older brother, Canh Hy, is a mandarin and has long loved studying Buddhism, so the layperson also strongly supports and supports Buddhism. He did many meritorious things, such as restoring the ancient Tho Luong temple, working as a bourgeois to buy incense fields for the pagoda, and inviting the monk Dai Xuan to become an abbot. When Dharma Master Duc Sum proposed casting a twenty-eight meter tall bronze statue of Guan Yin Bodhisattva, lay people also went out of their way to collect donations until the Buddhist work was completed.

In the 22nd year of the Republic of China, Canh Liet, a refugee from the war, came to Suzhou, took refuge with Master Quang, and received the Dharma name Duc Thanh. From then on, he kept the six pearls and specialized in cultivating pure karma. Before entering Buddhism, Canh Liet liked to fish with bird nets, creating a lot of karma. Due to that evil cause, the layman later suffered from very serious Dokhau Sang scabies, pain and moaning day and night. In the midst of suffering, he made vows to eliminate evil karma, dedicatedly chanting the name of Avalokitesvara and suddenly heard a strange, sweet scent, and his illness gradually improved.

By the 25th year of the Republic of China, lay people returned to their homeland. Although his faith had developed, because he was too busy with life and religious matters, he was not yet dedicated to practice, and only recited Buddha's name a little every day. In the 27th year of the Republic of China, due to the karma of this life and the previous life, lay people became seriously ill again. After being in constant pain for a long time, he found it difficult to endure, so he told his son Luu Phat Trang to send money to Dharma Master Duc Sum to make offerings to Mr. Quang and perform meritorious deeds to quickly eliminate sins. The magician wrote a poem in response advising lay people to become young men, but it took him until the end of the year to actually practice it.

After the 28th year of the Republic of China, the illness of lay people became more serious. His wife and children were all disciples of Mr. Quang, knowing the urgency of his deathbed, and quickly invited the Sangha at Tho Luong Pagoda to help recite. On the nineteenth day of the first month of that year, the layman knew he was going to die, so he told his family to bring a chair to the front yard to sit in to change his mood. After calling his brothers to explain the future and telling his son Phat Trang to kneel and listen to the will, his expression suddenly changed. Seeing this, his wife and children immediately helped him into the house, brought the statue of Amitabha to place it in front of the lay people, and then together with the Sangha loudly chanted the Buddha's name. For several months, the layman had been sick with his entire left arm, but when he saw the Buddha statue, he suddenly became able to function as usual, his hands clasped, his mouth chanting Buddha's name, his face showing joy and joy. At that time, it seemed that he no longer felt pain. Depending on everyone's chanting of Buddha for a long time, he was then peacefully transformed.

Lay people rebirth at the age of sixty-one. The few months he suffered from illness were due to the karma of killing living beings turning into contempt in the present. At the time of death, thanks to the power of chanting, a good omen appears, which can be called: The senses are happy and beautiful, mindful and clear, and equanimous and peaceful, as if in meditation. So the rebirth of the West is no longer in doubt. At the funeral and entertaining guests, the whole family followed Lord Quang's instructions and used only vegetarian food, which everyone praised.

The fact that lay people are reborn is due to mature good roots, but also thanks to the power of chanting at the time of death. So for the last important point, you all need to pay close attention.

2. The story of laywoman Duc Hoang

Laywoman Duc Hoang is the wife of a Ly family member in Duong Chau. Because her husband had a concubine and she was unable to conceive, she found it difficult to rest at home, so she went to live with her step-mother, laywoman Dinh Duc Nguyen. Mrs. Duc Nguyen also loved her like her own child, the two sides relied on each other's intimacy for twenty years like one day.

Venerable Hoang, a layman, cultivated pure karma and was very diligent early in the morning. She and her stepmother thought that life's blessings would be blessed and that their relatives would be blessed, so they relied on each other and became Dharma friends on the path. When it comes to faith and practice during the day, each girl is far superior to Liu Canh Liet. It's just a pity that because of all the temptations of karma and faulty fate, she always encounters troubles and rarely has peace of mind.

In the 27th year of the Republic of China, seeing that the Wuhan region was about to be engulfed in war, mother and daughter immediately moved from Hong Kong to Ho town to temporarily seek refuge. At that time, because of high property prices, renting a house was very difficult, and staying in a hotel for a long time was more expensive and even more inconvenient. Fortunately, thanks to the compassionate monk Dieu Chan, he opened a quiet room at Thai Binh pagoda for her mother and child and three other displaced Buddhists to live together.

In the 28th year of the Republic of China, around March, layman Duc Hoang suddenly felt typhoid. After continuing until April, the medicine was ineffective. The illness gets worse every day. At that time, there were many things in the Buddha temple and few rooms. It would be inconvenient for her to die there, so her stepmother had to take her to the hospital. The programs here are all Western-style. If you want to be able to freely support recitation at the time of death, it is very difficult to be complete. The lay person Hoang entered the hospital for two or three days. She knew the Buddha Dharma and could not come and go to support her, so on the morning of the eighteenth day of the fourth month, she sat confused in the hospital. At that time, the laywoman was fifty-one years old.

Like Venerable Hoang, a lay person is truly a person with faith in practice. If at the time of death, the correct dharma is supported by recitation, then all good signs and signs of rebirth will not follow the Liu layperson. Because of the obstacle of fate, in this life she was not able to take advantage of the virtue of cultivating and reciting her thoughts in normal times, only creating causes for salvation later on. What happened was unfortunate for her, but it also shows us that support at the time of death is really important.

3. The story of layman Duong Lien Hang

Layman Duong Lien Hang, who lived during the Republic of China, was from Yu Dieu district, Zhejiang province. The poor man was a businessman from a young age, and was more polite than others.

In the eleventh year of the Republic of China, Lien Hang learned that his neighbor Dong Giac Hang practiced pure karma, and in his heart loved to come back and listen to instructions. After that, he took ordination as a Buddhist monk. Although the literature part is still weak, the understanding of the Buddhist scriptures' meaning is superior to others. In September of the Year of the Pig, friends in Lien Xa promised each other to vow to worship Bodhi. Lien Hang also attended that ceremony.

At the end of the spring of the year Giap Ty, due to illness, lay people secretly broke the precept of killing, thereby gradually distancing themselves from their associates. By July, his illness had gotten worse. When his fellow practitioners came to visit, everyone said he would die. Lien Hang also realized that it was difficult for him to live, so he was alert and repented of what he had done. In early August, he painstakingly came before the Buddha's table, wholeheartedly expressing his sincere repentance, vowing to keep the five precepts, vowing not to violate them again. From then on, the layperson let go of all fates, stopped craving, silently chanted the Buddha's name, and waited until his death. Friends knew that the lay people's recitation effort was still limited, so six days before his death, they invited someone to come and help him recite. A few days later, fellow practitioners also personally came to recite Buddha's name for help.

The recitation started on the twelfth of August. After the full moon day, Lien Hang suddenly felt light and refreshed. On the seventeenth day, the layman said in his dream he saw a halo of light like five or six dazzling electric lights. In the evening, looking at his appearance as usual, the associates thought it was not yet time, continued reciting Buddha until the second watch, and then were about to leave. They did not expect that at that time the recitation support would become pure and effective.

Lien Hang heard the Buddha's chant suddenly stop and said: "I haven't arrived in the West yet. I hope to ask all of you to help me recite it all night long." They heard strange words and chanted Buddha loudly. Less than half an hour later, the layman suddenly smiled and said: "I went to the West. Oh! That Bao pond is so big! Behold! Lotus flowers are so beautiful! The light is also incredibly bright and beautiful!" Then he told the crowd to raise their voices to chant and not to stop. Before, Lien Hang was still quietly lying still. By now his hands and head were both working, his mouth continuously saying loudly: "Oh! Lotus flowers are so fresh and beautiful! The treasure pond is so bright and beautiful!" At that time, the layman's face smiled happily, looking like someone who suddenly had a joy beyond his expectations. So an hour later, he returned quietly without speaking, without moving his arms or legs, just lying on his back, staring intently at the Buddha statue in front of the bed. Next, my eyes gradually became dull and my breathing became weaker and weaker. At five o'clock in the morning of the eighteenth day, the layman finally passed away.

That night there were only four people involved, but they took turns loudly supporting the chanting throughout the night, and occasionally interjecting a few words of encouragement. Continue reciting like this until an hour and a half after the lay person has passed out, then switch turns with the others who have just arrived. The chanting continues until the person's body is completely cold, and family members are prevented from crying. At ten o'clock in the afternoon, a friend tried to probe, but everywhere else was cold, only his head was still as hot as boiling water.

In the sutra, there is a verse that says:

Holy name, eyes born in heaven.

People's hearts, hungry ghosts' stomachs.

Bang gave birth to his knees.

Hell on the soles of your feet.

When a person dies in all other places, but only when the head is hot at the end, that person is reborn in the Holy Land, the Buddha Land; Hot eyes will eventually lead to birth in heaven; The place where the heart and chest feel hot will eventually lead to rebirth in the human world. If in the abdomen, that person is reborn in the realm of hungry ghosts, in the knees is reincarnated as an eagle; on the soles of your feet, you will surely fall into hell. Wherever the consciousness escapes from, that place is the last to get hot. The layman finally got angry, proving that he was reborn to Ultimate Bliss.

Like Lien Hang, a lay person, his precepts are not perfect and his practice is still poor. But there was no rebirth, it was all thanks to the chanting support of fellow practitioners. Looking here, we see that mindfulness support is very essential for practitioners at the time of death. At that time, it was July 18, the 13th year of the Republic of China (1924), the layperson was thirty years old.

The Last Word

The ancients said: ã The poetry depends on the literary age. Ê This is what it means: Writing a book should wait until you are old, because the older you are, the more knowledge and experience you have, so the value of the book can be fulfilled. Authors are not yet in their old age, so their experience and understanding are bound to have many shortcomings, but because of the urgent need to benefit others, and not knowing when impermanence will come, so I try my best to use my ignorance as an offering to fake knowledge. Although this is said to be an original work, most of it draws from the Buddha's sutras and the opinions of ancient monks and wise men. So I think it can also bring some benefit to readers.

In the past, Master So Thach had two verses:

The birth of a thousand years of life is seven weeks of hy.

Returning from the past to the end of enlightenment!

These words were uttered while He was in his seventies, lamenting: Although a human life is said to be a hundred years, it is very rare to live to be seventy years old, and at the age of seventy like Him, when looking at the past, he sees that he has all made mistakes. If a high-ranking monk still criticizes himself like that, then how much are the mistakes of ordinary people? Therefore, when writers think that their sins are still full, and they have not yet finished saving themselves, they venture to talk about advising others, sometimes they feel ashamed and hesitant and do not want to write. But thinking back to the word encouragement, I actually don't dare to accept it, but using the personality of a person in a sea of suffering, I try to call on my friends to overcome the sea of suffering, hoping that thanks to that influence, I can reduce some of my sins, so I don't hesitate.



Recalling the Ming Dynasty in China, Mr. La Dien wrote the following test:

Pray hastily and painfully,

Rain, rain, sunshine, spring and autumn.

Every day, early in the morning, I worry about my livelihood,

Forgetting and forgetting to see the white head.

Thirst, philandering and philandering do not end,

Sorrows, afflictions, sorrows and sorrows.

There is a clearly clear path,

Tens of thousands of thousands refuse to practice!

The above text, although rudimentary, does not seem to have any profound principles, but it describes all actions and karma obstacles in human life very clearly. Anyone who can avoid the framework of the above test and try to practice is called a person on the path of liberation.

Mr. La Dien's reason for complaining above is because he sees that the sea of profanity is easy to sink and the path of practice is difficult to follow. In the Forty-Twelve Chapters of the Sutra, the Buddha taught:

There are twenty difficult things in human birth:

- Poverty giving is difficult

- Being rich and studying religion is difficult

- Giving up your life and deciding to die is difficult

- Reading the Buddha's Sutras is difficult

- Abstaining from desire is difficult

- Being born into the Buddha's life is difficult

- It is difficult to see what is good and not seek it

- It's difficult to be humiliated and not angry

- It's difficult not to rely on it

- It is difficult to encounter indifferent things

- Studying widely and researching a lot is difficult

- Getting rid of arrogance is difficult

- Not looking down on those who have not learned is difficult

- Equality of mind is difficult

- Not saying that gossiping is difficult

- Meeting good and knowledgeable people is difficult

- See the nature of learning the Dharma is difficult

- Depending on fate, helping people is difficult

- Seeing a scene without movement is difficult

- Knowing how to use the means is difficult.

Of the twenty things above, I would like to briefly mention a few details here. Like poverty, giving is difficult, because poverty even wants to give, but it is difficult to have the heart but lack the strength. If you try to give, it will affect your life, so it becomes difficult. Or like being rich, it is difficult to learn the Dharma, because although wealth has the power to give, it is attracted by sensual pleasures, making it difficult to let go of body and mind to practice. Being born into the Buddha's life is difficult, as the Treatise on Wisdom says: In the city of Xa Ve, there were nine billion people, but only three billion people had the opportunity to see the Buddha, three billion people, although they heard and believed in it, did not see it, and three billion people were completely neither heard nor seen. The Buddha lived in this land and taught for twenty-five years, but there are still three billion people who have not seen or heard of him. Those who were born in the Buddha's lifetime but lived far away, or were born before or after the Buddha was born, have the opportunity to meet the Buddha or hear the Buddha's teachings. It is not easy. But even though you don't meet the Buddha, but follow the Buddha's method of practice, it is the same as meeting the Buddha. If you do not follow Buddha's teachings, even if you are close to Buddha, you are still far away. As in the past, Devadatta was Buddha's cousin. Bhikkhu Thien Tinh worked as Buddha's attendant for twenty years. Because he did not follow the correct path, he ended up falling into hell. And the old woman in the east of Xa Ve city was born in the same year, month, day and time as the Buddha, but because she was unlucky, she did not want to see the Buddha. Therefore, to see the Buddha listening to the Dharma and following the teachings, must be a person with many good roots, merits and blessings. Now that Tathagata has entered nirvana, good wise men have replaced Buddha to spread the Dharma. If they closely listen to the advice of practice, they will also be liberated. But it is difficult for people with good roots and weak roots to meet good and knowledgeable people. Even if you have the opportunity to see and hear the Dharma, if you do not understand the meaning, or accept the external form and refuse to believe, it is all in vain. According to the Brahma Vong and Hoa Nghiem Sutras, if you want to seek good knowledge, don't be attached to external forms; For example, do not accept that the person is young, poor, low status, or of low birth, ugly appearance, or inadequate faculties, but only pray that the person understands the Buddha's teachings and can benefit you. Also, with a wise person, you should not look for mistakes, because that person sometimes acts like that because of the secret practice, because of the means of salvation, or even though his moral force is high but his habit energy has not yet ended. If you are attached to formality and look for mistakes, you will certainly not benefit on the path. When Buddha was still alive, Ca Luu Da Di had the habit of chewing his mouth back and forth like a buffalo; Bhikkhunī Lotus Flower Nature likes to look in the mirror and apply makeup; A Bhikkhu likes to climb trees and jump; Another Bhikkhu spoke to someone, saying in a loud voice that he was great. But the truth is that these four have all attained Arhat. Because in a previous life, one was a buffalo, one was a courtesan, one was a monkey, one was a Brahman aristocrat, lived in that situation for many lifetimes, and even though he has attained enlightenment now, the redundant habits still remain. Just like the Sixth Patriarch, because he saw that people studying Buddha at that time preferred to speak according to the sutra text and did not immediately recognize Buddha nature, he appeared as an ignorant and illiterate person. Because Ngoc Lam meditation master wanted to avoid predestined conditions to practice, he pretended to be a crazy person, dressed in messy clothes, and spoke impolitely. Venerable Hu Van, because he saw people in the Dharma Ending Age, most of them were leaving the home life, but the mind was not leaving the home life, so even though he had attained enlightenment, he often grew a beard and hair, his secret intention was to show that the Way is not about round heads and square clothes. But at their time, there were also many people who criticized the Sixth Patriarch for being ignorant, Ngoc Lam for being crazy, and the Venerable Hu Van for violating the rules of meditation. That's why it's so difficult to look for a wise man. Those who study Buddhism should also understand these things, to reduce stubbornness and avoid the mistake of scorning monks and nuns. As for the other difficult things, you can deduce them to understand.

However, difficulty and ease are opposites, in difficulty there is ease, in ease there is difficulty. If you understand and are determined, difficult tasks are not impossible. Like in the life of Buddha Bhikkhu Thi, there was a poor couple named Ke La Di and his wife who changed to wear the same loincloth. When the husband went to work, the wife had to stay naked and stay at home. The wife took turns going to work and the husband did the same. But when they heard that the Sangha was promoting and saying that Giving would have blessings to avoid poverty, the couple discussed giving that only loincloth through Giving's window, and had to resign themselves to being naked, closing the door, and lying dead in the house. Because of that determination to do good, the king heard about it and brought his clothes and money to help. From then on, in each life they were born, both husband and wife had their own clothes, and eventually they both attained enlightenment. Therefore, although poverty and giving are difficult, if you understand the cause of poverty due to not giving, and then resolve to endure the lack of hardship and use your own to practice blessings, all giving can be done. Like King Thuan Tri of the Qing Dynasty, he ascended the throne at the age of six, but at the age of twenty-four, he renounced the throne and followed the head monk Buddha, leaving the home life. Being an extremely wealthy emperor, living in the Dragon Palace, guarding the phoenix, eating delicious seafood, having thousands of beautiful concubines, and having the power to hold all the subjects in a country, what could be better than wealth? But if you clearly realize that the blessings of worldly happiness, impermanence, are like an illusory dream, and the scene of true and eternal peace, then it is truly joyous. Then, although it is said that learning the Dharma to be rich and wealthy is difficult, if you are determined, you can definitely practice it. In addition, it is still difficult to practice spiritually because of extreme poverty, but if you have the will, it is not impossible. Like when Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha was still alive, there was an old woman who was very poor. She rented a house for someone from the age of thirteen until she was eighty years old, still working hard. She worked without rest during the day. Every night she had to prepare rice until the second watch. The rooster crowed in the morning and gathered around the flour mill. In such a difficult and free time situation, wanting to practice is a difficult task. But thanks to Venerable Ca Chien Dien's encouragement, every evening after she finished eating rice, she showered, changed her clothes, and meditated until past midnight before going to rest. Thanks to that determination and effort, after death she was reborn as a heavenly son in Da Ma heaven.



Dear ladies and gentlemen! The human body is difficult to obtain, Buddha's teachings are difficult to hear. Now that you have received a human body, and have had the opportunity to read this book, that means you have encountered the mysterious method of becoming Buddha. Even though you encounter difficult circumstances, please clearly recognize the fate of this life of suffering and dreams, and be determined to practice, so that the precious lotus in the western sky can bloom with more virtuous lines.
